sections.name: Standing
rules: Standing is not cultivation Realm, social class, noble rank, or universal reputation. It is local and contextual.
There are five ordinary Standing grades.
No Standing. You are a stranger, guest, prisoner, petitioner, or unknown worker.
Servant Standing. You may perform basic labor, receive food or shelter, and be ordered around.
Outer Standing. You are trusted for ordinary duties, simple missions, shared facilities, and basic records.
Inner Standing. You are trusted with restricted duties, better instruction, inner facilities, low-grade resources, and sensitive errands.
Core Standing. You are trusted with disciples, stores, restricted archives, important missions, hall authority, or a named courtyard.

Some institutions may also recognize Elder Standing, Guest Elder Standing, Lineage Heir Standing, Clan Standing, Official Standing, or other campaign-specific statuses. These are story positions and are not automatically gained from this sphere.

When you learn Sect Stewardship, choose one institution where you have Servant or Outer Standing, subject to GM approval. If the campaign begins before you have joined any group, you instead gain the Petitioner status and can use the sphere to earn your first recognized place.

sections.name: Source Pulse

On a hit against an unattended object, the object takes the damage only.
The damage becomes 2d8 at Foundation Realm, 3d8 at Core Formation Realm, and 4d8 at Nascent Soul Realm.

sections.name: Source Reading
ordered: Source Reading is the basic act of inspecting stone, earth, ore, jade, crystal, a mine face, a source object, a sealed stone, or a mineral surface.

As an Action, you may inspect one unattended mineral object, one visible seal on a mineral object, or one 5-foot section of mineral surface within reach. The GM tells you whether it has obvious active qi, obvious instability, obvious artificial sealing, obvious spiritual contamination, or obvious recent disturbance.

By spending 10 minutes, you may make a Source check against a DC set by the GM to learn one useful fact about one mineral object, chamber, vein, quarry face, ruin wall, mine tunnel, source deposit, sealed stone, or similar feature you can examine. Examples include whether it is natural or worked, whether it contains active source qi, whether it is unstable, whether it has been cut recently, whether a stronger vein lies in a visible direction, whether a seal is present, whether opening it is obviously dangerous, or whether a seal is meant to contain, preserve, warn, lock, hide, or punish.

Source Reading does not reveal exact treasure value, full maps, hidden creatures behind total cover, secret doors automatically, command words, sealed creature identities, or the full rules of another sphere. It gives one grounded fact through stone and source.

You can maintain a number of active Source Seals equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If you create another Source Seal beyond this limit, choose one existing Source Seal you created to end.

sections.name: Breath of No Distance - Breath, Current

You may send a spoken message of up to one hundred words to that creature. If the creature is willing, it may answer with up to one hundred words.

If the path between you is blocked by sealed barriers, underground isolation, planar interference, a stronger Formation, or Void concealment, make an Air Check against the obstacle’s DC. On a failure, the message scatters and both creatures hear only wind.
sections.summary: You can carry breath through the world’s air.

Clear does not neutralize poison already inhaled or remove conditions already suffered.
sections.summary: When you use Gather Current, you may choose Clear as its Vector.

sections.name: Court of the Four Winds - Domain
rules: Once on each of your turns, you may use Gather Current without an action.
When a creature starts its turn inside the court, you may move one active Current up to 20 feet.
Your Wind Lash may originate from any active Current inside the court.
Allied creatures inside one of your Currents gain +10 feet to Speed while moving in the direction you choose.
Hostile creatures moving against one of your Currents treat the space as Difficult Terrain.
Once per round when an ordinary ranged weapon attack passes through one of your Currents, you may impose Disadvantage on that attack without using your Reaction.
The court ends early if you are Incapacitated or if you enter an airless sealed region that prevents currents from existing.
sections.summary: You establish a court of moving air around yourself. Choose four winds when the court appears: North, South, East, and West. Each wind is assigned one Vector: Lift, Press, Cut, Carry, Turn, or Scatter. You cannot assign the same Vector to more than two winds.

sections.name: When Heaven Exhales
rules: You make the sky exhale once.
Choose up to three of the following decrees. Each hostile creature, projectile, flying object, or active windlike technique in the area is affected as appropriate.

The Breath Returns: Breath-dependent hostile creatures make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they cannot speak, shout, chant, command, or use breath-required techniques until the end of your next turn. On a success, they cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn.

The Arrows Lose Their Road: Ordinary ranged weapon attacks, thrown weapons, volleys, and non-Secret physical projectile techniques in the area fail against targets you choose until the start of your next turn.
The Sky Rejects Weight: Allied creatures you choose gain a Fly Speed of 60 feet and Hover until the end of your next turn.

The Ground Receives the Proud: Hostile flying creatures make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, they descend up to 300 feet, land if possible, and fall Prone. On a success, their Fly Speed is halved until the end of their next turn.

The World Turns Sideways: Choose a direction. Hostile creatures and unattended objects not anchored to the ground are pushed 60 feet in that direction. A creature may make a Strength saving throw to halve the distance.
The Gate Opens: Create a Sky Road up to 1 mile long that lasts until the end of your next turn without Concentration.
After resolving the decrees, you may immediately move up to your Speed or Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Limits: When Heaven Exhales does not create regional weather permanently, erase mountains, move sealed buildings, kill breathless creatures automatically, or bypass stronger domain-scale authority without an opposed Cultivation Check. Creatures inside airtight sealed structures are affected only if the chosen decree can reach them through an air path or through a superior inheritance-level contest.

rules: You raise the axe and demand that Heaven show the root of what stands before you.

sections.name: First Circuit Method
rules: When you first gain the Lightning sphere, your meridians learn to hold a brief seed of unstable potential. This is called a First Circuit.

A First Circuit is not a full Charge and does not make you vulnerable to hostile Lightning talents unless a feature specifically says so. It is the internal spark that lets Lightning cultivation move through the body before it escapes into the world.

Once on each of your turns, when you use Gather Charge on yourself, a held weapon, a worn item, or a Lightning focus you are touching, choose one Circuit expression. The chosen expression lasts until the Charge ends.

Body Circuit. Before the Charge ends, when you deal lightning damage or consume a Charge, you may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from one creature damaged by your Lightning sphere this turn.

Edge Circuit. Before the Charge ends, the next time you hit with an unarmed strike, weapon attack, Lightning Lash, or Lightning talent delivered through a held implement, you deal additional lightning damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

Nerve Circuit. Before the Charge ends, when you would have your Speed reduced, be knocked Prone, or be denied Reactions by a non-Secret effect, you may discharge the Circuit to gain Advantage on the saving throw against that effect. If no saving throw is allowed, reduce the penalty by one step: ignore a Speed reduction of 10 feet or less, stand from Prone by spending 5 fewer feet of movement, or regain your Reaction at the start of your next turn.

Conduction Circuit. Before the Charge ends, when you apply Charge to a creature, object, formation node, talisman, weapon, armor, or 5-foot space, you may make yourself Conductive until the start of your next turn. While Conductive this way, your next Lightning talent that requires a Conductive Path may treat yourself, your held weapon, or your worn armor as the starting point of that path.
You may discharge only one First Circuit per round.

allies of your choice ignore Difficult Terrain from your Water effects;
when a hostile creature fails a saving throw against one of your Water effects, you may move it 10 feet into a legal space;
when you create a Basin, you may choose two forms from Shape Current instead of one, such as Mist plus Pressure or Cleansing plus Flow.

sections.name: Court of the Endless Tide - Domain
rules: The Domain does not fill the entire area with physical water unless you use talents that create floodwater.
sections.summary: You establish a tide court. The battlefield gains a spiritual slope toward your chosen sea.

items: the target cannot speak clearly;
the target cannot take Reactions;
the target has Disadvantage on Constitution saving throws to maintain Concentration;
the target cannot regain Hit Points until the start of your next turn.

sections.name: Crushing Current - Pressure
rules: If the target was already Soaked, you may choose two effects.
sections.summary: When a creature fails its saving throw against your Pressure Basin, you may apply Drowning Pressure until the start of your next turn.

sections.name: Cutting Current - Pressure
rules: If the target is Soaked, add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage. Against unattended mundane ropes, cloth, paper, ash, salt, mud, clay, or soft stone, this damage counts as Scouring Erosion.
sections.summary: Your Water Lash may deal slashing damage instead of bludgeoning damage.

sections.name: Drinking the Rain - Cleansing
rules: Each chosen creature may remove one level of Exhaustion caused by heat, dehydration, thirst, smoke, forced march, or similar environmental strain. A creature can benefit from this talent once per long rest.
sections.summary: When you finish a short rest while you have access to rain, mist, clean water, or one of your Cleansing Basins, choose up to six creatures who rested with you.

sections.name: Drown the Flame - Cleansing / Pressure
rules: Ordinary flames are extinguished. Magical flames and Fire sphere effects require a Water check against the creator’s Cultivation Save DC or an opposed Cultivation Check if the effect is especially strong.
If you succeed against a Fire effect, you may make one creature in the area Soaked or end one Burning-like ongoing fire effect on a creature.
sections.summary: When you create or move a Basin or Current, you may attempt to quench fire in the area.

sections.name: Erode the Mountain’s Name - Pressure / Spring
rules: Make a Water check against a DC set by the GM or against the creator’s Cultivation Save DC. On a success, the target gains an Erosion Mark for 24 hours.

While marked, Water damage against the target ignores ordinary Resistance and deals double damage if the target is mundane and erodible. If the target is a magical Barrier or formation anchor, the next successful Water check made to disrupt it before the mark ends has Advantage.
A single target can bear only one Erosion Mark from you at a time.
sections.summary: Choose one object, wall, Barrier, formation anchor, or terrain feature you can affect with Water damage. Spend 10 minutes and 5 CP directing a continuous current against it.

sections.name: Flood the Battlefield - Tide / Domain
rules: Until the start of your next turn, the Domain becomes waist-deep spiritual floodwater for creatures of your choice. Hostile creatures without Swim Speed treat the area as Difficult Terrain and have Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks made to resist your Water effects.

When you activate the flood, choose up to a number of hostile creatures equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Each makes a Strength saving throw. On a failure, a creature is knocked Prone, moved 30 feet into a legal space, and suffers Drowning Pressure until the end of its next turn. On a success, it is moved 10 feet and becomes Soaked.
sections.summary: While your Court of the Endless Tide is active, you may spend 3 CP as an action to flood it.

sections.name: Flowing Step - Current
rules: If you start your turn in rain, mist, wet ground, or a Basin you created, you may stand from Prone without spending movement once per turn.
sections.summary: When you use Return the Flow, you may target yourself instead of an ally even if you are not adjacent to the Water effect. Move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from creatures that are Soaked or standing in one of your Currents or Basins.

facts: 5 CP Uses: Once per long rest
sections.name: Heaven-Falling Tsunami - Tide
ordered: A vertical sea descends or a horizontal tide breaks across the field.
Each creature of your choice in the area makes a Strength saving throw.

a creature takes 8d8 bludgeoning damage, is pushed up to 60 feet, falls Prone, becomes Soaked, and suffers Drowning Pressure until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, it takes half damage, is pushed 15 feet, and becomes Soaked.
Objects and unattended structures in the area take the damage and may suffer Scouring Erosion.

Your Water Control Limit increases by one Created Water Basin.

sections.summary: At Foundation, your created water develops spiritual continuity.

make the attacker Soaked and give the next attack roll against it Advantage before the start of your next turn.

sections.summary: When a creature misses you or an ally inside your Mist Basin or while Soaked, you may use your Reaction and spend 1 CP.

sections.name: Mist Veil - Mist
rules: The area is Lightly Obscured. By spending 1 additional CP when you create it, you may make the area Heavily Obscured until the start of your next turn; after that, it becomes Lightly Obscured for the remaining duration.
A creature does not become Hidden automatically. It must still use Hide or another feature.
sections.summary: When you create a Mist Basin, you may make the area a 15-foot-radius sphere instead of a 10-foot square.

facts: 5 CP Uses: Once per long rest unless a feature says otherwise

items: you gain Swim Speed equal to twice your Speed and can breathe underwater;
Water Lash range becomes 300 feet;
Water Lash may originate from any Water Source, Basin, or Current you control within range;
once on each of your turns, you may use Return the Flow without an action;
your Water Control Limit increases by two Basins or Currents;
you may maintain Court of the Endless Tide without Concentration while this incarnation lasts;
when a creature fails a save against your Water effect, you may apply Soaked, move it 10 feet, or impose one Drowning Pressure option;
when you reduce damage with Water Shield, you may move the protected creature up to 30 feet.

sections.name: Ocean-Sovereign Incarnation - Realm Evolution
sections.summary: You become a sovereign current. Your body, breath, defense, and water effects move as one sea.

sections.name: Pressure Lance - Pressure
rules: Make one attack roll and compare it to the AC of each creature in the line. On a hit, a target takes Water Lash damage and becomes Soaked. If a target was already Soaked, add one Water Lash die to the damage.
Objects in the line take damage normally. Against unattended barriers, this can count as Scouring Erosion.
sections.summary: When you use Water Lash, you may spend 1 CP to make it a line 60 feet long and 5 feet wide.

sections.name: Pull of the River - Current
sections.summary: When your Water Lash hits a Soaked target, you may pull the target 10 feet instead of moving it 5 feet. If the target is Large or smaller and ends this movement adjacent to a Basin or Current you created, it must succeed on a Strength saving throw or fall Prone.

sections.name: Restorative Waters - Cleansing / Return
rules: At CL 11, the healing becomes 2d8 + your modifier. At CL 17, it becomes 3d8 + your modifier.
A creature can benefit from Restorative Waters once per short rest unless you spend 2 CP instead of 1 CP.
This is supportive restoration, not full Life-sphere regeneration.
sections.summary: When you use Return the Flow, you may spend 1 CP to restore Hit Points equal to 1d8 + your Water key ability modifier to one ally in or adjacent to the Water effect.

sections.name: River Cuts the Gate - Pressure / Erosion
rules: For 1 minute, repeated Water damage against that target ignores ordinary Resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical sources and deals double damage to mundane objects if the GM agrees the material can be eroded.

Against magical Barriers, use a Water check against the Barrier’s DC or the creator’s Cultivation Save DC. On a success, the next Water damage against the Barrier before the end of your next turn gains the same benefit.
sections.summary: When your Water Lash, Pressure Lance, Tidal Wave, or Whirlpool Prison damages an object, Barrier, gate, wall, formation anchor, or unattended structure, you may spend 1 CP to apply Scouring Erosion.

sections.name: River Passage - Tide
rules: If you begin adjacent to a Water Source, Basin, Current, river, canal, pond, cistern, rain curtain, or similar water path, you may teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space adjacent to the same connected water system or one of your Basins.
At CL 11, the range becomes 300 feet. At CL 15, it becomes 1 mile if both ends are connected to a significant Water Source.
sections.summary: You can use Return the Flow to carry yourself or a willing creature through connected water.

sections.name: River Path to the Sea - Tide / Travel
ordered: You can expand River Passage into a travel rite.

By spending 10 minutes and 5 CP at a significant Water Source, you may transport yourself and up to eight willing creatures to another significant Water Source you have personally visited or marked with a Water project. The destination must be within 10 miles per CL unless the journey follows a major river, coastline, sacred canal, or sea route approved by the GM.
This is a travel technique, not a combat teleport. Hostile wards, sealed Barriers, drought curses, or contested water deities may block or complicate the passage.

gain Advantage on the next saving throw against Poisoned or disease before the next long rest;
recover additional Hit Points equal to your CL during a short rest;
cleanse mundane filth, ash, smoke residue, or spiritual grime visible to ordinary senses.
groups.lead: For 24 hours, the site becomes a Sacred Spring. A creature that spends 10 minutes washing, drinking, or meditating there gains one benefit:

sections.name: Sacred Spring - Spring / Project
rules: A Sacred Spring cannot remove curses, resurrect the dead, replace Life, or produce infinite economic water. Long-term springs require project rules, maintenance, and local spiritual geography.
sections.summary: You may perform a 10-minute rite at a clean Water Source or Cleansing Basin, spending 3 CP.

sections.name: Still Surface Method - Mist
rules: The attacker has Disadvantage on the triggering attack roll unless it can see through obscurement or the attack does not rely on sight.
You may use this Reaction a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus per long rest, or by spending 1 CP.
sections.summary: When a creature inside your Mist Basin is targeted by an attack from outside the Basin, you may use your Reaction to ripple the mist.

sections.name: Ten Thousand Returning Streams - Return / Tide
rules: For each chosen effect, move it up to 20 feet, end it, or apply one minor Return effect. A creature can be moved by this talent only once per turn.
If at least two chosen effects end, you may restore Hit Points equal to your Water key ability modifier + your Proficiency Bonus to one ally inside the Domain.
sections.summary: When you use Return the Flow inside your Court of the Endless Tide, you may choose up to three Water effects you created instead of one.

sections.name: Tidal Wave - Tide / Current
outcomes: A creature takes 4d8 bludgeoning damage, is pushed 20 feet, falls Prone, and becomes Soaked. On a successful save, it takes half damage and becomes Soaked.
rules: Choose a line up to 90 feet long and 15 feet wide, or a 30-foot cone. Each creature of your choice in the area makes a Strength saving throw.
If used inside your Court of the Endless Tide, you may curve the wave once around a corner or obstacle you can perceive.
sections.summary: When you use Shape Current, you may spend 2 additional CP to create a wave.

sections.name: Water Breathing - Cleansing / Tide
ordered: You can use Shape Current to create a Breath Basin instead of one of its normal forms.

The Basin occupies a 10-foot-radius area and lasts for 1 hour without Concentration. Creatures of your choice in the Basin can breathe underwater, speak normally through water, and ignore the ordinary penalties of wet lungs, smoke inhalation, or choking dust while they remain in the area.

At CL 5, you may instead target up to a number of willing creatures equal to your Proficiency Bonus. They gain this benefit for 1 hour while within 1 mile of a Water Source you have touched during the last minute.

sections.summary: You can use Shape Current to create a Breath Basin instead of one of its normal forms.

sections.name: Water Clone - Basin / Mist
rules: The clone occupies one space inside the Basin and lasts for the Basin’s duration. It cannot attack independently. When a creature you can perceive attacks you or an ally within 30 feet of the clone, you may use your Reaction to have the clone interpose.

Roll a d20. On an 11 or higher, the attack targets the clone instead. The clone has AC equal to your Cultivation Save DC and Hit Points equal to twice your CL. If reduced to 0 Hit Points, it bursts and makes each hostile creature within 5 feet Soaked.
sections.summary: When you create a Mist Basin or Cleansing Basin, you may spend 2 CP to form a Water Clone in it.

facts: You or a creature within 30 feet that you can perceive takes damage from an attack or area effect.
sections.name: Water Shield - Current / Cleansing
rules: If the protected creature is Soaked or inside one of your Basins or Currents, also move it 10 feet into a legal space without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
At CL 11, reduce the damage by 2d10 + your modifier. At CL 17, reduce it by 3d10 + your modifier.
sections.summary: A current rises to absorb and redirect harm. Reduce the triggering damage by 1d10 + your Water key ability modifier.

sections.name: Water Whip - Current / Pressure
rules: The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or become Grappled by the water until the end of your next turn. While Grappled this way, it is also Soaked.
A target can escape early by using an action to make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against your Cultivation Save DC.
sections.summary: When Water Lash hits, you may spend 1 CP to wrap the target in a whip-current.

sections.name: Wave Burst - Current
rules: The area becomes a 10-foot-radius burst. Each creature of your choice in the area must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 feet away from the center and become Soaked.
sections.summary: When you create a Flowing Current with Shape Current, you may make it burst outward from a point instead of flowing in a line or square.

groups.lead: Choose three laws when the inheritance manifests:

items: all allies of your choice in the area move up to 60 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks;
one hostile creature that failed a saving throw against your Water effect during the inheritance is Restrained until the end of your next turn;
one Barrier, gate, or terrain feature damaged by the inheritance gains an Erosion Mark for 24 hours;

sections.name: When the Sea Forgets the Shore
rules: You declare that the battlefield was only temporarily dry.

For the duration, the area becomes a sovereign tide region. It may manifest as floodwater, descending rain-sea, rivers rising from stone, a phantom ocean overlapping reality, or every drop in the area remembering its original sea.

Every Path Returns. Once per round, when a hostile creature moves, teleports, flies, or is forced to move inside the area, you may move it up to 30 feet into a legal space after that movement resolves.

All Fire Drowns. Ordinary flames are extinguished. Fire effects that begin in the area or enter it must succeed on an opposed Cultivation Check or be suppressed until the start of the creator’s next turn.
Pressure Has No Surface. Up to three hostile creatures of your choice each round suffer Drowning Pressure until the start of your next turn.
The River Takes the Weapon. Once per round, when a hostile creature hits with a weapon attack inside the area, reduce the damage by 4d10 and move the attacker or target 30 feet into a legal space.
The Sea Gives Back. Once per round, an ally of your choice inside the area regains Hit Points equal to 4d8 + your Water key ability modifier when it starts its turn Soaked or inside a Water effect.
Mountains Become Silt. Objects, walls, gates, and unattended structures in the area suffer Scouring Erosion. Water damage against them is doubled if mundane and erodible.

This inheritance cannot permanently flood a nation, create an endless sea, override a superior divine or sect formation without contest, or solve regional drought by itself. Those outcomes require campaign-scale projects.
sections.summary: Secret Water Inheritance

sections.name: Whirlpool Prison - Pressure / Basin
outcomes: It is Restrained until the start of its next turn and suffers Drowning Pressure. On a success, its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn.
rules: The area becomes a 20-foot-radius Basin. A hostile creature that enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there makes a Strength saving throw.
A creature Restrained this way can use its action to repeat the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.
sections.summary: When you create a Pressure Basin, you may spend 2 additional CP to make it a whirlpool.

sections.name: Adhesive Pool
rules: A creature affected by Adhesive Pool is impressed by the wax.
sections.summary: When you create Soft Spread, you may make it adhesive. The first hostile creature each round that enters the area, starts its turn there, or is knocked Prone there must succeed on a Strength saving throw or have its Speed reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn.

sections.name: Base Sphere Abilities
rules: You also learn one Wax talent of your choice.
sections.summary: When you first gain the Sphere of Wax, you gain Mold Wax, Press Seal, and Kindle Wax.

sections.name: Mold Wax
ordered: Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute.
You create or awaken cultivated wax in an unoccupied space, on a surface, or over an unattended object within range. Choose one form.

Soft Spread. You create a 10-foot square of Soft Wax on a surface. The area is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures. The first hostile creature each round that enters the area or starts its turn there must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become impressed by the wax until the end of your next turn.

Set Shape. You create a Set Wax panel, ramp, handhold, brace, small bridge, shield plate, low wall, or similar structure that fits within two contiguous 5-foot cubes. It must be supported by a surface unless a talent says otherwise. It can provide cover, block a narrow passage, support weight, or create a short ramp or platform.

Fine Work. Outside initiative, you can shape wax into seals, molds, masks, tablets, candle forms, practice tools, ritual counters, labels, evidence casts, and small sculptures. Fine Work cannot create valuable trade goods, magical items, living organs, or permanent infrastructure unless the GM says otherwise.
At CL 5, your Soft Spread can cover a 15-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within four contiguous 5-foot cubes.
At CL 10, your Soft Spread can cover a 20-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within six contiguous 5-foot cubes.
At CL 15, your Soft Spread can cover a 25-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within eight contiguous 5-foot cubes.

sections.name: Press Seal
rules: You press or throw a cultivated Wax Seal onto one creature, object, surface, or 5-foot space within range. A willing creature, unattended object, or surface is sealed automatically. An unwilling creature or attended object makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the seal attaches. On a success, the seal fails.
When you place the seal, choose one base seal.

Clinging Seal. The sealed creature’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet while the seal remains. If placed on an object, the object adheres to the surface it touches and requires an Action and a successful Strength check against your Cultivation Save DC to remove.

Witness Seal. The seal records the next creature other than you that touches, opens, damages, moves, or passes through the sealed target. You know that the seal was triggered if you are within 1 mile, and you can later inspect the seal to see the outline, handprint, footprint, tool mark, weapon shape, or other physical Impression left behind.

Closing Seal. The seal holds a door, lid, drawer, container, wound wrapping, sheath, scroll case, coffin, or similar closure shut. Opening it requires an Action and a successful Strength check or Dexterity check with appropriate tools against your Cultivation Save DC. A creature can also destroy the seal normally.

Preserving Seal. The sealed object, corpse, medicine, food, blood sample, written page, track, footprint, wound dressing, or physical clue resists decay, contamination, smearing, and ordinary weather while the seal remains.
sections.summary: Action. Range 30 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration 1 minute.

sections.name: Kindle Wax
ordered: Bonus Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 0 CP.
You burn one Wax form, Wax Seal, candle, or wax object you created within range. The chosen wax is consumed. Choose one base release.

Candleflare. One creature within 5 feet of the kindled wax makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes fire damage equal to 1d6 + your Proficiency Bonus. On a success, it takes half damage.

Smoke Puff. The wax releases thick smoke in a 5-foot radius until the start of your next turn. The area is Lightly Obscured. This smoke is ordinary smoke once released and can be dispersed by strong wind.

Release Seal. If the kindled wax was a Wax Seal on an ally, the ally gains temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If it was a Wax Seal on an enemy, that enemy takes fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

Mark the Wick. You learn whether the wax had been touched, moved, damaged, or disturbed since you created it. If it held an Impression, you preserve a brief sensory image of the Impression before the wax burns.

sections.name: Borrowed Countenance
rules: The mask still does not alter voice, aura, cultivation pressure, memories, scent, or actual identity. Magical scrutiny, close social interaction, or careful inspection can expose the deception.
Using this talent for impersonation may be illegal, dishonorable, or forbidden in many sects.
sections.summary: When you create a Wax Mask from a true Impression of a creature’s face, hand, or identifying mark, the wearer may also imitate one physical sign of that creature: a handprint, a facial profile, a scar pattern, a lip shape, a bite pattern, or similar visible evidence.

sections.name: Candle Procession
ordered: Action. Cost 1 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 10 minutes.

You create up to six small cultivated candles in spaces you can see within 60 feet. The candles may float inches above the ground, cling to walls, or rest on surfaces. They shed dim light in a 10-foot radius.
As a Bonus Action, you may move each candle up to 20 feet. A candle cannot attack, carry objects, provide flanking, or occupy a creature’s space.
Allies who begin their turn within 5 feet of one of your procession candles may ignore the first 5 feet of Difficult Terrain they enter that turn.

sections.name: Candle Procession Across the Night - Wick Evolution
ordered: Your Candle Procession can carry allies along prepared candle routes.
Rite. 10 minutes. Cost 4 CP. Duration 1 hour.

You arrange a line of candles between two points you have physically visited within the last 24 hours, no farther apart than 1 mile per Proficiency Bonus. During the duration, you and up to six willing creatures may travel between those points as part of a quiet procession. The journey takes 10 minutes regardless of normal travel difficulty, provided the route is physically passable by some path.

This is not teleportation. It is a supernatural procession that finds the safe candle-lit way through streets, halls, forests, ruins, grave roads, or sect grounds. Barriers, sealed gates, warded borders, hostile patrols, or impossible terrain can still interrupt it.

sections.name: Candle That Remembers Every Footstep
ordered: Rite. 10 minutes. Cost 4 CP. Duration 24 hours.
You prepare a sovereign tracking candle from an Impression. While the candle burns, it remembers the path of the creature or object that left the Impression.
You can ask the candle one of the following questions each hour.
Did the subject pass within 1 mile of this location in the last 24 hours?
Which direction did the subject most recently travel from here?
Did the subject cross a threshold, gate, river, road, wall, or formation nearby?
Is the subject currently protected by a strong anti-divination, anti-tracking, or identity-concealing effect?

The candle answers by flame direction, scent, smoke pattern, wax flow, or script emerging in melted wax. It does not reveal exact location unless the GM decides the Impression is unusually strong and the subject is nearby.

sections.name: Clinging Seal
sections.summary: When a creature fails its saving throw against Press Seal, you may spend 1 additional CP to strengthen the seal. Until the seal ends, the target cannot benefit from the Dash action unless it first uses its Action to attempt to remove the seal.

sections.name: Court of Ten Thousand Candles - Wax Domain
rules: You establish a candle court in a 30-foot radius centered on a point you can see within 60 feet. The court fills with wax seals, thin candlelight, slow-falling droplets, and soft places waiting to harden.
Allies in the court gain the following benefits.
They ignore Difficult Terrain created by your Wax talents.
The first time each round an ally would be moved against their will, they may reduce that movement by 10 feet.
An ally who starts their turn adjacent to one of your Wax forms or candles gains temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Enemies in the court suffer the following effects.
The area is Difficult Terrain for them.
The first time each round an enemy fails a saving throw against one of your Wax talents, you may place a Wax Seal on that enemy without spending additional CP.
An enemy that damages one of your Wax forms is impressed by the court until the end of its next turn.

The court is visible and material. Fire, wind, dispelling, and object destruction can weaken parts of it, but do not end the entire Domain unless the central candle seal is destroyed or your concentration ends.
sections.summary: Action. Cost 4 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute.

sections.name: Effigy of the Absent - Effigy Rite
ordered: Rite. 1 hour. Cost 4 CP. Duration 7 days.
You create an advanced effigy of a missing creature, forgotten oath, lost object, dead witness, or sealed event.

Message Vessel. If the subject willingly gave you an Impression, name-seal, or token, the effigy can carry a message that reaches them in a dream, candle reflection, or moment of stillness if they are on the same plane and not protected against such contact.

Recognition Vessel. You may compare a creature, corpse, object, handwriting sample, wound, footprint, key, or aura trace against the effigy. The GM may grant advantage on checks to determine whether it matches the subject.
Funeral Vessel. If used in a respectful funeral rite, the effigy helps preserve a departing trace, name, or final memory long enough for Spirit, Fate, Dream, or ancestral rites to interact with it.
Effigy of the Absent cannot compel the subject to answer, appear, suffer harm, or reveal secrets by itself.

sections.summary: Rite. 1 hour. Cost 4 CP. Duration 7 days.

sections.name: Flowing Wax Step
ordered: You soften wax under your own feet and ride its yielding surface. Until the end of your turn, you ignore Difficult Terrain created by wax, mud, snow, shallow water, slick stone, or similar yielding surfaces. If you move through your own Soft Wax this turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from creatures standing in that wax.
rules: You soften wax under your own feet and ride its yielding surface. If you move through your own Soft Wax this turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from creatures standing in that wax.
sections.summary: Bonus Action. Cost 1 CP.

facts: A creature you can see within 60 feet would die, have its corpse destroyed, or have its departing trace scattered. Cost 5 CP.
sections.name: Funeral Candle Shelter - Wick Rite
ordered: You ignite a funeral candle and wrap the target in white wax light. Choose one effect.
Shelter the Dying. If the creature would die from damage, it instead falls to 0 hit points and becomes stable, provided the damage did not destroy the body outright. The candle ends.

Shelter the Departing Trace. If the creature dies, you preserve a respectful departing trace, final breath, name, or memory for 1 hour. This does not trap the soul or prevent resurrection. It gives allies time to perform Spirit, Fate, Dream, Medicine, funeral, or ancestral rites.
A creature can benefit from Funeral Candle Shelter only once per long rest.

A creature can benefit from Funeral Candle Shelter only once per long rest.
sections.summary: You ignite a funeral candle and wrap the target in white wax light. Choose one effect.

sections.name: Greater Mold - Mold Evolution
rules: When you create Soft Spread, increase one side of the area by 10 feet.
When you create Set Shape, you may create two separate Set Wax structures within range, each no larger than half your normal Set Shape limit.
You may also create stairs, handrails, short bridges, wax curtains, false walls, ramps, seals across multiple panels, or simple furniture appropriate to the available volume.
sections.summary: Your Mold Wax improves.

sections.name: Guiding Candle
ordered: You can create a small cultivated candle as part of Mold Wax or Press Seal. The candle burns for 1 hour, sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for another 10 feet, and is visible only as ordinary candlelight unless examined with supernatural senses.

As a Bonus Action, you may cause one Guiding Candle within 60 feet to flare. Until the start of your next turn, allies who can see the candle ignore nonmagical Difficult Terrain in a 10-foot radius around it.
rules: As a Bonus Action, you may cause one Guiding Candle within 60 feet to flare. Until the start of your next turn, allies who can see the candle ignore nonmagical Difficult Terrain in a 10-foot radius around it.
sections.summary: You can create a small cultivated candle as part of Mold Wax or Press Seal. The candle burns for 1 hour, sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for another 10 feet, and is visible only as ordinary candlelight unless examined with supernatural senses.

sections.name: Hundred
ordered: You ignite any number of your Wax Seals within range. Choose up to three creatures bearing those seals or adjacent to those seals. Each target makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes 4d8 fire damage and is pushed 10 feet away from the nearest ignited seal. On a success, it takes half damage and is not pushed.
rules: You ignite any number of your Wax Seals within range. Choose up to three creatures bearing those seals or adjacent to those seals. Each target makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes 4d8 fire damage and is pushed 10 feet away from the nearest ignited seal. On a success, it takes half damage and is not pushed.
All ignited seals are consumed.
sections.summary: Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 3 CP.

sections.name: Lingering Seal
sections.summary: When a Wax Seal would end because its duration expires, you may spend 1 CP to extend it for 10 minutes if it is on a surface, object, willing creature, corpse, or unattended item. This cannot extend a hostile creature’s combat seal unless a higher-Realm talent says otherwise.

sections.name: Living Wax Form
rules: You cultivate your own body as wax without losing your living nature. Choose one form when you activate this talent.

Soft Body. You can move through spaces as narrow as 1 inch wide if you are not carrying rigid equipment that cannot pass. You have advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to escape Grappled or Restrained. You have disadvantage on saving throws against effects that would push, pull, or knock you Prone.

Set Body. You gain temporary hit points equal to twice your Cultivation Level. While these temporary hit points remain, you reduce forced movement by 10 feet and have advantage on saving throws against being knocked Prone.

Wick Body. The first time each round a creature hits you with a melee attack, you may use your Reaction to deal fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus and shed bright candlelight in a 10-foot radius until the start of your next turn.
You may change forms as a Bonus Action by spending 1 CP.
sections.summary: Bonus Action. Cost 2 CP. Duration 1 minute.

sections.name: Medicinal Wax
rules: Cooling Wax. The target has advantage on the next saving throw it makes before the end of your next turn against fire, poison, or disease.
Stimulating Wax. The target’s Speed increases by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.
Numbing Wax. The first time before the end of your next turn that the target takes damage, reduce that damage by your Proficiency Bonus.
sections.summary: When you use Seal Wound or Waxen Shell, choose one of the following medicinal preparations.

facts: A creature within 5 feet of one of your Wax forms damages it with a melee attack or starts to tear away one of your Wax Seals.
sections.name: Melting Rebuke
ordered: You kindle that wax. The triggering creature makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes fire damage equal to 1d8 + your Proficiency Bonus and is impressed by the wax until the end of its next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and is not impressed.
sections.summary: You kindle that wax. The triggering creature makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes fire damage equal to 1d8 + your Proficiency Bonus and is impressed by the wax until the end of its next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and is not impressed.

sections.name: Mold Wax
ordered: Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute.
You create or awaken cultivated wax in an unoccupied space, on a surface, or over an unattended object within range. Choose one form.

Soft Spread. You create a 10-foot square of Soft Wax on a surface. The area is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures. The first hostile creature each round that enters the area or starts its turn there must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become impressed by the wax until the end of your next turn.

Set Shape. You create a Set Wax panel, ramp, handhold, brace, small bridge, shield plate, low wall, or similar structure that fits within two contiguous 5-foot cubes. It must be supported by a surface unless a talent says otherwise. It can provide cover, block a narrow passage, support weight, or create a short ramp or platform.

Fine Work. Outside initiative, you can shape wax into seals, molds, masks, tablets, candle forms, practice tools, ritual counters, labels, evidence casts, and small sculptures. Fine Work cannot create valuable trade goods, magical items, living organs, or permanent infrastructure unless the GM says otherwise.
At CL 5, your Soft Spread can cover a 15-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within four contiguous 5-foot cubes.
At CL 10, your Soft Spread can cover a 20-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within six contiguous 5-foot cubes.
At CL 15, your Soft Spread can cover a 25-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within eight contiguous 5-foot cubes.

sections.summary: Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute.

sections.name: Molten Snare
rules: This is heated wax, not broad fire control.
sections.summary: When a creature fails a saving throw against Adhesive Pool or Wax Cage, you may spend 1 CP to make the wax molten and dragging. Until the start of your next turn, the creature takes fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus whenever it moves willingly or is moved through the wax.

sections.name: Palace Raised From One Drip - Mold Evolution
rules: The total volume cannot exceed your Mold Wax limits, but you may divide the wax into any number of connected sections. The structure must remain physically plausible: it needs support, cannot hover freely, and cannot create machinery with complex moving parts unless another talent permits it.
sections.summary: When you use Mold Wax, you may create more elaborate connected structures: multiple walls, a low maze, a stairwell, a short bridge, a sealed booth, a temporary clinic bay, a wax gatehouse, or a layered rampart.

sections.name: Preserving Shroud - Seal Rite
rules: You wrap a willing creature, corpse, medicine, rare specimen, document, spiritual trace, or physical clue in preserving wax and cloth. For the duration, the target resists ordinary decay, contamination, rot, weathering, insects, drying, smearing, and casual handling.
If used on a living creature, the target gains advantage on saving throws against disease and poison for the duration, but its Speed is reduced by 10 feet while fully shrouded.
If used on a corpse or trace, the shroud preserves evidence. It does not prevent resurrection limits, command souls, or halt supernatural decay unless the GM allows it.
sections.summary: Rite. 10 minutes. Range Touch. Cost 2 CP. Duration 24 hours.

sections.name: Press Seal
rules: You press or throw a cultivated Wax Seal onto one creature, object, surface, or 5-foot space within range. A willing creature, unattended object, or surface is sealed automatically. An unwilling creature or attended object makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the seal attaches. On a success, the seal fails.
When you place the seal, choose one base seal.

Clinging Seal. The sealed creature’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet while the seal remains. If placed on an object, the object adheres to the surface it touches and requires an Action and a successful Strength check against your Cultivation Save DC to remove.

Witness Seal. The seal records the next creature other than you that touches, opens, damages, moves, or passes through the sealed target. You know that the seal was triggered if you are within 1 mile, and you can later inspect the seal to see the outline, handprint, footprint, tool mark, weapon shape, or other physical Impression left behind.

Closing Seal. The seal holds a door, lid, drawer, container, wound wrapping, sheath, scroll case, coffin, or similar closure shut. Opening it requires an Action and a successful Strength check or Dexterity check with appropriate tools against your Cultivation Save DC. A creature can also destroy the seal normally.

Preserving Seal. The sealed object, corpse, medicine, food, blood sample, written page, track, footprint, wound dressing, or physical clue resists decay, contamination, smearing, and ordinary weather while the seal remains.
sections.summary: Action. Range 30 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration 1 minute.

sections.name: Procession of Wax Attendants
ordered: You shape up to three Small wax attendants. They are fragile ritual helpers, not combat summons. Each attendant has AC 10, 1 hit point, Speed 20 feet, and can carry a light object, hold a candle, bear a seal, deliver a message to a visible creature within 300 feet, open an unlocked door, pour medicine, hold a bandage, or perform another simple task.
In combat, an attendant acts on your turn and can take only the Dash, Disengage, Help, Hide, Search, or Use an Object action. It cannot attack. If it takes damage, it is destroyed.

sections.summary: Action. Cost 3 CP. Duration 1 hour.

sections.name: Quiet Seal
ordered: You can place a Wax Seal without obvious light, heat, scent, or sound. A creature observing the target can still notice the seal with a Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check against your Cultivation Save DC.
You have advantage on checks made to hide Wax Seals among legal seals, candle drippings, wax repairs, cosmetics, medicine, funeral wrappings, or household objects.
rules: You have advantage on checks made to hide Wax Seals among legal seals, candle drippings, wax repairs, cosmetics, medicine, funeral wrappings, or household objects.
sections.summary: You can place a Wax Seal without obvious light, heat, scent, or sound. A creature observing the target can still notice the seal with a Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check against your Cultivation Save DC.

sections.name: Returning Wax
sections.summary: When one of your Wax forms is destroyed by damage, you may use your Reaction and spend 1 CP to have part of it flow back to you. You regain temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus, or you may immediately create a 5-foot square of Soft Wax in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of the destroyed form.

sections.name: Sculpted Implements
ordered: You may use Fine Work to create temporary wax tools, keys, wedges, handles, medical splints, practice weapons, stamps, labels, ritual counters, lock impressions, and evidence casts.

These implements are not metal and cannot replace specialized high-quality tools for every purpose. They can, however, grant advantage on checks to preserve evidence, copy an impression, mark a sealed object, splint an injury, create a temporary handle, or test whether a key shape fits a lock.

sections.summary: You may use Fine Work to create temporary wax tools, keys, wedges, handles, medical splints, practice weapons, stamps, labels, ritual counters, lock impressions, and evidence casts.

sections.name: Sealed Archive
rules: You create a wax-sealed archive for evidence, memories, letters, maps, relics, ingredients, court records, medical notes, or corpse-tags. The archive may be a chest, wall, rack, candle hall, ledger, or sealed cabinet.

While the archive remains undamaged, its contents resist ordinary decay, tampering, weather, vermin, and casual theft. A creature that opens the archive without your permission must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become marked by a Witness Seal for 24 hours.
This creates a temporary protected archive, not a permanent sect vault. Permanent archives require GM-approved sect-scale work.
sections.summary: Rite. 1 hour. Cost 4 CP. Duration 30 days.

sections.name: Seal of Preservation
rules: For the seal’s duration, the target gains advantage on saving throws against that danger. If the target is already suffering from the chosen danger, it may immediately make one new saving throw or ability check to resist or stabilize it if the GM judges the effect permits repeated attempts.
sections.summary: When you place a Preserving Seal on a living willing creature, choose one condition or danger: poison, disease, bleeding, exhaustion from exposure, suffocation from smoke, or ordinary environmental contamination.

sections.name: Seal Wound
ordered: You seal a wound with medicinal wax, pressure, and qi. The target gains temporary hit points equal to 1d6 + your Proficiency Bonus. If the target is bleeding, suffering from a mundane open wound, or taking ongoing damage from a wound effect that can be physically sealed, the GM may allow the target to make a new saving throw or ability check to end that effect.
This is not general healing. It is emergency closure, preservation, and stabilization.

sections.summary: Action. Touch. Cost 1 CP.

sections.name: Searing Seal
rules: A creature cannot lose Reactions from your Searing Seal more than once per round.
sections.summary: When you kindle a Wax Seal on a hostile creature, you may spend 1 CP to make it sear. The creature makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it takes 2d8 fire damage and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and suffers no Reaction loss.

sections.name: Smoke Wick
rules: Creatures that do not need to breathe can still have their sight blocked by the smoke.
sections.summary: When you use Smoke Puff, the smoke fills a 10-foot radius instead of a 5-foot radius. The area is Heavily Obscured until the start of your next turn, then becomes Lightly Obscured until the end of your next turn.

sections.name: Sovereign Seal of the Chosen Shape
rules: You place a sovereign Wax Seal on one creature or object. An unwilling creature makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, choose one chosen shape.
Shape of Stillness. The target’s Speed becomes 0, and it cannot teleport unless it first succeeds on a Charisma saving throw at the end of its turn.

Shape of Truth. The target cannot benefit from mundane disguise, physical masks, or shapechanging to conceal its basic body outline. Illusions are not dispelled, but creatures have advantage on checks to notice that something is being hidden.

Shape of Preservation. The target cannot be reduced below 1 hit point by damage from a source you can see, once during the duration. When this protection triggers, the seal ends and you gain one level of exhaustion or lose CP equal to your Proficiency Bonus, your choice.

Shape of Closure. One object, portal, container, wound, door, or threshold becomes sealed. Opening or crossing it requires a successful check or saving throw against your Cultivation Save DC, as appropriate to the situation.
A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the seal on a success.
sections.summary: Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 4 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute.

sections.name: Tempered Sealant
ordered: Your Set Wax and Wax Seals no longer have vulnerability to fire damage unless the fire comes from a creature whose Cultivation Level, Challenge Rating, or spell level is higher than your Cultivation Level or the GM decides the heat is overwhelming.
Your wax also resists ordinary rain, desert heat, cold rooms, household flame, and casual attempts to melt it.
rules: Your wax also resists ordinary rain, desert heat, cold rooms, household flame, and casual attempts to melt it.
sections.summary: Your Set Wax and Wax Seals no longer have vulnerability to fire damage unless the fire comes from a creature whose Cultivation Level, Challenge Rating, or spell level is higher than your Cultivation Level or the GM decides the heat is overwhelming.

sections.name: The Last Candle Refuses to Forget the Departed
rules: You light the last candle for a creature, place, oath, family, sect, battlefield, or vanished event that should have been forgotten. The candle burns with wax made from memory, evidence, grief, and refusal.
Choose one miracle.

Name Preserved. A creature whose name has been erased, denied, or ritually suppressed can be spoken again by those present. This does not defeat all curses, but it creates a true foothold for later Spirit, Fate, Dream, Blood, or ancestral restoration.

Trace Sheltered. A departing soul-trace, ancestral echo, final memory, or oath-fragment is preserved for 24 hours even if ordinary rites would fail. This does not imprison the dead. It prevents immediate scattering.

Evidence Refuses Fire. One physical record, body, trace, wound pattern, seal, footprint, weapon mark, or corpse-tag destroyed within the last day reappears as a wax Impression clear enough to be examined.

Door Remembered. A sealed, hidden, burned, moved, or forgotten threshold briefly appears as a wax outline. For 1 minute, creatures present can see where the passage was, what opened it, and what kind of seal closed it.

After using this inheritance, the candle leaves a permanent mark on your cultivation base. Until you complete a significant funeral, justice, remembrance, or reconciliation deed, you cannot use this inheritance again.
sections.summary: Forbidden Rite. 1 minute. Cost 8 CP.

sections.name: Thousand
rules: You surround yourself with many refined masks, hand impressions, name plaques, and wax figures. For the duration, you gain the following benefits.
You have advantage on checks made to create, detect, or analyze physical disguises, false bodies, forged handprints, seals, and masks.

When a creature hits you with an attack, you may use your Reaction to cause one wax false-face to break. The attack still hits, but the attacker becomes impressed by your Wax until the end of your next turn.
You may create a Wax Mask as an Action without the normal Rite time.
Once during the duration, when you would fail a Charisma check based on appearance, etiquette, legal identity, or ceremonial presence, you may reroll the check.
This does not alter your soul, aura, memories, voice, cultivation signature, or true identity.
sections.summary: Action. Cost 4 CP. Duration 1 hour.

sections.name: Waxen Bulwark
rules: Until the bulwark is destroyed or the effect ends, the first ally each round who starts their turn adjacent to it may choose to gain half cover until the start of their next turn, even if the bulwark would normally provide only partial protection.
sections.summary: When you create a Wax Rampart, you may spend 1 additional CP to make it a bulwark. Allies adjacent to the bulwark when it appears gain temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

sections.name: Waxen City of One Breath - Sovereign Mold Technique
ordered: Action. Cost 5 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 10 minutes.
You exhale a sovereign quantity of cultivated wax, shaping a battlefield district in a 60-foot radius centered on a point you can see within 120 feet. Choose up to four features when you create it.
Soft avenues that are Difficult Terrain for enemies.
Set Wax ramparts providing half cover.
Candle roads that allow allies to ignore your wax terrain.
Sealed doors, walls, or booths that require checks to open.
Raised platforms, bridges, stairs, or channels.
Preserving alcoves where allies gain temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus when they first enter.
Witness seals that mark the first enemy each round to damage a wax structure.

The city is temporary, visible, and material. It is not a real settlement and cannot create valuable goods. It can, however, transform a battlefield into a wax-sealed court, clinic, maze, barricade, or funeral avenue.

sections.summary: Action. Cost 5 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 10 minutes.

sections.name: Waxen Shell
ordered: Action. Range Touch. Cost 1 CP. Duration 1 minute.

You coat a willing creature in a flexible wax shell. The target gains temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. While any of these temporary hit points remain, the target has advantage on saving throws against being moved by wind, water, ordinary slippery terrain, or minor forced movement caused by unstable footing.
The shell is visible and may impose disadvantage on checks requiring delicate touch if the GM judges the wax would interfere.

The shell is visible and may impose disadvantage on checks requiring delicate touch if the GM judges the wax would interfere.
sections.summary: Action. Range Touch. Cost 1 CP. Duration 1 minute.

sections.name: Waxen Trail
rules: If the creature teleports, turns invisible, or changes shape while sealed, the seal snaps and leaves an obvious wax mark at the point of departure.
sections.summary: When a sealed creature moves, you may choose to have the seal leave a faint wax thread, scent, footprint line, or candle-colored trace. For the duration, you have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) or Intelligence (Investigation) checks made to track that creature through ordinary terrain.

sections.name: Wax Cage
ordered: Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 2 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute.

You create bars, sheets, cords, or lattices of Set Wax around one Large or smaller creature within range. The target makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it is Restrained by the wax. On a success, it moves to the nearest unoccupied space of its choice outside the cage and is not restrained.

A restrained creature can use its Action to attempt a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against your Cultivation Save DC, ending the restraint on a success. The cage can also be destroyed.
Wax Cage is visibly material. It can be cut, burned, broken, or bypassed by teleportation unless another talent prevents that.

sections.summary: Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 2 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute.

sections.name: Wax Effigy - Effigy Rite
ordered: Rite. 10 minutes. Range Touch. Cost 2 CP. Duration 24 hours.

You sculpt a small wax effigy of a creature, place, object, wound, oath, or event. The effigy must be based on a true Impression, eyewitness description, personal token, name-seal, or significant physical sample.
Memory Vessel. A creature who studies the effigy has advantage on one Intelligence check made to recall, recognize, reconstruct, or explain the subject represented by the effigy.
Message Vessel. You may record a short spoken message, image, gesture, or emotional impression into the effigy. The first creature you designate who touches the effigy receives the message.
Ritual Focus. The effigy can serve as a focus for a later Wax, Spirit, Fate, Blood, Divination, or Formation ritual if the GM agrees the link is appropriate.
Wax Effigy does not harm or control the subject by itself.

A sealed creature can use its Action to attempt a Strength saving throw against your Cultivation Save DC, breaking free on a success. The tomb can also be destroyed as a Set Wax object. A creature reduced to 0 hit points inside the tomb is stabilized rather than killed unless you choose to kindle the tomb with a Wick talent.

sections.name: Yin Domain: Court of Waning Return
rules: You establish a Domain where actions begin to return to stillness before they fully complete.

sections.name: Lesser Exorcism
sections.summary: Choose one Intrusion attached to the target that you can perceive:

items: 6 or More Lower: End one ordinary temporary Intrusion. For Possession, achieve Grade 2 Separation and place the Intruder in its legal adjacent manifestation, legal vessel, or visible noncontrolling outline. A permanent, Secret, artifact, divine, or explicitly anchored Intrusion is suppressed until the scene ends and reveals one printed release requirement instead.

3–5 Lower: Suppress the Intrusion for up to 1 minute while you maintain Concentration. The Host immediately repeats one saving throw the Intrusion allows with Advantage. The Intruder becomes perceptible and cannot conceal its link during suppression.

Within 2: Suppress the Intrusion until the end of the target's next turn. The Host immediately repeats one allowed saving throw with Advantage. If no repeat save exists, suppression is the complete result.

3 or More Higher: Do not suppress it. The Host immediately repeats one allowed saving throw with Advantage. Expose the Intrusion's manifestation and the direction of its sustaining Anchor to your Spiritual Sense until the end of your next turn.
groups.lead: On a successful check, compare Source CL:

sections.name: Resolution
rules: On a failed check, the Intrusion remains. Learn its broad category, its Source CL band relative to you, and whether it is sustained by a creature, Bond, vessel, location, Domain, or Spiritual Anchor.

A willing Host may waive resistance made on its behalf. A willing Intruder does not resist separation. If both Host and Intruder oppose separation, use the higher relevant Cultivation Save DC; if only one opposes, use that opponent's DC.
sections.summary: Make a Spirit Awakening Cultivation Check against the Intrusion's Cultivation Save DC. If it has no printed DC, use the possessing spirit's or creator's Cultivation Save DC. If neither exists, use the Rules Reference fallback Authority DC for the source's Realm.

sections.name: Limits
rules: - Lesser Exorcism cannot destroy a Complete Soul, transfer spirit ownership, create a Companion Bond, strip integrated ancestry, or remove legal character options.

rules: - Move along that route without provoking. This is not teleportation. Total cover, a sealed Formation, spatial lock, or a surviving solid barrier stops the movement at the nearest legal space before it. Occupied spaces and ordinary open gaps can be crossed only when your body can physically pass; you cannot end in an occupied space.

- After reaching the final space, choose any number of creatures within 20 feet. Each makes one Dexterity save and is affected once. Damage is 8d10 Force or Thunder, chosen for the activation, plus 1d10 for each Thunder Charge spent.

- On failure apply full damage, Prone, a 20-foot push directly away, and Reaction denial through the end of the target's next turn. On success apply half damage and a 5-foot push; it retains Reactions.
- Resolve pushes after damage. A blocked push stops at the nearest legal space and creates no collision unless another rule expressly creates one.

- Each eligible unattended object, temporary barrier, vehicle, structure, and Formation Anchor in the area takes one packet equal to twice the rolled damage. It makes no save unless its own profile says otherwise. Permanent world terrain must still be a legal target.

- After all area effects resolve, gain Resistance to all damage except Psychic and Void until the start of your next turn. Record one pending unarmed-strike rider before the end of your next turn; on a hit it adds 4d8 Force to that hit's packet. Reapplication is impossible because the feature is once per scene.
- Adamantine Descent does not automatically create a crater, destroy anatomy, silence an area, or pass through a surviving barrier.
sections.summary: - Choose an unoccupied legal destination within 120 feet and a continuous physical route through open air from your current space. At least 3 Thunder Charges are required. Spend the Action, 7 Stamina, and every current Thunder Charge when declared.

sections.name: Body of the Unbroken Bolt
rules: Unarmed strikes ignore ordinary Resistance to Bludgeoning, Lightning, Thunder, and Force.
Once per round when a hostile creature within reach misses you with a melee attack, gain 1 Thunder Charge.
sections.summary: Gain Resistance to Force and Thunder, Immunity to Deafened, Advantage against Paralyzed and Stunned, and Immunity to ordinary bone-breaking effects.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Body of the Unbroken Bolt
rules: - Advantage applies to saving throws made to avoid or end Paralyzed and Stunned. Immunity to ordinary bone-breaking effects prevents ordinary physical fracture and its direct penalties; it does not prevent Hit Point damage, nonbone Injury, Foundation damage, conceptual destruction, or explicit higher-authority anatomical effects.

- Unarmed strikes ignore ordinary Resistance to Bludgeoning, Lightning, Thunder, and Force. “Ordinary” excludes Immunity, artifact defenses, divine authority, Secret protections, Immortal defenses, and an explicit equal- or higher-Source-CL rule that cannot be bypassed.

- Once per round after a hostile creature currently within your reach resolves a melee attack against you and misses, gain 1 Thunder Charge subject to the normal maximum and one-normal-Charge-per-round limit.
- Reach expansion around a creature does not retroactively make an earlier miss qualify.
sections.summary: - Force and Thunder Resistance use ordinary damage ordering. Deafened Immunity blocks the condition but does not create hearing in silence, vacuum, destroyed hearing anatomy, or a stronger sensory suppression.

facts: You hit with an unarmed strike.

allowlist: results not directly after their save/attack
sections.name: Heaven-Breaking Knuckle
outcomes: Choose two; on a success, choose one of the first four:
rules: - Push 15 feet.
- Knock Prone.
- No Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Reduce AC by 2 until the start of your next turn.
- End one temporary barrier, ward, or defensive stance whose Source CL is no higher than yours.
The AC reduction does not stack.
sections.summary: Deal an additional 4d8 Force or Thunder.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Heaven-Breaking Knuckle
rules: - On failure choose two different results. On success choose one of the first four results; ending a defense is not available on success.
- The 15-foot push moves directly away along a legal route. Prone applies after movement. Reaction denial lasts until the start of the target's next turn.
- AC reduction begins after the hit and lasts until the start of your next turn. Reapplication refreshes and does not stack with itself.

- To choose the fifth result, identify one temporary barrier, ward, or defensive stance currently benefiting the target or occupying its space whose Source CL is no higher than this feature's Source CL. It must be a persistent temporary effect that expressly grants AC, cover, Resistance, damage reduction, attack Disadvantage, movement denial, or another defensive benefit.

- The selected defense ends after the triggering hit resolves. This result does not end permanent anatomy, armor, a Foundation, Method, Domain, artifact property, Immortal feature, beneficial condition without a persistent source, or an effect with higher Source CL.
- One use cannot select the same result twice.
sections.summary: - Declare after an unarmed strike hits, spend 2 Stamina and 2 Thunder Charges, and add 4d8 Force or Thunder to the triggering hit's packet. The same target then makes one Constitution save.

facts: You take Bludgeoning, Force, Lightning, or Thunder damage.
sections.name: Thunder Runs Through Bone
rules: If reduced to 0, gain 1 Thunder Charge, move 10 feet without provoking, and your next unarmed strike before the end of your next turn has Advantage. This Charge can exceed the normal gain limit.
sections.summary: Reduce damage by 2d10 + Constitution modifier.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Thunder Runs Through Bone
rules: - Reduce that packet by 2d10 + Constitution modifier at the shared flat-reduction step. It can combine with Stamina Guard or another legal reduction according to damage ordering.

- If final triggering damage applied becomes 0, gain 1 Thunder Charge even if you already gained a normal Charge this round, up to the normal maximum. Then move up to 10 feet without provoking along a legal route.
- Record Advantage on your next unarmed strike made before the end of your next turn. A new successful use refreshes, rather than stacks with, this pending Advantage.
- The movement and Advantage occur after the damage packet resolves. If no legal movement exists, remain in place and retain the other benefits.
- A packet that was canceled before damage existed, was not one of the listed types, or was reduced to 0 solely before this feature applied does not produce the extra Charge or follow-up benefits.
sections.summary: - Declare when one Bludgeoning, Force, Lightning, or Thunder damage packet would be applied to you, after percentage modifiers are known but before Hit Points are reduced. Spend the Reaction and 1 Stamina.

items: Become Large if smaller.
Unarmed reach +10 feet.
Resistance to all damage except Fire, Psychic, and Void.
Unarmed strikes deal 1d12 before modifiers.
Once per turn on a hit, additional 4d8 Piercing or Slashing.
Gain 1 Demon Spine at the start of each turn.
Maximum Spines +3.
Healing reduction applies only at 6 or more Spines.

sections.name: Calamity Briar Incarnation
sections.summary: Gain Demon Spines to maximum.

sections.name: Forest of Impalement
rules: - Successful Save: Half damage, pushed 10 feet, not Restrained.
A Restrained creature repeats the Dexterity save at the end of each turn, ending the state and falling safely to the nearest legal space on a success.
The thorn forest remains until the start of your next turn and is difficult terrain for hostile creatures.
sections.summary: - Failed Save: 8d8 Piercing, Restrained, Bleeding, and lifted up to 10 feet.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Calamity Briar Incarnation
rules: - The printed +10-foot reach is the transformation's reach increase and does not stack with Crown of Black Thorns' +5-foot reach unless the source explicitly says both apply; use the higher +10-foot increase.
- Resistance excludes Fire, Psychic, and Void. The 1d12 unarmed die replaces the normal base die; the once-per-turn 4d8 rider is separate.
- Gain 1 Spine at the start of each turn as a direct gain, even if the ordinary once-per-round gain flag is already used. Healing reduction uses the temporary 6-Spine threshold.
- Forest of Impalement: The Action creates a 30-foot-radius projected Body Field centered on you until the start of your next turn. Each affected creature saves once.

- On failure deal 8d8 Piercing, apply Restrained and Bleeding, and lift the target up to 10 feet vertically if a legal space exists. On success deal half, push 10 feet directly away, and do not Restrict.

- A Restrained creature repeats the Dexterity save at the end of each turn. On success it ends this restraint and moves or falls to the nearest legal supporting space without taking falling damage from the feature's own lift.
- The Field is difficult terrain for hostile creatures and moves with you because it remains centered on you. It creates no permanent terrain, harvestable demon-wood, or automatic Injury.
sections.summary: - On activation, gain Spines to the transformed maximum after increasing that maximum by 3. Become Large if smaller using transformation and legal-space procedures.

sections.name: Crown of Black Thorns
rules: Once per turn, when a hostile creature reaches the first qualifying space while willingly entering your unarmed reach or moving 10 feet within it, spend 1 Demon Spine without using an action. It makes a Dexterity save.
- Failed Save: 3d8 Piercing, movement ends in that space, and Bleeding.
- Successful Save: Half damage and movement continues.
A creature triggers once per turn.
sections.summary: Gain Resistance to Piercing and Slashing, Immunity to ordinary bleeding effects, and your Demon Spine damage ignores Resistance to Piercing and Slashing. While you have at least 1 Spine, unarmed reach increases by 5 feet during your turn.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Crown of Black Thorns
rules: - Demon Spine damage ignores ordinary Piercing and Slashing Resistance, not Immunity or a superior Source CL defense expressly immune to penetration.
- The 5-foot reach increase functions during your turn while at least 1 Spine remains. Spending the last Spine removes the reach after the current feature's trigger finishes.

- For the movement trigger, identify the first space a hostile creature reaches while willingly entering your unarmed reach or after it accumulates 10 feet of willing movement within that reach. It can trigger once per turn.

- Spend 1 Spine without an action before the creature leaves that qualifying space. It makes one Dexterity save. On failure deal 3d8, end its current movement in that space, and apply Bleeding; on success deal half and allow movement to continue.
- Teleportation, forced movement, and being carried do not trigger unless the movement is willingly performed by the target itself.
sections.summary: - Piercing and Slashing Resistance follows normal ordering. Immunity to ordinary bleeding does not grant Immunity to every blood, Injury, poison, or supernatural curse effect.

facts: Until the start of your next turn
sections.name: Impaling Garden
rules: - Successful Save: Half damage, Speed reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn, not Restrained.
The area is difficult terrain for hostile creatures. A Restrained creature may use its Action for a Strength check against your DC, ending the restraint on a success.
sections.summary: - Failed Save: 5d8 Piercing, Restrained until the start of your next turn, and Bleeding.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Impaling Garden
rules: - Choose hostile creatures in the area or affect every hostile creature according to the campaign's area convention; record the selection consistently. Each target makes one Dexterity save once per activation.
- On failure, deal 5d8 Piercing, apply Bleeding, and Restrict until the start of your next turn. On success, deal half, reduce Speed by 10 feet for the same duration, and do not Restrict.
- A Restrained target can use its Action for one Strength check against your Cultivation Save DC, ending only this restraint on success.
- Hostile creatures treat the area as difficult terrain. The Field does not block line of effect, create cover, damage unattended creatures, or produce permanent thorns unless another rule says so.
- Suppression or loss of the feature makes the Field dormant and ends its restraint and difficult terrain; already dealt damage remains.
sections.summary: - The Action creates a temporary projected Body Field in a 15-foot-radius sphere centered on you until the start of your next turn. It moves with you because it remains centered on you.

facts: A creature within reach hits you with a melee attack, Grapples you, or begins its turn Grappling you.
sections.name: Spines Answer Violence
rules: - Successful Save: Half damage and no Bleeding.
If Grappling you, resolve damage before any check to maintain or move the Grapple.
sections.summary: - Failed Save: 3d8 Piercing, Bleeding, and pushed 5 feet if not Grappling you.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Spines Answer Violence
rules: - Spend the Reaction and 1 Spine. The triggering creature makes one Dexterity save.
- On failure, deal 3d8 Piercing, apply Bleeding, and push 5 feet if it is not currently Grappling you. On success, deal half and apply no Bleeding.

- When the target is Grappling you, resolve damage before it attempts to move you or before another maintenance check. Damage alone does not automatically break the Grapple; use the normal Grapple and anatomy procedures.
- A single event triggers one use. Beginning the turn Grappling you does not also count as a new Grapple event.
sections.summary: - Declare after one listed trigger occurs. A melee hit triggers before its damage is applied; becoming Grappled triggers after the Grapple succeeds; beginning a turn Grappling you triggers at that turn's start before movement.

facts: You hit with an unarmed strike.

sections.name: Thorn-Flesh Armory
outcomes: The target becomes Bleeding until the start of your next turn. The first time it willingly moves 10 feet or makes an attack, it takes damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus and Bleeding ends.
