rules: Deal an additional 2d6 Piercing or Slashing.
sections.summary: Unarmed strikes may deal Piercing or Slashing.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Thorn-Flesh Armory and Bleeding
rules: - After a hit, spend 1 Spine, choose Piercing or Slashing, and add 2d6 to the hit once per turn. The target then makes one Constitution save.
- On failure, create one Bleeding record until the start of your next turn. A new Bleeding from this Subpath refreshes the duration and does not stack damage.

- The first time the target willingly moves a cumulative 10 feet or makes an attack while Bleeding, it takes damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus using the selected Piercing or Slashing type and Bleeding ends after the triggering action or movement commits.
- Forced movement, teleportation, involuntary falling, standing, and movement below 10 cumulative feet do not trigger it. An attack still triggers when it misses.

- Bleeding is a temporary Subpath condition, not an Injury, ordinary wound rule, or automatic blood loss. Immunity to ordinary bleeding applies only if its Source Rule covers supernatural Body conditions.
sections.summary: - Your unarmed strikes can choose Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing for each attack. This changes damage type but grants no separate weapon, reach, or attack.

facts: You took the Attack action and made at least one Staff attack during the turn
sections.name: Flowing Spin
ordered: Make one additional Staff attack. Its damage die is 1d6 before modifiers if the weapon's normal damage die is lower.
This attack follows the Granted Attack rule.
rules: This attack follows the Granted Attack rule.
sections.summary: Make one additional Staff attack. Its damage die is 1d6 before modifiers if the weapon's normal damage die is lower.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Flowing Spin
rules: - The Bonus Action makes exactly one additional Staff attack. It is a granted attack and cannot grant another attack.

- If the Staff's normal damage die is lower than 1d6, use 1d6 before modifiers for this attack. If it is 1d6 or higher, use the normal die. This floor does not add a second die and does not replace other printed damage.
- The requirement is not satisfied by an Opportunity Attack, Reaction attack, Flowing Spin attack, or another attack outside the Attack action.
sections.summary: - Confirm the requirement after at least one Staff attack has been made as part of the Attack action during the current turn. The attack need not have hit.

items: Your Staff reach increases by another 5 feet.
Gain one additional Reaction each round, usable only for a Staff Opportunity Attack, Deflecting Staff, or another Staff feature.
Hostile creatures provoke Opportunity Attacks when entering your reach.
A creature hit by your Opportunity Attack has its Speed reduced to 0 for the remainder of the turn.
You and allies within 10 feet gain Half Cover against ranged weapon attacks and physical projectiles.
Push the target 10 feet.
Move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Prevent the target from taking Reactions until the start of its next turn.
Gain +1 AC until the start of your next turn.
groups.lead: Once per turn after hitting with a Staff attack, choose one:

sections.name: Heavenly Staff Barrier
sections.summary: For the duration:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Heavenly Staff Barrier
rules: - Reach geometry. During the barrier, your Staff reach is increased by 5 feet outside your turn and by a total of 10 feet during your turn: 5 feet from Staff Form and another 5 feet from this feature. This lets entry into the barrier reach provoke as printed.

- The additional Reaction refreshes at the start of each round and can be spent only on a Staff Opportunity Attack, Deflecting Staff, or a Reaction explicitly identified as a Staff feature. It does not remove any once-per-round limit.

- A hostile creature provokes when it voluntarily enters your current Staff reach. Forced movement, teleportation, appearing in place, and the reach expanding around a creature do not provoke unless another rule says they do.
- On a Staff Opportunity Attack hit, Speed becomes 0 only for the remainder of the current turn. It does not end a teleport already completed or retroactively cancel movement before the hit.

- The 10-foot Half Cover aura moves with you, requires no action, and applies only against ranged weapon attacks and physical projectiles. A creature receives the benefit while within the aura at the instant the attack is resolved.

- The once-per-turn hit rider is chosen after a Staff hit resolves. The 10-foot self-movement requires a legal route and does not provoke. The AC option lasts exactly until the start of your next turn and does not stack with itself.
sections.summary: - You must wield a Staff to receive its reach, Opportunity Attack, Deflecting Staff, and cover benefits. If you cease wielding one, those benefits become dormant while the duration continues and resume when you wield one again.

items: Use Constitution instead of Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls.
You may use your Cultivation Attack Modifier for its attack rolls.
It is integrated into your Body Refining cultivation.
Its reach increases by 5 feet during your turn.
Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply to it.

sections.name: Staff Form
rules: This does not grant the Spear or Weapons Sphere.
sections.summary: Gain proficiency with Staff weapons.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Staff Form
rules: - Ability and attack choice. For each Staff attack, choose Constitution or another ability the weapon already permits. If you choose Constitution, use the Cultivation Attack Modifier and Constitution for damage. The same attack cannot add two ability modifiers unless another rule expressly permits it.

- Integrated weapon. The wielded Staff is an integrated weapon while you wield it. Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply their cultivation-powered, adamantine, Force-damage, and object-damage permissions; they do not replace the Staff's normal damage die with the Iron Fist die unless another Source Rule explicitly does so.

- Turn-limited reach. The 5-foot increase applies to Staff attacks and Staff features only during your own turn. It does not enlarge your ordinary threatened reach for Opportunity Attacks outside your turn. Heavenly Staff Barrier changes this geometry as stated in its normalized procedure.
- No Sphere grant. Staff Form does not grant a Sphere, Sphere talent, Recorded Art, or proficiency with another Polearm.
sections.summary: - Staff record. A Staff is a quarterstaff or a weapon carrying the Staff tag. Record the specific weapon integrated by this feature. Its item properties, enhancement, damage type, handedness, and other tags remain unchanged unless this Subpath expressly changes them.

items: Gain +1 AC.
Gain Advantage against being Disarmed.
Gain Advantage on Opportunity Attacks made with the Staff.

facts: You or an ally within 5 feet takes damage from a ranged weapon attack or physical projectile.

items: Catch the projectile if it is small enough to hold.
Deflect it into an unoccupied space within 15 feet.
Move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Grant the protected ally Half Cover until the start of your next turn.
groups.lead: If this reduces the damage to 0, choose one:

sections.name: Deflecting Staff
rules: Deflecting Staff does not block a ray, beam, purely energetic projectile, or save-based area effect.
sections.summary: Reduce the damage by 2d10 + Constitution modifier.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Staff of One
rules: - Advantage against being Disarmed applies to checks and saving throws made specifically to retain the Staff. It does not prevent theft while you are helpless or the destruction of the weapon by a legal higher-authority effect.
- The Opportunity Attack Advantage applies only when the attack is made with the Staff.

- Deflecting Staff timing. Declare after the triggering ranged weapon attack or discrete physical projectile has determined damage but before that packet reduces Hit Points. Apply the reduction as an other flat reduction under the shared damage order.

- “Physical projectile” means a discrete material projectile whose path can be intercepted, including ordinary ammunition, thrown weapons, stones, needles, bolts, and comparable manifested matter. It excludes rays, beams, purely energetic bolts, sound, gaze effects, save-based areas, and effects whose rule says they cannot be physically intercepted.

- If a mixed damage packet qualifies because the attack is delivered by a physical projectile, reduce the entire triggering packet. A separate explosion, poison cloud, curse, or area effect created after impact is not canceled unless its Source Rule says interception prevents it.

- If damage becomes 0, choose exactly one printed option. Catching requires a discrete object small enough for one free hand and does not duplicate ammunition or an item. Deflecting into a space ends the triggering attack against its original target; it does not make an attack against another creature. The 5-foot movement must end in a legal space. Half Cover applies only to the protected ally and lasts as printed.
- Deflecting Staff remains once per round even if another feature grants an additional Reaction.
sections.summary: - The +1 AC requires you to be wielding a Staff. It is an AC bonus, not a base AC calculation, and does not stack with another instance of Staff of One.

facts: You hit with a Staff attack.
lossy: allowlist: result followed by a list
allowlist: results not directly after their save/attack
sections.name: Sweeping Strike
rules: - Knock the target Prone.
- Push it 10 feet.
- Move it to another unoccupied space within your reach.
- Prevent it from taking Reactions until the start of its next turn.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Sweeping Strike
rules: - Prone and Reaction denial apply after the hit resolves.
- A push moves directly away from you along the shortest legal route. A target that cannot move the full distance moves as far as legally possible; no collision damage is created.

- “Move it to another unoccupied space within your reach” is forced physical repositioning, not teleportation. Choose a legal space within your current Staff reach. The target travels through a legal route no longer than the distance between its original and destination spaces and cannot pass through a solid barrier or an occupied space unless ordinary forced movement permits it.
- On a successful save, the 5-foot push is mandatory. If no legal space exists, the target remains in place and no substitute effect is invented.
- One target can be affected by Sweeping Strike only once per turn from you, even if you make multiple Staff attacks.
sections.summary: - Declare the feature after the Staff attack hits and its ordinary hit damage is determined. Spend Stamina before the target rolls the save.

facts: An attack deals damage to you.
sections.name: Bone Armor
ordered: Reduce the triggering damage by 2d8 + Constitution modifier if it includes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, or 1d8 + Constitution modifier otherwise.
Bone Armor and Stamina Guard both require your Reaction. You cannot use both against the same damage packet unless another feature grants and permits a second Reaction.
rules: Bone Armor and Stamina Guard both require your Reaction. You cannot use both against the same damage packet unless another feature grants and permits a second Reaction.
sections.summary: Reduce the triggering damage by 2d8 + Constitution modifier if it includes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, or 1d8 + Constitution modifier otherwise.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Bone Armor
rules: - If the packet includes any Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, use 2d8 + Constitution modifier against the entire triggering packet. Otherwise use 1d8 + Constitution modifier. Mixed packets are not split for this choice.
- Apply the result as an other flat reduction in the shared damage order. It cannot reduce damage below 0.
- Bone Armor and Stamina Guard each require a Reaction. A separate additional Reaction is not enough by itself; another Source Rule must also explicitly permit both to modify the same damage packet.
- Flavorful bone cracking does not create an Injury. Any actual bone Injury follows the shared bodily-harm hierarchy.
sections.summary: - Declare Bone Armor after the attack's damage packet is determined but before that packet reduces your Hit Points. The triggering attack must have hit and be dealing damage.

sections.name: Bone Guard Manifestation
ordered: Manifest one Bone Guard. You may maintain only one at a time.
sections.summary: Manifest one Bone Guard. You may maintain only one at a time.

sections.name: Bone Guard Statistics
rules: - AC: 14 + Proficiency Bonus
- Hit Points: 5 x your CL
- Speed: 30 feet
- Saving Throws: Uses your saving-throw modifiers
- Immunities: Poison damage, Poisoned
- Cultivation Level: Your CL
sections.summary: - Size: Medium

sections.name: Bone Strike
sections.summary: Melee Cultivation Attack: Uses your Cultivation Attack Modifier; reach 5 feet; hit 2d8 + Constitution modifier Piercing or Bludgeoning damage.

sections.name: Guard the Sovereign
rules: The Bone Guard acts immediately after your turn. As a Bonus Action, command it to Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Move, or Guard one creature or doorway. Without a command, it takes Dodge and remains within 30 feet of you if possible.
It disappears at 0 Hit Points, when the duration ends, or when you create another.
sections.summary: Reaction: When you or an ally within 5 feet of the Bone Guard is targeted by an attack, impose Disadvantage on that attack roll.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Bone Guard Manifestation
rules: - It occupies a Medium space. It has no ability scores or proficiencies beyond what its printed statistics require. “Uses your saving-throw modifiers” means use the numerical modifier shown on your character record for the called save; it gains no separate save proficiency.

- The Guard can move normally during its turn. When you command Attack, it may move and make one Bone Strike. Dash, Disengage, Dodge, and Help use the corresponding action and allow ordinary movement. Move lets it move up to its Speed and take no action. Guard lets it move and prepare Guard the Sovereign.

- Issuing the command costs your Bonus Action. The source prints no command distance, so no additional distance limit is imposed while you and the Guard are on the same plane and no effect blocks your direct cultivation control.
- Without a command, it takes Dodge and, if possible, uses movement to remain within 30 feet of you. It does not independently choose attacks or tactics.

- Guard the Sovereign is the Bone Guard's Reaction, usable once per round. Declare after a legal protected creature is targeted but before the attack roll. The Guard must be within 5 feet of that creature at that moment.

- Bone Strike is a cultivation attack made by the Guard using your Cultivation Attack Modifier. The Guard is the attack's origin, but you remain the controlling Source Rule for Source CL and feature attribution. It cannot deliver your personal hit riders unless a feature expressly permits it.
- Ordinary creature healing does not restore the Guard unless the healing rule can target a Body Asset. At 0 Hit Points it disappears with no transferable remains, materials, or injury to you.
sections.summary: - The Bone Guard is a manifested Body Asset, not a Complete Soul, Companion, independent character, corpse, or harvestable supply of permanent bone. Creating another causes the existing Guard to disappear.

items: End one Bleeding state affecting you whose Source CL is no higher than yours.
End one temporary Speed reduction caused by a physical injury whose Source CL is no higher than yours.
Repeat a saving throw against Poisoned with Advantage.
Repeat a saving throw against Paralyzed or Restrained when caused by a broken bone, crushed limb, physical binding, or bodily deformation.

sections.name: Marrow Regeneration
rules: Marrow Regeneration cannot restore a destroyed Foundation, remove a Hidden Injury, or repair soul or identity damage.
sections.summary: Regain 2d10 + Constitution modifier Hit Points, increasing to 3d10 + Constitution modifier at CL14.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Marrow Regeneration
rules: - The healing applies to you only, is ordinary Hit Point healing, and does not reconstruct missing anatomy unless the shared reconstruction rules and another Source Rule permit it.
- Ending Bleeding or a temporary Speed reduction requires the listed state to have Source CL no higher than yours. A higher-Source-CL state is unaffected and the option is spent if selected.

- “Repeat a saving throw” grants one immediate repeat against the original DC and using the original ability. It applies only if the condition has or had a saving throw. On success, resolve the original effect's successful-repeat result; do not invent a new removal rule.

- The physical Paralyzed or Restrained option requires the condition's record to identify broken bone, crushed limb, physical binding, or bodily deformation as its cause. It does not apply to psychic, spiritual, spatial, oath, or conceptual restraint merely described with physical imagery.
- The CL14 increase replaces 2d10 with 3d10; it does not add both expressions.
sections.summary: - The healing and selected secondary benefit occur as one Bonus Action activation. Resolve healing first, then choose one legal option.

facts: You are reduced to 0 Hit Points but are not killed outright.

items: You are Incapacitated.
Your Speed is 0.
You cannot take actions or Reactions.
Your body cannot be targeted separately from the cocoon.
You do not make death saving throws.

sections.name: Sovereign Reconstruction
sections.summary: Instead of falling Unconscious normally, your body collapses into a bone cocoon until the start of your next turn.

items: Regain Hit Points equal to half your maximum.
Stand without spending movement.
End Prone, Grappled, Restrained, and one Bleeding or temporary physical-injury state on yourself.
Each hostile creature of your choice within 10 feet makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 6d6 Piercing damage and falling Prone on a failure, or half damage and remaining standing on a success.
groups.lead: At the start of your next turn, if the cocoon has at least 1 Hit Point:

sections.name: Bone Cocoon
rules: - Hit Points: 5 x your CL
- Resistance: Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing
- Immunity: Poison and Psychic
- Source CL: Your CL
If the cocoon reaches 0 Hit Points, reconstruction fails. You remain at 0 Hit Points and begin making death saving throws at the start of your next turn.
sections.summary: - AC: Your Cultivation Save DC

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Sovereign Reconstruction
rules: - The Bone Cocoon is a Body Asset occupying your current space and matching your size. Your body is contained within it and cannot be targeted separately; an area affecting that space targets the Cocoon normally.
- Damage to the Cocoon does not transfer to you. You retain existing conditions unless the feature ends them on emergence. You make no death saves while the Cocoon has at least 1 Hit Point.

- The Cocoon has no actions, movement, or Reactions. It can be moved, restrained, contained, repaired, or suppressed only when a rule can legally affect a Body Asset. Its printed Resistance and Immunities apply normally.

- At the start of your next turn, check the Cocoon before resolving ordinary start-of-turn effects from your body. If it has at least 1 Hit Point, perform every printed reconstruction step, destroy the Cocoon, and take the turn normally.

- If the Cocoon reaches 0 Hit Points before then, it breaks immediately. You remain at 0 Hit Points in its space, do not receive the reconstruction benefits, and begin normal death-saving-throw timing at the start of your next turn. Excess Cocoon damage does not transfer, but an effect that kills or destroys the contained body explicitly can still do so.
- The emergence burst affects only hostile creatures you choose within 10 feet. Each is affected once. It creates no permanent bone Injury or terrain without another rule.
sections.summary: - Declare when you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, before Unconsciousness or death saves. This is a 0-Hit-Point replacement and cannot resolve together with Marrow Memory or another replacement of the same event.

items: Critical hits against you become normal hits.
Advantage on saving throws against Prone, forced movement, physical paralysis, forced bodily transformation, and effects that break, deform, or liquefy the body.
Your bones cannot be permanently broken by an effect whose Source CL is lower than yours.

sections.name: Unbroken Bones
sections.summary: You gain:

facts: You would be reduced to 0 Hit Points but are not killed outright.
sections.name: Marrow Memory
ordered: You are reduced to 1 Hit Point instead.
Only one feature that prevents or replaces the same reduction to 0 Hit Points may resolve.
rules: Only one feature that prevents or replaces the same reduction to 0 Hit Points may resolve.
sections.summary: You are reduced to 1 Hit Point instead.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Unbroken Bones
rules: - The listed Advantage applies only to checks or saves resisting those physical effects. It does not grant a new save where none is permitted.
- A lower-Source-CL effect cannot create a permanent broken-bone Injury. It may still deal damage or impose its printed temporary condition or Injury for its printed duration.

- Marrow Memory timing. Declare when a resolved damage packet or effect would reduce you to 0 Hit Points but not kill you outright. Spend 4 Stamina and remain at 1 Hit Point. The feature does not remove conditions, restore anatomy, or negate non-damage riders.

- Marrow Memory competes with every other feature replacing the same reduction to 0 Hit Points. Choose one; all unchosen replacements remain unspent unless their rules say declaration already spent them.
sections.summary: - A critical hit against you becomes a normal hit before damage dice and critical-only riders are resolved. It remains a hit and retains noncritical riders.

sections.name: Empty Cup
rules: After the reroll resolves, move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. During this movement, you may fall Prone, stand from Prone, move through one hostile creature's space as difficult terrain, or end in an unoccupied space on the opposite side of the attacker.
If the rerolled attack can still reach your new space, resolve it normally. Otherwise, it misses.
sections.summary: The attacker rerolls the attack with Disadvantage and uses the new result.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Empty Cup
rules: - Determine the rerolled result against your Armor Class before moving, but do not apply damage yet. Then take the granted movement. After movement, recheck the same attack's legal target, reach or range, line of effect, and cover from the attacker's unchanged origin.

- If the reroll misses your Armor Class, the attack misses regardless of movement. If it would hit but can no longer legally reach or target your new space, it misses. Otherwise, resolve the attack and its riders against you normally.

- Passing through one hostile creature's space does not permit you to end there and does not let you pass through an effect that physically blocks passage. The “opposite side” space must be adjacent to the attacker and legal for you.
- This movement occurs during the triggering attack's resolution and cannot itself trigger Empty Cup again.
sections.summary: - Declare after an attack roll has hit but before damage or hit riders resolve. The reroll replaces the original attack roll even if the new result is higher.

facts: You intentionally fall Prone, are knocked Prone, or stand from Prone.
lossy: allowlist: result followed by a list
allowlist: results not directly after their save/attack
sections.name: Falling Fist
rules: - Move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Push the target 5 feet.
- Prevent the target from taking Reactions until the start of its next turn.
This attack follows the Granted Attack rule.
sections.summary: Make one unarmed strike against a creature within reach.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Falling Fist
rules: - Declare the Reaction immediately after the triggering change of posture resolves. The target must then be within current unarmed reach.
- The granted attack cannot trigger another Falling Fist from movement, a fall, or a posture change caused by one of its own riders.
- The 5-foot self-movement occurs after the hit and must use a legal space. The target cannot make an Opportunity Attack against that movement; other creatures can unless another rule says otherwise.
sections.summary: - One event can trigger Falling Fist only once. Intentionally falling Prone and then standing during the same movement are two events, but the once-per-round limit still allows only one use.

items: Gain Advantage on Dexterity saving throws.
Opportunity Attacks against you have Disadvantage.
Standing from Prone costs no movement.
Crawl at your full Speed.
Move through hostile creature spaces as difficult terrain.
Once per round when an enemy misses you, move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Use Falling Fist once per round without spending your Reaction.
Once per turn after intentionally falling Prone, gain +2 AC until the start of your next turn.

sections.name: Heavenly Drunk
rules: The reaction-free Falling Fist still follows the Granted Attack rule.
sections.summary: For the duration:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Heavenly Drunk
rules: - The once-per-round movement when an enemy misses you requires no action and occurs after that attack is fully resolved. A miss created by Empty Cup qualifies, but movement from the same miss occurs only once under this bullet.
- Moving through a hostile space treats each such space as difficult terrain and still requires enough movement. You cannot end in an occupied space.

- The +2 AC begins immediately after you intentionally become Prone and lasts until the start of your next turn. Repeated intentional falls refresh but do not stack it. Being knocked Prone unwillingly does not qualify.
sections.summary: - “Use Falling Fist without spending your Reaction” removes only the Reaction cost. Falling Fist remains limited to once per round total, whether used normally or through this feature.

facts: You hit with an unarmed strike.
lossy: allowlist: result followed by a list
allowlist: results not directly after their save/attack
sections.name: Staggering Blow
outcomes: Move yourself 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
rules: - Knock the target Prone.
- Push it 10 feet.
- Move yourself 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Staggering Blow
rules: - The self-movement options are voluntary granted movement. They must end in a legal space and do not permit movement through creatures unless another rule does.
- The push is directly away from you. If blocked, move the target as far as legally possible; no collision damage is created.
- The Speed reduction modifies each of the target's Speeds and cannot reduce a Speed below 0. Reapplication refreshes rather than stacks.
sections.summary: - Declare after the hit. The target makes one Dexterity save before the selected failed-save effect resolves.

items: Move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Stand from Prone without spending movement.
Fall Prone intentionally, then move 5 feet.
Gain Advantage on your next Dexterity saving throw before the start of your next turn.
Gain Advantage on your next Acrobatics check before the start of your next turn.
groups.lead: Whenever you use Stomping Step, choose one:

sections.name: Swaying Step
rules: The additional movement is separate from the movement granted by Dash.
sections.summary: Gain proficiency in Acrobatics. If already proficient, gain a +2 bonus to Acrobatics checks.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Swaying Step
rules: - The 5-foot movement must end in a legal space. “Fall Prone intentionally, then move” means you become Prone before moving and use your normal Prone movement rules unless the feature or another rule changes them.
- Standing from Prone through this feature spends no movement and can occur even if your Speed is 0, unless a restraint or anatomical effect expressly prevents standing.
- Advantage granted by an option applies to one qualifying roll and expires at the stated time. It does not stack with another source of Advantage.
sections.summary: - Choose exactly one option each time you activate Stomping Step. The option is part of that same activation and does not require another action.

items: Speed doubles.
Advantage on unarmed attack rolls.
Once per turn on a hit, deal an additional 4d8 Force damage.
Ordinary effects cannot Frighten, Paralyze, or Stun you.
Gate damage becomes 1d6 per open Gate.

sections.name: Eighth Gate: Heaven-Defying Gate
sections.summary: When Gate damage reduces you to 0 Hit Points, all Gates close, you fall Unconscious, and Blood Pump, Invincible Iron, Crimson Oni, Sovereign Reconstruction, and similar remain-at-1 features cannot prevent this reduction. You are stable unless another effect states otherwise.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Eighth Gate
rules: - Advantage applies to unarmed attack rolls only. The 4d8 Force damage is once per turn, part of one qualifying hit, and cannot critically multiply separately.

- “Ordinary effects” cannot Frighten, Paralyze, or Stun you. This automatically blocks mundane effects, ordinary creature traits, and lower-Source-CL effects. Artifact, divine, Secret, Tribulation, Foundation, Method, Immortal, or equal- or higher-Source-CL authority can still contest or apply those conditions according to its own rule.
- While Gate 8 is open, every open Gate contributes 1d6 instead of 1d4 Gate damage at the start of your turn.

- If that Gate damage reduces you to 0 Hit Points, close all Gates immediately, ignore every remain-at-1, 0-Hit-Point replacement, delayed-collapse, cocoon, statue, rebirth, reconstruction, or similar feature for that event, fall Unconscious, and become stable.
- The special collapse applies only to Gate damage. A hostile attack or another damage source can still interact with legal 0-Hit-Point replacement features.
- Stability does not restore Hit Points, remove other conditions, prevent later damage, or end a separate effect already affecting you.
sections.summary: - Speed doubling applies after fixed additions to walking Speed. A movement mode equal to walking Speed uses the doubled value; a fixed Speed or teleport range is not doubled.

sections.name: Fifth Gate: Gate of Thunder
rules: This attack follows the Granted Attack rule, cannot replace more than one attack, and does not grant another action.
sections.summary: While open, once during each of your turns when you take the Attack action, make one additional unarmed strike as part of it.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Fifth Gate
rules: - The attack follows the Granted Attack rule, does not create another Attack action, cannot be replaced by several attacks unless a feature expressly permits replacement of a granted attack, and cannot itself grant another attack.
- If you take more than one Attack action during the turn, Gate of Thunder still grants only one additional strike total.
sections.summary: - Once during each of your turns when you take the Attack action, make one additional unarmed strike as part of that same action. Choose its timing among your other attacks.

sections.name: First and Second Gates
rules: - First Gate - Gate of Breath: Speed increases by 10 feet.
- Second Gate - Gate of Blood: Once per turn when you hit with an unarmed strike, deal additional damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
sections.summary: You may open two Gates.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — First and Second Gates
rules: - Gate of Blood's additional damage applies once per turn after an unarmed strike hits. It is part of that hit's damage packet, uses one damage type dealt by the strike as chosen by you, and cannot critically multiply separately.
- The once-per-turn Gate of Blood damage remains one total use across granted attacks, reactions, and additional Attack actions.
sections.summary: - Gate of Breath adds 10 feet to walking Speed. Any movement mode explicitly equal to walking Speed updates from that value; fixed movement modes and teleport ranges do not.

sections.name: Sixth and Seventh Gates
rules: - Seventh Gate - Gate of the Tyrant: Resistance to all damage except Force and Psychic; unarmed strikes ignore ordinary damage Resistance; once per turn on a hit, push 10 feet or prevent Reactions until the start of the target's next turn.
Gate damage is not reduced by Seventh Gate.
sections.summary: - Sixth Gate - Gate of Heaven: Fly Speed equal to walking Speed and Hover.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Sixth and Seventh Gates
rules: - Gate of the Tyrant grants Resistance to every damage type except Force and Psychic. It does not reduce Gate damage because Gate damage expressly bypasses reduction.

- Your unarmed strikes ignore ordinary damage Resistance. “Ordinary” excludes Immunity, artifact defenses, divine authority, Secret protections, Immortal defenses, and a specific equal- or higher-Source-CL rule that states it cannot be bypassed.

- The once-per-turn hit rider is chosen after an unarmed hit. A push moves 10 feet directly away from you along a legal route. Reaction denial lasts until the start of the target's next turn. The rider remains once per turn total.
sections.summary: - Gate of Heaven grants a Fly Speed equal to current walking Speed and Hover. If it closes or is suppressed while you are unsupported, resolve falling immediately unless another flight or support remains.

sections.name: Third and Fourth Gates
rules: - Third Gate - Gate of Tendons: Jump distances tripled, Climb Speed equal to walking Speed, Advantage on Strength and Dexterity ability checks.
- Fourth Gate - Gate of Bone: +2 AC, Advantage against Prone and forced movement, and reduce forced movement by 10 feet.
sections.summary: You may open four Gates.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Third and Fourth Gates
rules: - Gate of Bone's +2 AC is an AC bonus and does not replace your formula. Its Advantage applies to checks or saves made to avoid or resist being knocked Prone or moved against your will.

- Reduce each instance of forced movement by 10 feet after the source determines distance. A distance reduced to 0 causes no movement and no collision unless the source expressly creates an impact without movement.
- Gate of Bone does not reduce teleportation, planar transfer, voluntary movement, or a bodily transformation unless the effect expressly treats itself as forced physical movement.
sections.summary: - Gate of Tendons triples final jump distances after ordinary jump calculations and grants a Climb Speed equal to current walking Speed. Its Advantage applies to Strength and Dexterity ability checks, not attack rolls or saving throws.

sections.name: Five-Viscera Circuit
ordered: Gain the Organ Furnace system. When Initiative is rolled, choose an active Furnace before the first turn. You may suppress or reveal visible signs without using an action.
sections.summary: Gain the Organ Furnace system. When Initiative is rolled, choose an active Furnace before the first turn. You may suppress or reveal visible signs without using an action.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Five-Viscera Circuit
rules: - At the start of your first turn, choose again under the normal Organ Furnace procedure. A use spent before your turn does not prevent the Furnace's new-turn use after the turn begins.

- Becoming Unconscious does not destroy the cultivated organs, but active Furnace benefits become dormant while a rule prevents you from using Path features. When that state ends, resume the previous legal Furnace selection until the next start-of-turn choice.
sections.summary: - When Initiative is rolled, choose the Furnace active before your first turn. This choice applies during the interval before that turn and can use its once-per-turn benefit during another creature's turn if its trigger occurs.

sections.name: Fivefold Organ Harmony
ordered: All five Furnaces are active simultaneously, with separate once-per-turn limits.

Also gain Resistance to Acid and Poison, Immunity to ordinary disease, immunity to spoiled or ordinarily poisonous food, and add Constitution modifier to one healing roll from a potion, pill, medicine, medicinal food, or alchemical consumable.
Excess healing from such a consumable becomes Temporary Hit Points, to a maximum of twice your Proficiency Bonus.
rules: Also gain Resistance to Acid and Poison, Immunity to ordinary disease, immunity to spoiled or ordinarily poisonous food, and add Constitution modifier to one healing roll from a potion, pill, medicine, medicinal food, or alchemical consumable.
Excess healing from such a consumable becomes Temporary Hit Points, to a maximum of twice your Proficiency Bonus.
sections.summary: All five Furnaces are active simultaneously, with separate once-per-turn limits.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Fivefold Organ Harmony
rules: - Acid and Poison Resistance use ordinary damage ordering. Immunity to ordinary disease prevents new ordinary diseases and suppresses their active effects; artifact, divine, Secret, Tribulation, Foundation, Method, Immortal, or explicit equal- or higher-Source-CL disease authority can still contest it.

- Immunity to spoiled or ordinarily poisonous food prevents its harmful poison and contamination effects. It does not make nonfood substances edible, supply nutrition, negate curses, or neutralize an alchemical item before another creature consumes it.

- When you receive healing from one potion, pill, medicine, medicinal food, or alchemical consumable, add Constitution modifier to one healing roll made by that consumable. If it has several healing rolls, choose one after rolling but before applying healing.

- After all healing from that consumable is applied, calculate healing that exceeded missing Hit Points. Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to that excess, to a maximum of twice Proficiency Bonus. These Temporary Hit Points replace rather than stack with existing Temporary Hit Points unless another rule says otherwise.
- This benefit applies once per consumed item or dose and does not multiply healing from repeated ticks produced by the same dose.
sections.summary: - All five Furnaces are active simultaneously. Each retains one separate once-per-turn limit; a single Stamina activation can legally trigger both Liver and Kidney, and can also trigger Spleen only if Stamina Guard or a qualifying forced-movement save occurred.

items: Heart: Once per turn on a hit, additional 3d8 Fire, Radiant, or Force.
Lung: Ranged attacks against you have Disadvantage; no air required; immune to inhaled poison, smoke, gas, and suffocation.
Liver: Once per turn after spending Stamina, regain 2d8 + Constitution modifier Hit Points.
Kidney: Once per turn after spending Stamina, move 15 feet without provoking, across liquids and vertical surfaces; fall if unsupported afterward.
Spleen: Once per turn after Stamina Guard or a successful saving throw, gain Temporary Hit Points equal to twice Proficiency Bonus and reduce forced movement by 10 feet until your next turn.

sections.name: Inner Cosmos Furnace
rules: Refine the Impure costs 0 Stamina but remains a Bonus Action.
sections.summary: All Furnaces remain active and improve:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Inner Cosmos Furnace
rules: - Heart: Once per turn on a hit, choose Fire, Radiant, or Force and add 3d8 to that hit's packet.

- Lung: Every ranged attack roll against you has Disadvantage. You require no air and are immune to inhaled poison, smoke, gas, and suffocation. This does not grant sight through smoke, immunity to corrosive contact, or immunity to a noninhaled poison.
- Liver: Once per turn after a Stamina-spending activation resolves, regain 2d8 + Constitution modifier Hit Points if above 0. It replaces the normal Proficiency Bonus healing.

- Kidney: Once per turn after a Stamina-spending activation resolves, stand from Prone without movement and move up to 15 feet without provoking, across liquids and vertical surfaces. If unsupported at the end, fall immediately. It replaces the normal 5-foot movement.

- Spleen: Once per turn after Stamina Guard resolves or after any successful saving throw against a hostile effect, gain Temporary Hit Points equal to twice Proficiency Bonus and reduce hostile physical forced movement against you by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. The reduction applies to each qualifying physical movement packet during that duration, but not teleportation.

- Refine the Impure costs 0 Stamina during the state but remains a Bonus Action and otherwise follows its complete procedure. A 0-Stamina use does not trigger Liver or Kidney because no Stamina was spent.
- Becoming Unconscious ends Inner Cosmos Furnace under the general transformation rule. Ending it does not remove healing, movement, or Temporary Hit Points already resolved.
sections.summary: - Activate as a Bonus Action, spend 6 Stamina, and record the 1-minute once-per-scene state. All five Furnaces remain active and their CL18 versions replace their normal numerical effects for the duration; the normal and improved versions do not stack.

items: Poisoned: Repeat the original save with Advantage. Success ends it; failure suppresses it until the start of your next turn.
Disease: Make a Constitution save against its printed DC. Success suppresses active penalties for 24 hours. Three successes against the same disease end it; failures do not erase successes.
Ongoing Acid or Poison: Repeat its save with Advantage. Success ends it; failure reduces its next damage by 2d8 + Constitution modifier.
Contaminated Substance: End one temporary numerical penalty directly caused by consumed poison, spoiled medicine, contaminated food, or ordinary alchemical substance.

sections.name: Refine the Impure
rules: Cannot remove Exhaustion, Hidden Injuries, Foundation damage, Tribulation scars, curses, possession, permanent corruption, or an effect tagged Curse, Tribulation, Foundation Injury, or Permanent.
sections.summary: Choose one effect:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Refine the Impure
rules: - Poisoned: Use the original save and DC that imposed the Poisoned condition. If no save was printed, make a Constitution save against the source's Cultivation Save DC or its fallback Authority DC. Success ends that one Poisoned condition. Failure suppresses only that condition's effects until the start of your next turn; its duration continues.

- Disease: Make a Constitution save against the printed disease DC or fallback Authority DC. Record successes separately for each disease. A success suppresses that disease's active penalties for 24 hours and adds one success; three total successes end it. Failure adds no consequence and erases no successes. A new infection is a new record unless the disease says otherwise.

- Ongoing Acid or Poison: Repeat the save printed by one ongoing Acid- or Poison-damage effect. If none exists, make a Constitution save against its source DC. Success ends that effect. Failure reduces only its next damage packet by 2d8 + Constitution modifier, to a minimum of 0; after that packet the reduction expires.

- Contaminated Substance: End one temporary numerical penalty directly and solely caused by consumed poison, spoiled medicine, contaminated food, or an ordinary alchemical substance. This can end a penalty to AC, Speed, an ability check, attack roll, save, damage roll, or maximum Hit Points only when the source explicitly identifies that numerical penalty. It does not end damage, a condition, disease, curse, addiction, beneficial tradeoff, or the source item itself.
- The printed exclusions remain absolute. An effect carrying any excluded tag is not eligible merely because it also uses Poison or Disease language.
- Repeated use can attempt the same effect again on later turns. Stamina and the Bonus Action are spent whether the save succeeds or fails.
sections.summary: - Choose one effect currently affecting you, spend the Bonus Action and 2 Stamina, and resolve only its matching option. Refine the Impure is a bodily purification procedure, not general dispelling or exorcism.

sections.name: Twin Furnace Circulation
rules: Once per turn after spending Stamina, replace one active Furnace with another without using an action. The new Furnace applies immediately but does not retroactively affect events already resolved.
sections.summary: At the start of each turn, choose two different Organ Furnaces. Both remain active until the start of your next turn.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Twin Furnace Circulation
rules: - Once during the turn after a Stamina-spending activation resolves, replace exactly one active Furnace with one currently inactive Furnace without using an action. You can replace only one Furnace through this clause even if the activation spent several Stamina.

- The newly active Furnace can respond to a later qualifying event during that turn if its own once-per-turn benefit has not already been used. Re-selecting a Furnace whose benefit was used earlier that turn does not refresh it.

- Replacing a Furnace does not cancel a duration already created by it, such as Temporary Hit Points or movement already completed, and does not retroactively grant AC, Resistance, healing, or another result to an earlier event.
sections.summary: - Choose two different Furnaces at the start of each turn. Both are active simultaneously and track their once-per-turn uses separately.

items: You have Advantage on checks or rolls made to prevent its escape.
You move at full Speed while dragging a creature no more than one size larger than you.
The creature cannot benefit from movement granted by a willing ally unless that movement first ends your Grapple.

sections.name: Crushing Grip
sections.summary: At the start of your turn, you may spend 1 Stamina to crush one creature you are Grappling. It takes damage equal to one Iron Fist damage roll. This requires no attack roll, occurs once per turn, cannot trigger an attack-hit rider, and does not end the Grapple.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Crushing Grip
rules: - “Prevent its escape” includes checks, saves, and opposed Cultivation Checks made specifically to end or break your Grapple. It does not grant Advantage against teleportation, phasing, bodily transformation, or severance unless that procedure directly calls for a Grapple escape roll.

- A willing ally can still target the Grappled creature with granted movement. That movement resolves only if it first ends, transfers, or legally carries the Grapple under its own rule. The clause does not prohibit forced movement, unwilling teleportation, or movement that carries both you and the target together.

- The crush is one damage packet equal to one current Iron Fist damage roll, including the die but not an attack's ability modifier or hit-only riders unless a rule expressly adds them. It is not an attack, cannot critically hit, and cannot trigger “when you hit” or “when an attack deals damage” features.
sections.summary: - Choose the Grappled creature when the start of your turn is reached, before taking an action or moving. You must still be Grappling it when the damage resolves.

items: Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your CL.
Your reach increases by 5 feet.
Once per turn when you deal damage with a Body Refining melee attack, add your Constitution modifier to one damage roll.
Increase every push caused by one of your Body Refining features by 5 feet.
You count as one additional size larger for Grappling and Shoving.

sections.name: Mountain-Demon Might
rules: When Mountain-Demon Might ends, Titan's Frame also ends.
sections.summary: Activate Titan's Frame without paying its normal cost. If Titan's Frame is already active, increase your size by one additional category, to a maximum of Huge.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Mountain-Demon Might
rules: - Temporary Hit Points from this feature follow the normal nonstacking rule. Reapplication replaces them only if the new amount is higher.

- The once-per-turn Constitution damage applies to one damage roll from one Body Refining melee attack after that attack hits. It is not added to Grapple damage, Crushing Grip, a collision, or an area effect unless that effect is itself a Body Refining melee attack.

- “Every push caused by one of your Body Refining features” increases only a printed push distance. It does not create a push where none exists and does not increase a pull, teleport, throw arc, or self-movement.
- If Mountain-Demon Might ends because it is dispelled, suppressed, or its duration expires, Titan's Frame ends at the same time even if Titan's Frame would otherwise have remaining duration.
sections.summary: - Activating this feature activates or refreshes Titan's Frame as part of the same Bonus Action. It ignores Titan's Frame's 2-Stamina cost but not legal-space requirements.

items: Gain Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
Count as one size larger for Grappling, Shoving, carrying, dragging, lifting, and pushing.
Double your carrying, dragging, lifting, and pushing capacity.
Your Iron Fist damage die becomes 1d10.
Your reach does not increase unless another feature states otherwise.
Push the target 5 feet.
Move 5 feet toward the target without provoking Opportunity Attacks from it.
Gain Advantage on your next attempt to Grapple or Shove that target before the end of the turn.
groups.lead: Once during each of your turns after you hit with a Body Refining melee attack, choose one:

sections.name: Titan's Frame
rules: Activating Titan's Frame again refreshes its duration but does not increase your size further.
sections.summary: Increase your size by one category, to a maximum of Large.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Titan's Frame
rules: - Legal space. You can activate the feature only if the new size can occupy your current space. If the available space permits Large but not a later Huge increase, you grow only to the largest legal printed size. A space that becomes too small after you enter it does not crush you; you are Squeezing under the normal rules until you leave or the transformation ends.

- Existing size effects. Determine your actual size after all replacement effects, then apply each distinct “count as larger” permission only to the listed operations. Titan's Frame does not stack with itself. A later activation refreshes the duration and may select a different legal size at CL14.

- Once-turn rider. The rider triggers after the hit resolves. The movement toward the target must end closer to it and in a legal space. The Advantage option expires at the end of the same turn and applies to only the next Grapple or Shove attempt against that target.

- Ending the form. When the form ends, return to your normal recorded size in your current space. If that space is illegal for the returning size, use Failed Spatial Movement to place you in the nearest legal space; no damage occurs unless another rule prints it.
sections.summary: - Transformation record. Titan's Frame is a temporary size transformation. It changes occupied space, size-dependent reach only where printed, carrying capacity, and equipment fit under Body Refining Shared Procedures. It does not create extra limbs, attacks, Hit Dice, or inherent weapon reach.

items: It may increase you directly to Large or Huge.
Your Iron Fist damage die becomes 1d12.
Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your CL when you activate it.
Your carrying, dragging, lifting, and pushing capacity is quadrupled rather than doubled.
You may Grapple creatures up to two sizes larger than you.
Gain Advantage on saving throws against being pushed, pulled, or knocked Prone.
Your Iron Fist damage becomes 2d8 before modifiers.
You may become Huge even if you began Small.
A creature no more than one size larger than you does not gain size-based protection against your Grapples, Shoves, or forced movement.

sections.name: Titanic Frame
sections.summary: Titan's Frame gains the following improvements:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Titanic Frame
rules: - “Count as one additional size larger” from Mountain-Demon Might is a functional permission for Grappling and Shoving only. It does not enlarge occupied space, reach, natural weapon damage, or carrying capacity beyond the values already printed.

- If another rule changes Iron Fist to a larger damage expression, use the largest applicable replacement unless a rule expressly says the expressions stack. The 2d8 Mountain-Demon expression is a replacement, not 1d12 + 2d8.
- The Temporary Hit Points granted by ordinary Titan's Frame and Mountain-Demon Might are separate grants but still follow the normal nonstacking Temporary Hit Point rule.
sections.summary: - When activating Titan's Frame, choose Large or Huge, subject to legal space. The choice is a direct replacement; you do not need to pass through an intermediate size or pay more Stamina.

lossy: allowlist: results not directly after their save/attack
sections.name: World-Shaking Stomp
outcomes: A creature takes 10d6 Bludgeoning, Force, or Thunder damage, falls Prone, and is pushed 10 feet away from you. On a successful save, it takes half damage, remains standing, and is pushed 5 feet.
rules: The ground in the cone becomes difficult terrain until cleared or repaired. Unattended objects, temporary barriers, vehicles, structures, terrain sections, and Formation Anchors take double damage.
If you are Huge when you activate this feature, its cone becomes 40 feet.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — World-Shaking Stomp
rules: - The cone originates from your space and requires line of effect. It affects creatures and eligible objects in the area once each.

- Forced movement is directly away from you along the shortest legal route. A creature that cannot move the full distance moves as far as legally possible. No collision damage occurs unless another rule expressly creates it.

- The difficult terrain applies only to ordinary ground, floors, or structural surfaces physically struck by the effect. It does not alter open air, incorporeal terrain, an artifact surface, or a higher-authority area unless the governing rule permits it.

- “Double damage” is applied once to the listed unattended targets after Resistance, Immunity, Damage Threshold, and other modifiers in the universal damage procedure. A Formation Anchor that is also a structure is not doubled twice.
sections.summary: - Choose Bludgeoning, Force, or Thunder when you activate the feature; all damage from that activation uses the chosen type.

items: Standard Guard: 1d10 per Stamina.
Gilded Guard: 2d8 per Stamina.
You take no falling damage from falls of 60 feet or less.
Gain Advantage against effects that crush, fracture, or break your bones.

sections.name: Gilded Bones
rules: Once per round, if damage remains after using Gilded Guard, gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus after the damage resolves.
sections.summary: When using Stamina Guard, choose one die type for all dice spent against that damage packet:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Gilded Bones
rules: - Gilded Guard replaces 1d10 per Stamina with 2d8 per Stamina; it does not roll both. All other Stamina Guard timing, maximum spend, Reaction cost, and damage ordering remain.

- After the complete triggering damage packet resolves, if at least 1 damage reduced your Hit Points and you have not gained these Temporary Hit Points this round, gain Temporary Hit Points equal to Proficiency Bonus. They do not reduce the triggering packet retroactively and follow ordinary nonstacking rules.
- Falls of 60 feet or less deal no falling damage. A fall longer than 60 feet uses the normal full falling-damage procedure; this feature does not subtract 60 feet from it.
- Bone-protection Advantage applies to checks and saves resisting crushing, fracturing, or bone-breaking. It does not prevent a higher-authority explicit Injury without a save.
sections.summary: - When activating Stamina Guard against one damage packet, choose Standard Guard or Gilded Guard before rolling any reduction dice. Every Stamina die spent for that activation uses the chosen expression.

sections.name: Golden Aura
rules: A hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura makes a Wisdom saving throw.
- Failed Save: Choose Disadvantage on its next attack, inability to benefit from Invisible, or no Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Successful Save: It cannot benefit from Invisible until the start of its next turn.
sections.summary: For the duration, you and allies of your choice in the aura gain Advantage on saving throws against Frightened, Resistance to Necrotic damage, and Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus the first time they enter the aura or start a turn there during the activation.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Golden Aura
rules: - Each chosen ally gains the Temporary Hit Points only once per activation: the first time it enters the aura or starts a turn there. Leaving and re-entering does not grant them again during the same activation.
- Advantage against Frightened and Necrotic Resistance apply while the chosen ally is in the aura. They end immediately upon leaving, though already gained Temporary Hit Points remain.

- Each hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura makes one Wisdom save. Choose its failed-save result after it fails. The “next attack” Disadvantage is expended whether the attack hits or misses. Named effects from this aura refresh rather than stack.
- Invisible denial removes the condition's benefits for the printed duration. It does not automatically expose a creature behind cover or identify an illusion not based on Invisible.
- If the aura is suppressed, its duration and scene use continue; it grants no benefits while dormant.
sections.summary: - The aura moves with you and extends 10 feet from your current space. You choose whether each ally is included whenever that ally would receive a benefit; no action is required.

items: Gain +1 AC.
Gain Advantage on saving throws against disease, Poisoned, corrosion, bodily decay, and physical deformation.
You may use Constitution instead of Charisma for Intimidation checks while your golden transformation is visible.

sections.name: Golden Sheen
sections.summary: You may reveal or suppress the visible golden sheen without using an action.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Golden Sheen
rules: - Advantage applies to checks or saves directly resisting disease, Poisoned, corrosion, bodily decay, or physical deformation. It does not grant immunity or a new save where none exists.
- Using Constitution for Intimidation requires the golden transformation to be perceptible to the target. This changes only the ability modifier; proficiency and other modifiers remain.

- Revealing or suppressing the sheen requires no action and can be done whenever you could communicate or change a cosmetic stance. Suppressing visibility does not suppress the feature's mechanical defenses.
sections.summary: - The +1 AC applies only while using Unarmored Defense and is an AC bonus, not a second base calculation.

facts: You would be reduced to 0 Hit Points but are not killed outright.

items: You are Incapacitated.
Your Speed is 0.
You cannot take actions or Reactions.
Gain Resistance to all damage.
Gain Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage.
You remain aware of your surroundings.
An effect whose Source CL is lower than yours cannot move you.
Regain Hit Points equal to 5 x Proficiency Bonus.
End the statue transformation.
Activate Golden Aura without paying its cost or expending its use.
Take your turn normally.
groups.lead: At the start of your next turn:

sections.name: Immortal Gold
rules: An equal- or higher-CL effect may move the statue by winning an opposed Cultivation Check.
Only one feature that prevents or replaces the same reduction to 0 Hit Points may resolve.
sections.summary: You are reduced to 1 Hit Point instead and become a golden statue until the start of your next turn.

items: Deal additional Radiant damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Cause the target to shed Dim Light in a 10-foot radius until the start of your next turn.
Prevent the target from benefiting from Invisible until the start of your next turn.
Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
groups.lead: Once per turn when you hit with an unarmed strike, choose one:

sections.name: Radiant Fist
rules: Against Undead, Fiends, creatures with the Daemonic tag, or active daemonic corruption, the additional Radiant damage becomes twice your Proficiency Bonus.
sections.summary: Your unarmed strikes may deal Radiant damage.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Radiant Fist
rules: - Once per turn after an unarmed hit, choose exactly one rider. The additional damage is Radiant. The light is centered on the target and moves with it. Invisible denial suppresses the benefits of the Invisible condition but does not reveal a hidden target's exact location through total cover or another concealment. Temporary Hit Points follow ordinary nonstacking rules.

- If the target is Undead, Fiend, has the Daemonic tag, or bears an active daemonic corruption, only the additional Radiant-damage rider increases from Proficiency Bonus to twice Proficiency Bonus. The other three options are unchanged.
- A target meeting several qualifying categories receives the doubled value only once.
sections.summary: - Choose the damage type of each unarmed strike when making it. Radiant replaces, rather than adds to, its ordinary damage type.

items: Reduce the first instance of that damage each round by Proficiency Bonus.
You know when an effect about to damage you includes that type.

lossy: allowlist: header fact inside the body
sections.name: Flesh Remembers Pain
rules: At CL3, maintain one; a new one replaces it.
Gain Resistance to that type against the triggering packet.
sections.summary: Once per round after qualifying hostile damage, choose one valid type in the packet. Gain a Damage Adaptation until scene end.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Flesh Remembers Pain
rules: - At CL3, if another Damage Adaptation is already maintained, choose whether the new record replaces it. Declining the new record is legal.

- The first instance reduction applies to the first packet each round that would apply at least 1 damage of that type after percentage modifiers. Reduce that type's portion by Proficiency Bonus at the shared flat-reduction step, to a minimum of 0. It is then spent for the round even if the portion becomes 0.

- The Reaction is declared when an adapted damage packet is about to be applied, after the packet and type are known but before Resistance and Hit Point loss are finalized. Spend 1 Stamina and gain Resistance to that type for the triggering packet only.

- The Reaction and the Adaptation's flat reduction can apply to the same packet: apply Resistance first under normal damage ordering, then the flat reduction. Immunity or a canceled packet does not require or consume the Reaction.
- The once-per-round acquisition limit, first-instance reduction, and Reaction limit are separate records.
sections.summary: - After one qualifying hostile damage event resolves and applies at least 1 damage of a valid type to your Hit Points, choose one valid type present and gain its Adaptation. This acquisition can occur once per round.

items: Add Proficiency Bonus to saves made to end it.
If no save is normally allowed during your turn, spend 2 Stamina at the end of your turn to repeat the original save against the original DC, once per round.
groups.lead: While affected by the adapted condition:

sections.name: Meridians Remember Affliction
sections.summary: Once per round after failing a save and becoming Blinded, Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, Restrained, or Stunned, record it as your Affliction Adaptation until scene end. Maintain one.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Meridians Remember Affliction
rules: - Acquisition occurs once per round. At the current one-record limit, a new record can replace the existing one or be declined.

- Add Proficiency Bonus to every save made specifically to end the adapted condition, including repeat saves printed by its source. This bonus does not apply to the initial save that created the Adaptation.

- When the condition normally grants no save during your turn, at the end of your turn you may spend 2 Stamina to repeat the original save using the original ability and DC. This can occur once per round.

- A successful repeat ends only the adapted condition and failure-only ongoing functions directly dependent on it. It does not reverse damage, movement, consumed resources, a completed transformation, or another condition unless its Source Rule links them.
- If the original source no longer exists, use its recorded DC. If no valid original DC was recorded, use the fallback Authority DC for its Realm.
sections.summary: - Gain an Affliction Adaptation only after failing a hostile save and actually becoming one of the listed conditions. Several eligible conditions from one failed save create one chosen Adaptation.

facts: You take a valid unadapted damage type or fail a save imposing an eligible condition.
sections.name: Perfect Counter-Evolution
rules: - Affliction Response: Gain the Affliction Adaptation and reroll the failed save, using the new result.
Return the Lesson deals 4d8 Force instead of 2d8.
You still cannot adapt to Void, untyped damage, maximum-Hit-Point loss, aging, Realm Suppression, CL reduction, permanent identity rewriting, or an effect explicitly barring adaptation.
sections.summary: - Damage Response: Gain the Adaptation before damage is finalized and apply its benefits to the triggering packet.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Perfect Counter-Evolution
rules: - Create the Adaptation immediately, replacing an existing record if capacity requires. Apply its CL14 benefit to the triggering packet: automatic Resistance for listed ordinary types, or twice-Proficiency-Bonus reduction for Force or Psychic.

- Perfect Counter-Evolution itself does not also activate the 1-Stamina Flesh Remembers Pain Reaction; one Reaction cannot pay both features. Force and Psychic therefore receive their printed flat reduction, not packet Resistance, from this response.

- Declare the Affliction Response after failing a save that would impose an eligible condition but before applying that condition. Spend 2 Stamina, create the Adaptation, and reroll the same save against the same DC. Use the new result.
- On success, do not apply conditions or riders imposed only on failure. On failure, resolve the failure and retain the new Affliction Adaptation for later ending saves.
- Return the Lesson's damage becomes 4d8; this replaces 2d8.
- The printed prohibited categories remain absolute. A broad “adapt to anything” interpretation cannot override them or a higher-authority Source Rule that expressly bars adaptation.
sections.summary: - Declare the Damage Response after an unadapted valid damage type in a hostile packet is identified but before damage is finalized. Spend 2 Stamina and choose one valid type in that packet.

facts: You hit a creature that dealt your adapted damage type to you or imposed your adapted condition during the current scene.

items: Push 10 feet.
No Reactions until the start of its next turn.
Speed 0 until the start of its next turn.
Disadvantage on its next save against one of your Body Refining features before the end of your next turn.
Move 10 feet without provoking.

sections.name: Return the Lesson
sections.summary: Deal an additional 2d8 Force damage and choose one:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Return the Lesson
rules: - Declare after hitting a qualifying creature. Spend 1 Stamina, add 2d8 Force to that hit, and choose one printed result. This can occur once per turn.
- Push is directly away from you and follows forced-movement rules. Reaction denial begins after the hit and lasts until the start of the target's next turn. Speed 0 uses the same duration.

- For the save penalty, name one Body Refining feature you possess when applying the rider. The target has Disadvantage on its next save against that named feature before the end of your next turn; the rider expires after that save or at the stated time.
- The movement option moves you up to 10 feet without provoking after the hit resolves. It is physical movement along a legal route.
- Environmental hazards, unattended objects, and effects without a source creature can create Adaptations but cannot be targets of Return the Lesson unless they are represented by a legal creature.
sections.summary: - Every Adaptation records the creature that dealt the adapted damage or imposed the adapted condition. A creature qualifies if it appears in at least one maintained record from the current scene.

sections.name: Ten Thousand Answers
ordered: Maintain three Damage Adaptations and two Affliction Adaptations.
Gain automatic Resistance to adapted Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Piercing, Poison, Radiant, Slashing, and Thunder damage.
Force and Psychic Adaptations instead reduce the first instance each round by twice Proficiency Bonus. Flesh Remembers Pain may still grant Resistance to Force or Psychic against one packet.
rules: Gain automatic Resistance to adapted Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Piercing, Poison, Radiant, Slashing, and Thunder damage.
Force and Psychic Adaptations instead reduce the first instance each round by twice Proficiency Bonus. Flesh Remembers Pain may still grant Resistance to Force or Psychic against one packet.
sections.summary: Maintain three Damage Adaptations and two Affliction Adaptations.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Ten Thousand Answers
rules: - For Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Piercing, Poison, Radiant, Slashing, and Thunder, the maintained Adaptation grants Resistance continuously until scene end.
- For Force and Psychic, replace the CL3 first-instance reduction with twice Proficiency Bonus. Do not add both the Proficiency Bonus and twice-Proficiency-Bonus reductions.

- Flesh Remembers Pain's Reaction remains legal against Force or Psychic and can grant packet-only Resistance before the twice-Proficiency-Bonus reduction. It is redundant for types already receiving automatic Resistance but can still be declared if another rule would temporarily remove that Resistance.
- Several maintained Adaptations do not combine against one type or create double Resistance.
sections.summary: - Increase maintained capacities to three different Damage Adaptations and two different Affliction Adaptations. When a new record exceeds capacity, choose one record of the same category to replace or decline the new record.

items: Use Constitution instead of Strength or Dexterity for attack and damage rolls.
You may use your Cultivation Attack Modifier.
It is integrated into Body Refining.
Reach increases by 5 feet during your turn.
Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply.

sections.name: Chain-Body Integration
rules: This does not grant the Chains Sphere.
sections.summary: Gain proficiency with Chain Weapons.

facts: You hit with a Chain Weapon or unarmed strike.

items: It cannot willingly move more than 20 feet from you.
It cannot benefit from willing allied movement that carries it beyond 20 feet.
Teleportation beyond 20 feet requires a Cultivation Check against your DC; failure uses Failed Spatial Movement.
You know its direction within 60 feet.

lossy: allowlist: results not directly after their save/attack
sections.name: Meridian Tether
outcomes: The target becomes Tethered until the end of your next turn.
rules: A Tether ends if you become Unconscious, willingly end it, the target ends its turn more than 30 feet away because of hostile forced movement, or an effect severs cultivation bindings.
At CL3, maintain one Tether; a new one replaces it.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Chain Integration and Meridian Tethers
rules: - The 5-foot reach increase applies only during your turn. At CL14 the two turn-only increases combine for +10 feet during your turn; they do not enlarge threatened space outside your turn.

- Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply only through their printed integrated-weapon interface. If several rules replace the same weapon damage die, use the highest legal replacement rather than adding several base weapon dice.

- Declare Meridian Tether after the triggering hit resolves, spend 1 Stamina, select one creature hit, and have it make one Strength save. A Tether is a cultivation restraint, not Grappled or Restrained, and it does not by itself prevent attacks, actions, forced movement, falling, or movement toward you.

- Record the Tether's source, target, Source CL, maximum distance, direction-sense range, duration, and removal conditions. At CL3 you can maintain one Meridian Tether; creating another immediately ends the previous one after the new target fails its save.

- A Tethered creature can willingly move within the 20-foot boundary and can move closer to you. It cannot use its own willing movement, or accept willing allied movement, to end farther than 20 feet from you. Hostile forced movement can carry it beyond that boundary.

- A willing teleport or other spatial movement that would end farther than 20 feet requires one Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC before movement occurs. On failure use Failed Spatial Movement; on success the movement resolves normally unless another feature intervenes.

- Direction sense functions only while the target is within 60 feet and on the same plane. It gives direction, not exact distance, condition, identity through disguise, line of sight, or permission to target through total cover.

- The Tether ends at its printed duration, when you become Unconscious, when you willingly end it without an action, when a legal effect severs cultivation bindings, or when the target ends its turn more than 30 feet from you after hostile forced movement. Being momentarily farther than 30 feet before that end-of-turn check does not end it.
sections.summary: - Record each qualifying Chain Weapon by weapon group. While wielding it, Constitution replaces Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls, and you may use your Cultivation Attack Modifier for its attack rolls. Integration grants no Sphere, talent, extra Chain Weapon, or independent chain manifestation.

lossy: allowlist: results not directly after their save/attack
sections.name: Drag the Heavens
outcomes: Pull it 20 feet, move yourself 20 feet toward it without provoking, pull it 10 feet and knock it Prone, or rotate it to another unoccupied space within 20 feet.
Pull it 5 feet or move yourself 5 feet toward it.
rules: A creature more than two sizes larger has Advantage.
If it collides with a surface or creature, both take Bludgeoning damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus; a second creature avoids this damage on a successful Dexterity save.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Drag the Heavens
rules: - On a failed save, choose exactly one printed result. On a success, choose one of the two printed 5-foot results. Self-movement and target movement are part of this activation and do not create another movement trigger from Drag the Heavens.

- A pull moves the target directly toward you along the shortest legal route. Self-movement moves you directly toward the target, does not provoke Opportunity Attacks, and must end in a legal space. The 10-foot pull-and-Prone result applies Prone after movement ends.

- The rotation result moves the target through a curved or straight legal route no longer than 20 feet to an unoccupied space within 20 feet of you. It cannot pass through total cover or a sealed barrier and cannot end beyond the Meridian Tether boundary.

- Forced movement stops at the nearest legal space before an obstruction. If the moving target first collides with a damageable surface or one creature because no legal continuation exists, resolve one collision only. The moved target takes Bludgeoning damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A damageable surface takes the same damage; a second creature makes one Dexterity save, taking the same damage on failure and none on success.

- Collision damage is one packet per affected creature, does not repeat for several occupied squares or chained contacts, and does not create an Injury, Grapple, or additional forced movement unless another Source Rule says so.
- A successful-save 5-foot pull or self-movement uses the same route and legal-space rules. If no legal movement is possible, that movement becomes 0; the Stamina and Bonus Action remain spent.
sections.summary: - Select one creature currently Tethered to you, spend the Bonus Action and 1 Stamina, then resolve one Strength save. A creature at least three size categories larger than you has Advantage; functional size expressly applicable to Grappling or forced movement counts.

facts: A creature within 30 feet is hit by a ranged attack or would be moved at least 10 feet against its will.

items: Catch the Attack: Reduce ranged attack damage by 3d10 + Constitution modifier. If reduced to 0, move the protected creature 10 feet toward you without provoking.
Anchor the Body: Reduce forced movement by 20 feet. If reduced to 0, prevent Prone from the same effect and move it 5 feet toward you.

sections.name: Guardian Chain
rules: Guardian Chain cannot prevent teleportation unless the creature is Tethered.
sections.summary: Choose one:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Guardian Chain
rules: - Catch the Attack: Reduce the triggering attack's total damage packet by 3d10 + Constitution modifier at the shared damage-reduction step. This protects only the chosen hit creature and does not reduce later attacks or separate damage packets from the same activation. If final damage applied becomes 0, move that creature up to 10 feet directly toward you along a legal route without provoking Opportunity Attacks. This is granted movement created by you and does not require willingness.

- Anchor the Body: Reduce the triggering physical forced-movement distance by 20 feet after the source determines distance. If final distance becomes 0, also prevent Prone caused by that same movement effect and move the protected creature up to 5 feet toward you without provoking. Prevented movement creates no collision unless the source expressly creates one without movement.

- Guardian Chain does not reduce ordinary teleport distance. If the protected creature is Tethered and the trigger is willing or hostile spatial movement, you may use Anchor the Body; replace the 20-foot reduction with one Cultivation Check by the spatial effect's activator against your Cultivation Save DC. On failure, use Failed Spatial Movement; on success, the spatial movement resolves normally. Do not roll both this check and the Meridian Tether check for the same spatial activation; Guardian Chain uses this Reaction-based check instead.
