sections.summary: Make one unarmed strike.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Isshun Sengeki
rules: - On a hit, the 10d10 is additional attack damage and follows normal critical-hit rules unless another rule changes them. Choose and resolve the Constitution save after all hit damage is determined.

- “Ordinary Resistance to Force” means non-absolute Resistance from a creature statistic, temporary effect, armor, item, or technique. Immunity, a permanent artifact defense, and a rule explicitly immune to physical or Force authority remain.

- When the damage packet is resolved, choose one temporary damage-reduction effect applying to that packet whose Source CL is no higher than yours. It is ignored for this strike. Its action, Reaction, resource, or limited-use cost remains spent unless its rule says otherwise.

- A lower-Source-CL Reaction cannot redirect the strike. It can still perform a different legal function, such as reducing damage, if not otherwise ignored. Equal- or higher-Source-CL redirection resolves normally.
- Double damage to listed unattended targets applies once. A target belonging to several listed categories is not doubled repeatedly.
- The failed-save options are temporary combat impairments, not injuries. The push uses forced-movement rules. The successful-save Reaction denial is the only save result on success.
sections.summary: - The Action makes exactly one unarmed strike. Pay the Stamina and expend the scene use when the Action is declared; a miss still spends both.

items: You cannot be Surprised.
Gain Advantage on Initiative.
Gain Advantage on your first attack roll during the first round of a scene.
Gain Advantage on saving throws against effects that directly predict, compel, or overwrite your immediate bodily movement.

sections.name: Mushin
sections.summary: When Initiative is rolled at the start of a new scene, regain 2 Stamina. This restoration occurs once per scene and cannot raise you above your maximum.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Mushin
rules: - Initiative Advantage and first-round attack Advantage are separate. The first-round benefit applies to your first attack roll of that round, regardless of action type, and is expended on the roll.

- The movement-defense Advantage applies only to a save whose direct purpose is to predict, compel, script, possess, or overwrite your immediate bodily movement. It does not apply merely because an area effect or ordinary forced movement would move you.

- Regain 2 Stamina when Initiative is first rolled for a new scene. Re-rolling Initiative, joining an ongoing scene, a summoned creature rolling separately, or splitting the same conflict into phases does not restore it again.
- The restoration is not a rest and cannot exceed maximum Stamina.
sections.summary: - Use the campaign's canonical Surprise procedure. “Cannot be Surprised” prevents the Surprised state; it does not reveal hidden creatures or prevent an ambush from beginning a scene.

items: Move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Push the target 5 feet.
Gain +1 AC against the target until the start of your next turn.

lossy: allowlist: result followed by a list
allowlist: results not directly after their save/attack
sections.name: Perfect Breath
rules: - Deal additional damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
sections.summary: After you use Stomping Step, the first unarmed attack you make before the end of the turn ignores one source of Disadvantage affecting its attack roll. Other sources of Disadvantage still apply normally.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Perfect Breath
rules: - Ignoring one source of Disadvantage removes one identified cause before Advantage and Disadvantage are combined. Other causes remain. This does not create Advantage by itself.
- The Proficiency Bonus damage and chosen rider apply only if that first unarmed attack hits, and together constitute one once-per-turn use of Perfect Breath.

- The 5-foot movement occurs after the hit resolves, uses no action, must end in a legal space, and does not provoke. The push is directly away and creates no collision damage. The +1 AC applies only against the hit target and does not stack with itself.
sections.summary: - The first unarmed attack you make after using Stomping Step must occur before the end of the same turn. If it misses or is never made, the benefit expires.

facts: You hit with an unarmed strike.
lossy: allowlist: results not directly after their save/attack
sections.name: Precision Strike
outcomes: The target cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn regardless of the selected area.
rules: - Arm: On a failed save, Disadvantage on the target's next weapon attack before the start of your next turn.
- Leg: On a failed save, reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
- Breath: On a failed save, it cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn.
- Balance: On a failed save, it has Disadvantage on its next Strength or Dexterity saving throw before the start of your next turn.
sections.summary: Choose a target area before the saving throw.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Precision Strike
rules: - A creature does not become ineligible merely because its body plan lacks a human arm, leg, lungs, or ordinary balance organ. Apply the selected printed mechanical effect through the closest equivalent bodily function unless the creature has an explicit Source Rule making it immune to that exact form of physical interference.

- Arm affects only the next weapon attack and is expended whether that attack hits or misses. Leg is a fixed 10-foot Speed reduction and cannot reduce a Speed below 0. Breath prevents Reactions. Balance affects only the next Strength or Dexterity saving throw.
- On a successful save, the Reaction denial replaces the failed-save result; it does not add the selected failed-save result.
- Multiple Precision Strikes from you do not stack the same named effect. Reapplication refreshes its duration or next-roll expenditure.
sections.summary: - Choose Arm, Leg, Breath, or Balance after the triggering hit but before the save. The labels identify a temporary combat impairment; they do not create an injury, severance, disabled organ, Hidden Injury, or permanent anatomical change.

items: Use Dexterity or Constitution for its attack and damage rolls.
If using Constitution, use your Cultivation Attack Modifier.
It is integrated into your Body Refining cultivation.
Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply to it.
Deal additional Slashing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Reduce the target's Speed by 5 feet until the start of your next turn.
Prevent it from taking Reactions until the start of its next turn.
Draw or stow one Blade weapon.
groups.lead: Once per turn when you hit with an unarmed strike or integrated Blade weapon, choose one:

sections.name: Blade Fist
sections.summary: Your unarmed strikes may deal Slashing damage and gain the Finesse property. You may use Dexterity instead of Strength or Constitution for Iron Fist attack and damage rolls.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Blade Fist
rules: - Granting Finesse to your unarmed strikes permits Strength or Dexterity under the weapon-property rule; this feature additionally permits Constitution through Iron Fist. Choose one ability for each attack and add it once.

- While wielding an integrated Blade, choose Dexterity or Constitution for each attack. Choosing Constitution uses the Cultivation Attack Modifier. The weapon retains its normal item statistics and tags.
- Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply their cultivation-powered and high-authority weapon benefits to the integrated Blade; they do not add a second Iron Fist damage die.

- The once-per-turn rider is chosen after a hit. The additional Proficiency Bonus damage is one packet of Slashing damage. The Speed reduction does not stack with itself. Reaction denial lasts as printed. Drawing or stowing one Blade is part of the hit rider and does not create another object interaction.
- An unarmed strike dealing Slashing damage remains an unarmed strike and natural bodily attack; it does not become a held Blade weapon for a feature requiring one.
sections.summary: - A Blade is a dagger, sword, saber, cutting-edged axe, or weapon carrying the Blade tag. Record each integrated Blade weapon.

items: Gain +1 AC.
Your unarmed strikes and integrated Blade attacks may deal Force or Slashing damage.
Once per turn after hitting, move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
When a creature within your reach misses you with a melee attack, use your Reaction to make one unarmed or integrated Blade attack against it.

sections.name: Flowing Blade Stance
rules: The reaction attack follows the Granted Attack rule.
sections.summary: For the duration:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Flowing Blade Stance
rules: - Choosing Force or Slashing is made separately for each eligible attack. This changes that attack's damage type; it does not add damage.
- The once-per-turn 5-foot movement occurs after the hit is fully resolved, requires no action, must end legally, and does not provoke.

- The Reaction attack is declared after a melee attack within your reach misses you. You must still have the attacker within your current reach and be capable of making the chosen unarmed or integrated Blade attack. It is one granted attack and cannot grant another.
- The stance ends under the universal transformation/state rules only as printed; being Disarmed does not end it, though Blade-specific attacks require an available Blade.
sections.summary: - The +1 AC is a bonus, requires no particular weapon, and does not stack with another instance of this stance.

facts: You hit with an unarmed strike or integrated Blade attack.

items: Arm: On a failed save, Disadvantage on all weapon attacks until the end of your next turn.
Leg: On a failed save, Speed is halved until the end of your next turn.
Breath: On a failed save, no Reactions until the end of your next turn.
Flow: On a failed save, Disadvantage on Concentration saving throws and Cultivation Checks made to maintain techniques until the end of your next turn.
Guard: On a failed save, AC is reduced by 2 until the start of your next turn.

lossy: allowlist: results not directly after their save/attack
sections.name: Severing Palm
outcomes: The chosen effect lasts until the start of your next turn. Guard instead reduces AC by 1.
rules: A target cannot suffer multiple instances of the same Severing Palm effect. Reapplication refreshes its duration.
sections.summary: Choose one severing effect:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Severing Palm
rules: - Choose Arm, Leg, Breath, Flow, or Guard after the triggering hit but before the save. Apply the printed result even to a nonhumanoid body through the nearest equivalent function unless an explicit Source Rule grants immunity to that exact impairment.
- Distinct named effects can coexist. The same named effect from you does not stack; reapplication refreshes its duration and uses the new save result.

- Arm affects all weapon attacks for the failed-save duration. Leg halves each applicable Speed after fixed bonuses and before a minimum of 0. Breath prevents Reactions. Flow affects only Concentration saves and Cultivation Checks made to maintain existing techniques. Guard modifies final AC as a penalty and cannot reduce AC below 0.
- On a successful save, the chosen effect still lasts until the start of your next turn, with Guard reduced to -1 AC as printed.
- Ending or repairing an actual bodily Injury does not remove Severing Palm early unless a Source Rule expressly ends temporary technique impairments.
sections.summary: - The term “severing” describes temporary disruption of bodily combat lines. This feature does not sever anatomy, create an Injury, damage a Foundation, or permanently block a meridian.

items: Move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Draw or manifest a Blade weapon and make one unarmed or integrated Blade attack against a creature within reach.
Gain +2 AC until the start of your first turn.
Gain Advantage on your first attack roll during the first round.

sections.name: Sword Draws Before Thought
rules: This feature functions once per scene. The granted attack follows the Granted Attack rule.
sections.summary: When Initiative is rolled at the start of a scene and you are not Surprised, choose one:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Sword Draws Before Thought
rules: - Choose exactly one option. The movement is granted movement, requires a legal route, and does not provoke. It occurs before the first creature's turn.

- To draw a Blade, it must be carried or otherwise legally accessible. To manifest one, choose an integrated Blade recorded to you; the same weapon or bodily expression appears in your free hand and is not duplicated. If it was elsewhere, it is unavailable there until the manifestation ends or you release it under its Source Rule.

- The granted attack occurs immediately after drawing or manifesting, requires a legal target within reach at that moment, and follows the Granted Attack rule. If no target is legal, no attack is made and you do not choose another option.
- The +2 AC ends at the start of your first turn. The attack-roll Advantage applies to your first attack roll in the first round and is expended whether it hits or misses.
- Re-rolling Initiative or entering an ongoing scene does not reactivate the feature.
sections.summary: - Resolve when Initiative is first rolled for a new scene. If you are Surprised at that instant, the feature does not activate later in the same scene.

items: Gain a Fly Speed of 40 feet and Hover.
Gain +2 AC.
Your unarmed strikes and integrated Blade attacks may deal Force or Slashing damage.
Your critical-hit range becomes 19-20.
Once per turn when you hit, deal an additional 3d8 Force or Slashing damage.
Your melee reach increases by 5 feet.
Move through hostile creature spaces as difficult terrain.
Opportunity Attacks against you have Disadvantage.

sections.name: Sword Saint Incarnation
rules: The first time during a turn that a hostile creature enters your reach or starts its turn there, it makes a Dexterity saving throw.
- Failed Save: It takes 3d8 Force or Slashing damage and either cannot take Reactions or has its Speed reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn.
- Successful Save: It takes half damage and its Speed is reduced by 5 feet until the start of its next turn.
sections.summary: For the duration:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Sword Saint Incarnation
rules: - Hover prevents falling when your Fly Speed becomes 0, but a feature that removes flight or suppresses the transformation uses normal falling and Failed Spatial Movement rules.

- The critical range of 19–20 applies only to attack rolls made by you with unarmed strikes or integrated Blade attacks unless another rule expressly broadens it. It does not stack with another expanded critical range; use the broadest range.
- The 3d8 additional damage applies once per turn to one eligible hit. Choose Force or Slashing when dealt.

- Moving through a hostile creature's space treats each such space as difficult terrain. You cannot end movement there and gain no protection from that creature's reactions beyond the printed Disadvantage.

- Each hostile creature can trigger the reach save once per turn: the first time it enters your reach during that turn, or when it starts its turn there if it has not already triggered during that turn. Expanding your reach around a stationary creature does not count as entering.

- The reach effect is not an attack and cannot trigger hit riders. On a failed save choose Reaction denial or the 10-foot Speed reduction. On success apply half damage and the 5-foot reduction. Reapplication refreshes, not stacks, a Speed reduction from this feature.
sections.summary: - This is a temporary Body transformation. Record activation, current integrated Blade, Source CL, Fly Speed, reach, and selected damage types. It ends if you become Unconscious unless another rule preserves it.

facts: You hit with an unarmed strike.

items: No Reactions until the start of the target's next turn.
It cannot benefit from Invisible until the start of your next turn.
Disadvantage on its next Concentration saving throw before the start of your next turn.
Disadvantage on its next saving throw against possession, forced transformation, or a soul-affecting effect before the end of your next turn.

sections.name: Empty Strike
rules: Empty Strike affects Incorporeal creatures, possessing entities, Spirits, and soul-bound Constructs normally.
sections.summary: Deal an additional 2d8 Psychic or Force damage.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Empty Strike
rules: - The additional Psychic or Force damage is part of the triggering attack's damage packet. Choose its type for each use.

- “Cannot benefit from Invisible” suppresses the mechanical benefits of the Invisible condition for that target during the duration; it does not automatically end the condition, reveal disguises, or make the target visible to creatures that otherwise cannot perceive it.
- A Disadvantage option affects only the next qualifying saving throw in its duration and is then consumed. If no qualifying save occurs, it expires without effect.

- Empty Strike can affect a legally targeted Incorporeal creature, Spirit, possessing entity, or soul-bound Construct without losing damage or riders solely because of that nature. It does not by itself reveal an unseen entity, target an Intruder through a Host, or grant authority to strike a Complete Soul that is not otherwise a legal target.
sections.summary: - Declare after the unarmed strike hits. Spend Stamina before selecting and resolving the rider.

items: Move through creature spaces as difficult terrain.
Pass through openings as narrow as 1 inch.
Gain Advantage against Grappled, Restrained, possession, forced transformation, and unwilling teleportation.

sections.name: Hollow Immortal
sections.summary: You gain the following passive benefits:

items: Gain a Fly Speed of 40 feet and Hover.
Gain Resistance to all damage except Force, Radiant, and Void.
Move through ordinary walls, floors, ceilings, barriers, and creatures as difficult terrain.
You cannot be Grappled or Restrained by a physical effect whose Source CL is no higher than yours.
Use Hollow Step once per turn without paying its Stamina cost.
After emerging from an object, barrier, or creature's space, gain Advantage on your next attack roll before the end of the turn.
Empty Strike deals 3d8 additional damage instead of 2d8.

sections.name: Empty-World Incarnation
rules: You cannot end a turn inside an occupied space or object.
An artifact barrier, spatial lock, or higher-CL phasing barrier prevents passage unless you win an opposed Cultivation Check.
sections.summary: For the duration:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Hollow Immortal
rules: - The listed Advantage applies only to the checks and saves directly resisting or escaping the named effects. It does not create immunity.
sections.summary: - Passing through a 1-inch opening changes only the minimum opening needed by your body and normally carried equipment. It does not allow you to carry an oversized object, unwilling creature, vehicle, or structure through that opening.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Empty-World Incarnation
rules: - Hollow Step retains its Bonus Action, duration, targeting, and once-per-turn practical action limit; only its Stamina cost is waived. Activating Empty-World Incarnation does not automatically activate Hollow Step on the same Bonus Action.

- Physical Grapple or Restraint from a Source CL no higher than yours cannot be newly established and becomes ineffective while the state persists. A higher-Source-CL physical effect remains subject to its normal checks and saves.

- Emerging means leaving an object, barrier, or creature space after occupying at least part of it through this feature. Advantage applies to one next attack before the end of the same turn and does not stack from passing through multiple spaces.
- Empty Strike uses 3d8 instead of 2d8; this is a replacement, not 2d8 + 3d8.

- When attempting to enter or cross an artifact barrier, spatial lock, or higher-Source-CL phasing barrier, make one opposed Cultivation Check for that discrete barrier and movement attempt. On failure, movement ends in the nearest legal space before the barrier. On success, pass through for that movement only unless the barrier's rule says otherwise.
- Ending the turn in an illegal space uses the Phase Flesh displacement and unavoidable-damage procedure.
sections.summary: - Empty-World Incarnation is a temporary bodily state, not a separate projection. It preserves one body, one turn, one Hit Point total, and one set of conditions.

facts: Until the start of your next turn

items: Become Invisible.
Become Incorporeal.
Gain a Fly Speed equal to your walking Speed and Hover.
Move through creatures and nonartifact objects as difficult terrain.
Creatures unable to perceive you cannot make Opportunity Attacks against you.

sections.name: Hollow Step
rules: When the effect ends, gain Advantage on your first attack roll before the end of your next turn. The first hit before then deals an additional 2d8 Psychic or Force damage.
You cannot end the turn inside an occupied space or object. Use the Phase Flesh displacement and damage procedure if you do.
Spatial locks and barriers explicitly blocking phasing prevent passage.
sections.summary: For the duration:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Hollow Step
rules: - You remain one creature with one Hit Point total, action economy, condition set, equipment set, and Concentration limit. Hollow Step does not create a projection or duplicate body.
- Movement through creatures and nonartifact objects uses the Phase Flesh passage procedure. A creature whose space you enter is not damaged, pushed, or automatically aware of you.

- At the start of your next turn, after the state ends, record the attack benefit. Advantage applies to your first attack roll made before the end of that turn. If that attack hits, the same hit gains the 2d8 Psychic or Force damage. If it misses, both benefits are expended.
- If you end your turn in an illegal space, resolve displacement and 2d10 unavoidable Force damage immediately, before the state ends.
- A spatial lock or explicit phasing barrier blocks passage; it does not automatically end Hollow Step's other benefits.
sections.summary: - The state begins when the Bonus Action resolves and ends at the start of your next turn. Invisible, Incorporeal, flight, and phasing are one combined activation.

facts: An attack deals damage to you.

items: Move through creature spaces and nonartifact solid objects as difficult terrain.
Ignore nonmagical difficult terrain.
Gain Advantage on checks and saving throws to escape Grappled or Restrained.
groups.lead: Until the start of your next turn:

sections.name: Phase Flesh
rules: You cannot end a turn inside an occupied space or solid object. If you do, move to the nearest legal space and take 2d10 Force damage that cannot be reduced, prevented, redirected, or absorbed.
sections.summary: Halve the triggering damage after Resistance and Vulnerability are applied.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Phase Flesh
rules: - The phasing state begins after the triggering damage packet resolves. It does not make the triggering attack miss or invalidate riders that already resolved.

- During the state, a creature space or nonartifact solid object is difficult terrain. You need enough movement to traverse every entered space and cannot see through an opaque object merely because you can enter it.
- Worn and carried equipment moves with your phased body. You cannot use the feature to leave an unwilling creature, restrained passenger, structure, or oversized object inside solid matter.

- If you end a turn in an illegal occupied or solid space, move by the shortest route to the nearest legal space. If several are equally near, you choose among them. Then take the printed 2d10 Force damage. This damage ignores all reduction, prevention, redirection, absorption, Temporary Hit Points granted specifically against damage, and immunity.
- Phase Flesh does not bypass an artifact barrier, spatial lock, or effect explicitly preventing phasing.
sections.summary: - Declare after the triggering attack's damage has been calculated and Resistance and Vulnerability have been applied, but before Hit Points are reduced. Halve the remaining triggering damage, rounding down, before Stamina Guard and other flat reductions.

facts: You hit with an unarmed strike.
lossy: allowlist: results not directly after their save/attack
sections.name: Soul Severance
outcomes: The target is Stunned until the end of your next turn, cannot take Reactions, cannot willingly teleport or become Incorporeal, and has Disadvantage on Concentration saving throws. On a successful save, it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

items: Diagnosis: Learn the exact source, Source CL, save DC, duration, and removal procedure of one possession, forced transformation, soul-binding, or spiritual state.
Exorcism: A possessing entity makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, it is expelled into the nearest legal space.
Sever Temporary Bond: End one temporary possession, forced transformation, or soul-binding whose Source CL is no higher than yours.
Suppression: Suppress one higher-CL qualifying effect for 1 minute. This does not remove it.

sections.name: Spiritual Surgery
sections.summary: You may perform Soul Severance as a 10-minute procedure on a willing, Restrained, Incapacitated, or Unconscious target. Choose one:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Soul Severance
rules: - On failure, all printed restrictions last until the end of your next turn. On success, only Reaction denial applies, with its shorter printed duration.

- The temporary prohibition on willing teleportation or Incorporeality does not cancel an already occupied space or forcibly eject a creature from an existing form. It prevents new willing activations and voluntary use during the duration.
- A target can be affected by only one Soul Severance duration from you at a time; reapplication refreshes rather than stacks.
sections.summary: - Declare after the unarmed strike hits and spend Stamina before the Charisma save. The save and its riders are part of the same attack activation.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Spiritual Surgery
rules: - Diagnosis reveals only the listed mechanical data. A specific equal- or higher-Source-CL concealment can contest one datum through a Cultivation Check; failure tells you that datum is concealed rather than supplying false information.

- Exorcism targets one possessing entity already identified in the target. On a failed Charisma save, use the shared possession-separation procedure and place it in the nearest legal space capable of containing it. This does not destroy, bind, convert, or claim the entity.

- Sever Temporary Bond ends one temporary, unwilling possession, forced transformation, or temporary soul-binding whose Source CL is no higher than yours. It cannot end spirit ancestry, a legal character option, a permanent consensual Bond, a Complete Soul's personhood, or a higher-authority relationship without another rule.

- Suppression selects one qualifying higher-Source-CL effect. It becomes dormant for 1 minute but retains duration and ownership. This option does not remove it, transfer it, or prevent a higher-authority rule from ending the suppression.
- Use the Spirit Awakening Rules Reference or later Universal Cultivation Authority procedures for possession, Complete Souls, spiritual states, and authority collisions.
sections.summary: - The 10-minute procedure requires uninterrupted physical access to the target and a recorded qualifying spiritual state. The target must remain willing, Restrained, Incapacitated, or Unconscious for the full procedure.

facts: You hit with an unarmed strike.

items: The target cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
Its Speed becomes 0 until the start of its next turn.
It has Disadvantage on its next Concentration saving throw before the end of your next turn.
It has Disadvantage on its next saving throw against being Grappled or Joint Lock before the end of your next turn.
It makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it drops one nonartifact object it is holding.

sections.name: Death of a Thousand Cuts
sections.summary: The attack deals an additional 6d6 Piercing damage.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Death of a Thousand Cuts
rules: - Choose exactly one rider. The rider is not contingent on the target taking damage unless its own wording requires a save.

- For the drop-object rider, identify one nonartifact object the target is holding that you can perceive. On a failed save, it falls into the target's space or the nearest legal space. An integrated weapon, body part, worn item, or object physically fused by a higher-authority effect is not “held.”
- Disadvantage riders affect only the next qualifying roll in the duration and are then consumed. Reapplication refreshes rather than stacks.
sections.summary: - Declare after the hit and before rolling the additional damage. The 6d6 is part of the triggering attack's damage packet for Resistance and other damage modifiers.

items: Gain Advantage on the first attack roll you make against it during each turn.
Gain Advantage on attempts to Grapple it.
It has Disadvantage on the first saving throw it makes against Joint Lock during each of your turns.

sections.name: Eye of the Mantis
rules: The feature ends if the target is more than 1 mile from you.
sections.summary: Learn its current and maximum Hit Points, Armor Class, damage Resistances, damage Immunities, whether it is maintaining Concentration, its active physical conditions, and whether Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution is its lowest physical saving throw.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Eye of the Mantis
rules: - If an equal-or-higher-authority effect specifically conceals one listed datum from supernatural diagnosis, make a Cultivation Check against that effect's save DC. On failure, you learn that the datum is concealed rather than receiving false information.
- “Lowest physical saving throw” compares the target's total current Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution save modifiers, including temporary modifiers. If tied, learn all tied abilities.

- Each per-turn first occurrence is tracked separately: first attack roll, first Grapple attempt, and first Joint Lock save. The target being unseen does not by itself end the feature, but normal attack and perception rules still apply.
sections.summary: - The feature reads the target's current mechanical profile when activated. It reveals only the listed data and does not reveal hidden actions, future choices, spell or technique lists, exact ability scores, vulnerabilities, Source CL, or identity unless another rule does.

lossy: allowlist: results not directly after their save/attack
sections.name: Joint Lock
outcomes: The target is Restrained until the start of your next turn or until the Grapple ends. On a successful save, it cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn.
rules: Reusing Joint Lock requires a new saving throw.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Joint Lock
rules: - On failure, Restrained ends at the earlier of the start of your next turn, the Grapple ending, you becoming unable to maintain the required anatomy, or the target leaving your Grapple reach through a legal exception.
- On success, the no-Reactions result applies even though the target avoided Restrained.
- Each use is a new activation and save. Reapplication can refresh but never extend the Restrained duration beyond the start of your next turn.
sections.summary: - Select one creature you are currently Grappling and within your Grapple reach. The Grapple must be maintained by you, not solely by an ally or independent Asset.

sections.name: Mantis Hooks
rules: Once per turn when you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, attempt to Grapple it without using another action. The target makes a Strength or Dexterity saving throw, its choice. On a failure, it is Grappled by you.
Before rolling the attack's damage, you may choose to deal damage equal only to your ability modifier. If you do, the target has Disadvantage on the Grapple saving throw.
sections.summary: Your unarmed strikes may deal Piercing damage.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Mantis Hooks
rules: - The target chooses Strength or Dexterity each time it saves. This is a saving throw against your Cultivation Save DC, not an ability check.

- If you reduce the attack's damage, the total damage from that hit becomes only the ability modifier used for the attack roll, minimum 0. Do not roll the weapon or Iron Fist damage dice and do not add other damage riders from that attack unless they state they apply when the attack deals no normal damage.
- The hit still counts as a hit for Mantis Hooks and other non-damage triggers. The reduced-damage choice must be made before any damage dice are rolled.
- Mantis Hooks can activate once per turn, regardless of the number of attacks, reactions, or granted attacks you make.
sections.summary: - The free Grapple attempt occurs after the triggering hit resolves and requires the target to remain within your Grapple reach. Apply normal size and anatomy restrictions from Body Refining Shared Procedures.

sections.name: Rapid Pincer
rules: The additional strike cannot grant another attack, cannot cause Mantis Hooks to activate more than once during the turn, cannot apply the same once-per-turn damage rider twice, and cannot be replaced by Rapid Pincer.
sections.summary: Once per turn when you take the Attack action, replace one unarmed strike with two unarmed strikes.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Rapid Pincer
rules: - Both strikes are part of one Rapid Pincer activation, but each is a separate attack and damage packet.

- The additional strike is the second of the two. It cannot be replaced by a feature that replaces an attack with multiple attacks, cannot grant an attack, and cannot receive a once-per-turn rider already used during the turn.
- Rapid Pincer can be used only once per turn, even if you take more than one Attack action.
sections.summary: - Replace one unarmed strike when that strike would be made during your Attack action. Resolve the two replacement strikes sequentially against the same or different legal targets.

items: Fly Speed 30 feet and Hover.
Cannot be knocked Prone while airborne.
Count as one size larger when resisting forced movement.
groups.lead: While you have at least 3 Marks:

items: Temporary Hit Points equal to Proficiency Bonus.
Move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Add Proficiency Bonus to your next Strength or Dexterity saving throw before the start of your next turn.
groups.lead: When you would gain a Mark at maximum, choose one, each no more than once per round:

sections.name: Constellation Circuit
sections.summary: Maximum Marks becomes Proficiency Bonus + 3. When Initiative is rolled, gain 3 Marks.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Constellation Circuit
rules: - While current Marks are at least 3, gain Fly Speed 30 feet and Hover, cannot be knocked Prone while airborne, and count as one size larger when resisting forced movement. If Marks fall below 3 while unsupported, resolve falling immediately unless another flight remains.

- When a Mark would be gained at maximum, choose one overflow benefit instead. Each of the three benefits can be chosen no more than once per round, allowing up to three different overflow benefits in a round if separate legal Mark gains occur.
- Temporary Hit Points equal Proficiency Bonus and do not stack. The 5-foot movement is voluntary granted movement and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.

- For the save bonus, choose Strength or Dexterity when gained. Add Proficiency Bonus to one next save of that type before the start of your next turn, then consume the benefit. This is a feature bonus, not proficiency.
- An overflow gain still counts as that round's normal Stamina-generated Mark event. It cannot be repeatedly generated from the same activation.
sections.summary: - Maximum Marks becomes Proficiency Bonus + 3. The initiative grant becomes 3 Marks and replaces the former 1-Mark grant.

sections.name: Falling-Star Descent
rules: Each other chosen creature within 15 feet makes a Dexterity saving throw.
- Failed Save: 6d8 Force or Radiant damage, Prone, pushed 10 feet.
- Successful Save: Half damage, no Prone or push.
The ground becomes difficult terrain until repaired. Unattended ordinary objects, temporary barriers, vehicles, structures, and Formation Anchors take double damage.
sections.summary: Move to the selected space without provoking Opportunity Attacks, crossing open air but not solid barriers, total cover, sealed Formations, or spaces too small for you.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Falling-Star Descent
rules: - The movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. If the destination becomes illegal before arrival, stop in the nearest legal space along the route; the impact area is centered on the space where you stop.
- Choose any number of other creatures within 15 feet after arrival. Each makes one Dexterity save and is affected once. Choose Force or Radiant for the activation.
- Resolve damage, Prone, and push after arrival. A push moves directly away from you and stops at the nearest legal space. A successful save prevents Prone and push.

- The impacted ground in the 15-foot area becomes difficult terrain. Each 5-foot square can be cleared or repaired under the Body environmental-terrain procedure. This does not automatically create a crater, chasm, or permanent regional damage.

- Eligible unattended objects, temporary barriers, vehicles, structures, and Formation Anchors take double damage once. A surviving obstruction does not prevent the radial impact unless it provides total cover from your arrival space.
sections.summary: - Choose an unoccupied legal space within 60 feet that you can identify. The movement follows one continuous unobstructed route through open air or open space. It is physical celestial movement, not teleportation, and cannot pass through solid barriers, total cover, sealed Formations, or spaces too small for you.

items: Fly Speed 60 feet and Hover.
Resistance to all damage except Psychic and Void.
Unarmed strikes may deal Force or Radiant.
Once per turn on a hit, additional 4d8 Force or Radiant damage.
Hostile creatures treat spaces within 10 feet as difficult terrain.
A creature of your CL or lower cannot push, pull, knock you Prone, or move you against your will unless its feature explicitly ignores gravity or bodily anchoring.

sections.name: Nine-Star Incarnation
rules: Once per round when you hit, force a Strength save. On a failure, push or pull 20 feet and knock Prone; on a success, push or pull 5 feet.
Teleportation, spatial displacement, and effects explicitly ignoring gravity still function.
sections.summary: For the duration:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Nine-Star Incarnation
rules: - The 60-foot Fly Speed and Hover replace the conditional 30-foot flight while the form lasts. Resistance applies to every damage type except Psychic and Void and follows ordinary damage ordering.
- Each unarmed strike may replace its ordinary damage types with Force or Radiant. The once-per-turn 4d8 rider is part of one hit and uses Force or Radiant as chosen.

- Hostile creatures treat every space within 10 feet of you as difficult terrain while moving through it. Starting inside the area does not itself cost movement; each foot moved inside costs according to difficult terrain.

- A physical push, pull, Prone, or involuntary bodily movement with Source CL no greater than your effective Body Refining CL fails unless its Source Rule explicitly ignores gravity or bodily anchoring. Higher-Source-CL effects and explicit bypasses use their own authority. Teleportation and spatial displacement remain legal as printed.

- Once per round after an unarmed hit, choose that target for the Strength save. On failure, push or pull it up to 20 feet along a legal route and knock it Prone; on success, push or pull it 5 feet. If no legal destination exists, shorten or prevent movement, but Prone on a failed save still applies unless the target is immune.
- Suppression makes the transformation dormant, does not refund Marks or Stamina, and does not extend the one-minute duration.
sections.summary: - This is one temporary bodily and gravitational transformation. Spend 5 Marks when activating; its benefits do not require retaining 3 Marks afterward.

facts: An attack hits you, or you fail a Dexterity saving throw against a damaging effect.
sections.name: Orbital Body
ordered: Reduce the damage by 2d8 + Constitution modifier, then move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. If reduced to 0, move 15 feet instead.
The movement cannot cross a solid barrier, sealed Formation, or occupied space.
rules: The movement cannot cross a solid barrier, sealed Formation, or occupied space.
sections.summary: Reduce the damage by 2d8 + Constitution modifier, then move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. If reduced to 0, move 15 feet instead.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Orbital Body
rules: - Reduce one damage packet by 2d8 + Constitution modifier after Resistance, Vulnerability, and percentage modifiers but before other flat reductions that resolve later under Shared Procedures.
- After that packet resolves, move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks; move 15 feet instead if the packet was reduced to 0 by this feature and any earlier modifiers.
- The movement is voluntary granted movement. It cannot cross total cover, a solid barrier, sealed Formation, occupied space, or another explicit movement prohibition.
- Moving does not retroactively remove you from the triggering attack or area and does not negate other targets or later damage packets from the same activation.
- If no legal destination exists, remain in place; the damage reduction still applies.
sections.summary: - Declare after an attack hits you or after you fail a Dexterity save against a damaging effect, once damage is calculated but before Hit Points are reduced. Spend the Reaction and 1 Mark.

facts: You hit with an unarmed strike.

items: Move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Push the target 5 feet.
Pull it 5 feet toward you.
Gain +1 AC against it until the start of your next turn.
groups.lead: Deal an additional 1d8 Force or Radiant damage and choose one:

lossy: allowlist: header fact inside the body
sections.name: Star-Lit Acupoints
sections.summary: While you have at least 1 Mark, you may emit or suppress Dim Light in 5 feet.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Star-Lit Acupoints
rules: - Declare the strike rider after an unarmed hit, spend 1 Mark, and add 1d8 Force or Radiant damage. It is part of the triggering hit and cannot critically multiply separately.

- Choose one movement or defense result. Self-movement is voluntary granted movement and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Push and pull use a legal straight route and cannot place the target in an occupied or solid space.
- The +1 AC applies only against attacks made by the triggering target and lasts until the start of your next turn. It is an AC bonus and does not replace your formula.
- The feature remains once per turn even if Marks are regained during the same turn.
sections.summary: - Emitting or suppressing Dim Light requires no action and can be changed once during your turn. The light reveals your space normally and grants no concealment, truesight, or Radiance authority.

items: Once per turn when an unarmed strike damages a Bloodied qualifying hostile creature, gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

When you reduce a qualifying hostile creature to 0 Hit Points with an unarmed strike, regain Hit Points equal to your Constitution modifier plus your Proficiency Bonus. This healing can occur once per creature.
groups.lead: While Oni Mask or Oni Form is active:

sections.name: Blood Drinker
sections.summary: Blood Drinker cannot generate healing or Temporary Hit Points from harmless animals, allied creatures, creatures created for resource loops, repeatedly revived or recaptured targets, or creatures that do not qualify under the Qualifying Hostile Creature rule.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Blood Drinker
rules: - Temporary Hit Points are granted after the damage packet resolves. They follow the normal nonstacking rule.

- The 0-Hit-Point healing resolves after the target is actually reduced to 0 Hit Points and before later corpse, death, or capture procedures. It can occur only once for that creature from you, regardless of revival, transformation, replacement body, or later recapture.
- “Qualifying hostile creature” uses the universal anti-farming rule. A creature created, summoned, revived, healed, captured, or staged primarily to generate this benefit does not qualify.
- Blood Drinker is bodily predation, not soul consumption. It does not capture a soul, steal a Foundation, copy a Sphere, or create harvestable blood authority.
sections.summary: - Determine whether the target is Bloodied immediately before the qualifying unarmed strike deals damage. A hit that first makes an unbloodied target Bloodied does not satisfy the first bullet for that hit.

facts: You would be reduced to 0 Hit Points but are not killed outright.

items: Regain Hit Points equal to half your maximum Hit Points.
Activate Oni Form without paying its cost, even if it was already used.
End Frightened, Stunned, or Restrained on yourself when the effect's Source CL is no higher than yours.
Gain Advantage on unarmed attack rolls against Bloodied hostile creatures.
Blood Drinker grants Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus.
Your unarmed strikes deal an additional 3d6 Necrotic damage once per turn instead of 2d6.

sections.name: Crimson Oni
rules: When this Oni Form ends, gain 1 level of Exhaustion and your demonic traits remain impossible to conceal until you complete a full 2-hour Cultivation Session.
Only one feature that prevents or replaces the same reduction to 0 Hit Points may resolve.
sections.summary: Instead:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Crimson Oni
rules: - Only one feature can replace that reduction. If killed outright, if your body is completely destroyed, or if an effect expressly forbids this restoration, Crimson Oni cannot resolve unless another rule overrides that prohibition.

- Regain half maximum Hit Points, rounding down, then activate Oni Form without its Stamina cost or scene restriction. This special Oni Form has the normal 1-minute duration and all normal Oni Form rules.
- End only the listed conditions whose creating Source CL is no higher than yours. If multiple qualifying instances exist, all qualifying instances of those three named conditions end.
- During the special form, Blood Drinker's Temporary Hit Points become twice Proficiency Bonus. The 3d6 rider replaces Oni Form's 2d6 and Oni Mask's 1d6; do not add them together.
- When this special form ends for any reason, gain 1 Exhaustion and begin the visible-trait aftermath. Suppression does not postpone the aftermath beyond the form's original ending time.

- “Full 2-hour Cultivation Session” means two uninterrupted hours of demonic restraint, breath regulation, blood purification, or an equivalent recorded Oni rite. Interruption requires restarting the session. Completing it ends only the concealment aftermath, not Exhaustion or another consequence.
sections.summary: - Declare after damage is determined to reduce you to 0 Hit Points but before Unconsciousness, death saves, or other 0-Hit-Point consequences. Pay 6 Stamina and expend the scene use when declared.

sections.name: Demon Roar
ordered: Choose Psychic or Necrotic damage. A Bloodied creature has Disadvantage on its first saving throw against this feature.
a creature takes 4d8 damage and is Frightened of you for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each turn and ending Frightened on a success.
it takes half damage and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
outcomes: A creature takes 4d8 damage and is Frightened of you for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each turn and ending Frightened on a success.
It takes half damage and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
sections.summary: Choose Psychic or Necrotic damage. A Bloodied creature has Disadvantage on its first saving throw against this feature.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Demon Roar
rules: - A creature is Bloodied for the initial-save Disadvantage if it is at or below half its maximum Hit Points when that initial save is rolled.

- “Its first saving throw against this feature” means the initial save against that activation. Repeat saves against Frightened are not made with Disadvantage from this clause unless another effect applies it.
- On success, Reaction denial begins after damage resolves. On failure, Frightened uses the printed repeat-save timing and ends only for that creature when it succeeds.
- The roar does not force movement, compel attacks, reveal hidden creatures, or affect unattended objects unless another rule expressly says so.
sections.summary: - Choose Psychic or Necrotic when activating the feature. The cone originates from your body and requires line of effect.

items: Become Large if smaller.
Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your CL.
Gain Resistance to Cold, Fire, and Necrotic damage.
Gain Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
Your unarmed reach increases by 5 feet.
Once per turn when you hit with an unarmed strike, deal an additional 2d6 Necrotic damage instead of Oni Mask's 1d6.
Blood Hunger applies whenever you can perceive any Bloodied hostile creature within 30 feet.

sections.name: Oni Form
rules: When Oni Form ends, Oni Mask also ends.
sections.summary: Activate Oni Mask without paying its cost.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Oni Form
rules: - If smaller than Large, become Large only if the current space can legally contain that size. If already Large or larger, retain the current size. Equipment follows the shared transformation procedure.
- Temporary Hit Points are granted once when the form begins and do not refresh each turn. Reapplication follows the normal nonstacking rule.
- The unarmed reach increase is persistent for the duration. Advantage on Strength checks and saves does not apply to Constitution-based Cultivation Checks unless another rule says so.
- The 2d6 once-per-turn Necrotic damage replaces Oni Mask's 1d6 rider; do not add both.
- Blood Hunger is checked whenever any perceived Bloodied hostile creature is within 30 feet, as printed. The form creates no obligation when no such creature is perceived.
- When Oni Form ends for any reason, the Oni Mask activation included with it also ends. An independently activated Mask with a separate later duration is not created by the form.
sections.summary: - Oni Form is a temporary transformation and includes one free activation or refresh of Oni Mask as part of the same Bonus Action. Do not pay Oni Mask's Stamina cost.

items: Gain Advantage on Intimidation checks.
Gain Disadvantage on Persuasion checks.
Once per turn when you hit with an unarmed strike, deal an additional 1d6 Necrotic damage.
Iron Voice may manifest as a demonic roar.
Blood Hunger applies.

sections.name: Oni Mask
rules: You may end Oni Mask without using an action.
sections.summary: For the duration:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Oni Mask
rules: - Ending the Mask requires no action and can occur at any time you are able to make decisions, including during your turn. Ending it does not refund Stamina.
- The 1d6 Necrotic rider applies to one qualifying unarmed-strike hit per turn and is part of that attack's damage packet.
- Iron Voice may use demonic presentation but retains its own range, action, costs, saves, and effects.
- Activating or refreshing Oni Mask creates one duration; multiple uses do not stack its social modifiers or damage rider.
sections.summary: - Oni Mask is a temporary bodily manifestation. Record its visible traits when first learned. It does not change size, occupied space, equipment, reach, or anatomy unless another Oni Blood feature says so.

facts: You fail a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution saving throw.
lossy: allowlist: results not directly after their save/attack
sections.name: Ash-Shedding Reversal
outcomes: Resolve the successful-save result, do not apply conditions imposed only on failure, and move 5 feet without provoking after the effect resolves.
rules: Cannot reroll death saves, breakthrough checks, training checks, Hidden Injury repair checks, or a roll already rerolled.
sections.summary: Reroll the save and use the new result.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Ash-Shedding Reversal
rules: - Spend 2 Embers and reroll the same save against the same DC. The new roll replaces the old roll even if worse.

- On a new success, resolve the feature's printed successful-save result. A condition or rider that applies only on failure is not applied. Damage or another effect that also occurs on success still occurs.

- After the triggering effect finishes resolving, move up to 5 feet without provoking along a legal route. This movement occurs even if the successful-save result still dealt damage, but not if you became Incapacitated or unable to move before it occurs.
- One roll can be rerolled only once. This feature cannot chain with itself or another reroll after a reroll has already replaced that roll.
- The exclusions in the source are absolute and cannot be bypassed through an Insight, item, or Subpath interaction unless that Source Rule explicitly names Ash-Shedding Reversal.
sections.summary: - Declare immediately after learning that the Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution save failed, before applying failure-only damage, conditions, movement, or other consequences.

sections.name: Cinder Blood
rules: At the start of your turn, spend 1 Rebirth Ember to regain 1d8 + Constitution modifier Hit Points, increasing to 2d8 at CL11 and 3d8 at CL17. This requires no action and functions once per turn, but not while at 0 Hit Points.
sections.summary: Gain Resistance to Fire damage.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Cinder Blood
rules: - At the start of your turn, after resolving mandatory start-of-turn damage and before taking an Action, you may spend 1 Ember. This is not an Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, technique activation, or Stamina expenditure.
- Roll the printed healing once. Add Constitution modifier once, to a minimum of 0 Hit Points regained. The die scaling replaces the earlier die rather than adding to it.
- Cinder Blood can function once during each of your turns. It cannot be declared while you are at 0 Hit Points and cannot retroactively interrupt damage.
- Healing from Cinder Blood is self-generated Body Refining healing for Flesh Rejects Gentleness and similar procedures.
sections.summary: - Fire Resistance follows normal damage ordering.

sections.name: Flame-Wing Rush
rules: Until the end of the turn, the first unarmed strike you hit with deals an additional 2d8 Fire or Radiant damage.
Moving through open flame or burning terrain during this movement does not damage you or count as difficult terrain.
sections.summary: Whenever you spend a Rebirth Ember through Cinder Blood, move up to half your Speed without provoking.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Flame-Wing Rush
rules: - Open flame and burning terrain crossed during this granted movement deal no damage to you and do not count as difficult terrain. An unrelated hazard, solid barrier, creature space, or non-Fire terrain remains relevant.
- If you end this movement inside an ongoing Fire hazard, Furnace Without Fuel or Fire Resistance/Immunity applies normally to later instances; Flame-Wing Rush does not create continuing immunity.

- Record one Flame-Wing charge until the end of the current turn. The first unarmed strike you hit with consumes it and adds 2d8 Fire or Radiant damage, chosen on the hit. A second Cinder Blood use is impossible during the same turn and cannot create another charge.
- The extra damage is part of the hit's damage event and does not separately trigger hit riders or critical multiplication.
sections.summary: - After Cinder Blood resolves and restores at least 1 Hit Point, move up to half your current Speed without provoking. This movement is physical movement, not flight or teleportation, and follows legal-space and terrain rules except as printed below.

sections.name: Furnace Without Fuel
rules: When a hostile creature, active supernatural effect, or active environmental hazard would deal Fire damage equal to at least Proficiency Bonus before Immunity, gain 1 Rebirth Ember after the damage resolves, obeying the once-per-round limit.
Ash-Shedding Reversal may also respond to Paralyzed, Petrified, or Stunned. Petrified costs 3 Embers.
sections.summary: Gain Immunity to Fire damage.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Furnace Without Fuel
rules: - For Ember generation, calculate the Fire portion the hostile source or genuine active environmental hazard would have applied before your Fire Immunity, but after any other reductions that would still apply. If that amount equals or exceeds Proficiency Bonus, gain 1 Ember after the instance resolves.
- The damage need not reduce Hit Points because Immunity prevents it. It must nevertheless be a real damaging instance with a legal source; standing in a harmless decorative flame does not qualify.
- This generation obeys the shared once-per-round Ember limit. Several Fire packets in the same area or activation cannot grant additional Embers that round.

- Ash-Shedding Reversal can respond to Paralyzed, Petrified, or Stunned even if the failed save uses an ability other than Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution only when the effect itself imposed one of those named conditions and its Source Rule permits a save reroll. Paralyzed and Stunned cost 2 Embers; Petrified costs 3.
- A successful reroll against Petrified prevents only failure-only Petrification consequences. It does not reconstruct anatomy or reverse an already completed permanent Petrification.
sections.summary: - Fire Immunity replaces Fire Resistance.

facts: You would be reduced to 0 Hit Points.
6 Stamina and at least 3 Rebirth Embers

items: Regain half your maximum Hit Points.
Stand without movement.
End Blinded, Deafened, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, Restrained, and Stunned.
Each chosen hostile creature within 20 feet makes a Dexterity save, taking 8d8 Fire or Radiant damage and being pushed 10 feet on a failure, or half damage and no push on a success.
Move up to your Speed without provoking.

sections.name: Rebirth from Cinders
rules: Cannot activate against instant death, total bodily destruction, an effect explicitly preventing recovery, or a reduction that another zero-Hit-Point replacement already resolves.
sections.summary: Consume all Embers. Instead of reaching 0:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Rebirth from Cinders
rules: - You must have 6 Stamina and at least 3 Embers. Spend the Stamina, then consume every Ember. The cost is paid even if a later collision or authority rule prevents some secondary result.
- This use replaces reaching 0 Hit Points. Set your Hit Points to half maximum, rounded down, with a minimum of 1. It does not count as healing from 0, resurrection, or reconstruction.

- Resolve the printed results in order: regain Hit Points; stand without spending movement if a legal standing posture is possible; end the listed conditions; choose Fire or Radiant for the entire burst; resolve chosen hostile creatures within 20 feet; then move up to your Speed without provoking.

- A chosen creature makes one Dexterity save. On failure it takes 8d8 and is pushed 10 feet directly away from you; on success it takes half and is not pushed. The burst originates from you and requires line of effect. A creature can be chosen once.
- The final movement is physical movement and must follow a legal route. It does not grant flight or passage through creatures or barriers.

- Only one 0-Hit-Point replacement can resolve against an event. Instant death, total bodily destruction, Erasure, a legal effect that explicitly prevents recovery, or an event already replaced by another feature bars this use.
- Realm Suppression after activation does not reverse the regained Hit Points, but can make the burst or movement dormant if suppression occurs before that component resolves.
sections.summary: - Declare after all damage modifiers and reductions are determined, at the moment the event would reduce you to 0 Hit Points but before entering the 0-Hit-Point state, making a death save, or applying a rider that requires you to reach 0.

items: Add one Gather and Return damage die.
Increase the attack's push by 5 feet.
Move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
groups.lead: When using Gather and Return, spend between 1 and 3 Momentum. For each Momentum spent, choose one benefit:

sections.name: Avalanche Meridian Circuit
rules: When the normal Momentum rules would grant 1 Momentum, gain 2 instead. A feature directly stating "gain 1 Momentum," such as Store the Collision, still grants exactly 1 unless stated otherwise.
You may choose the same benefit more than once.
sections.summary: Your maximum Momentum becomes Proficiency Bonus + 3.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Avalanche Meridian Circuit
rules: - The once-per-round normal Momentum grant becomes 2. A feature directly saying “gain 1 Momentum” remains 1 and is not doubled.
- At this level, Gather and Return's cost and option procedure is replaced: spend 1, 2, or 3 Momentum and make one selection for each point spent from the three printed benefits.
- Each damage selection adds one die of Gather and Return's current size (2d8 at CL14 and 3d8 only when the base feature reaches CL17). Multiple selections add multiple dice.
- The first push selection creates a 5-foot push; each additional push selection adds 5 feet. The push remains directly away unless another rule permits a different direction.

- Each movement selection grants 5 feet of voluntary movement without Opportunity Attacks after the hit. Combine multiple selections into one movement of the total distance or divide them into legal segments during that resolution.
- You may repeat any printed selection. The CL3 +1 AC option is not among Avalanche Meridian Circuit's printed selection list and is unavailable when using this replaced procedure.
sections.summary: - Replace maximum Momentum with Proficiency Bonus + 3.

facts: You hit with an unarmed strike.

items: Push the target 5 feet.
Move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Gain +1 AC against the target until the start of your next turn.
Add 5 feet to the next forced movement you impose before the end of the turn.

sections.name: Gather and Return
sections.summary: The attack deals an additional 1d8 Bludgeoning or Force damage, increasing to 2d8 at CL11 and 3d8 at CL17.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Gather and Return
rules: - The additional damage is part of the triggering attack's damage packet and uses the printed scaling.
- A 5-foot push is directly away along a legal route. The 5-foot self-movement is voluntary granted movement after the hit and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- The +1 AC applies only against attacks made by the triggering target and expires at the start of your next turn. Reapplication refreshes and does not stack.

- The forced-movement increase applies to the next forced movement you impose before the end of the same turn. It does not create forced movement, affect teleportation, or stack with another instance from the same activation unless Avalanche Meridian Circuit permits repeated selection.
sections.summary: - Declare after the unarmed strike hits, spend Momentum, and select the damage type and one option before resolving the rider.

sections.name: Heaven-Returning Impact
rules: Move to an unoccupied space you can see along the line without provoking Opportunity Attacks. You may move through hostile creature spaces, but not through total cover, a sealed Formation, spatial lock, or solid barrier that survives the damage.
Each creature whose space the line crosses or that is within 5 feet of it makes a Dexterity saving throw.
Damage equals 6d10 Force + 1d10 per Momentum spent.
- Failed Save: Full damage, pushed up to 20 feet perpendicular to the line, knocked Prone, and no Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Successful Save: Half damage, pushed 5 feet, and remains standing.
A creature can take this damage only once per use. Unattended objects, temporary barriers, vehicles, structures, terrain sections, and Formation Anchors take double damage.

If a barrier survives, your movement ends before it and you take Force damage equal to twice your CL. Stamina Guard may reduce this recoil, but no Momentum feature can reduce it or generate Momentum from it.
The destination becomes a 10-foot-radius impact zone of difficult terrain until cleared or repaired.
sections.summary: Movement: Up to 120 feet in a straight line

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Heaven-Returning Impact
rules: - The line has your normal occupied width unless the map requires a 5-foot-wide line. You travel along it without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Hostile creature spaces are passable; total cover, a surviving solid barrier, sealed Formation, or spatial lock is not.
- Resolve every creature's save once. A creature whose space intersects the line and is also within 5 feet of it still takes damage only once.

- Damage is one 6d10 + 1d10 per Momentum spent Force packet. On failure, you choose one of the two perpendicular directions and push up to 20 feet along a legal route; on success, push 5 feet in the chosen perpendicular direction.

- Resolve eligible objects, structures, terrain sections, vehicles, barriers, and Formation Anchors as the line reaches them. Apply double damage once. If a solid barrier is destroyed by the activation, movement can continue; if it survives, movement ends in the nearest legal space before it.

- Recoil from a surviving barrier is one Force packet equal to twice your CL. Stamina Guard can reduce it. No Momentum feature can reduce, prevent, redirect, absorb, or generate Momentum from that recoil.
- The destination impact zone consists of the bounded 10-foot radius of ordinary damaged ground. It remains difficult terrain until cleared or repaired under the shared damaged-terrain procedure.
sections.summary: - Confirm at least 3 Momentum, choose a visible unoccupied legal destination on a straight line within 120 feet, then pay 5 Stamina and all current Momentum. Record the Momentum spent before rolling damage.

facts: A hostile creature within 60 feet moves you, misses you with a melee attack, or damages you with a melee attack.
sections.name: Rebounding Assault
rules: If you end within unarmed reach, make one unarmed strike. On a hit, deal additional Force damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus and either push the target 10 feet or knock it Prone.
The attack follows the Granted Attack rule.
sections.summary: After the triggering effect resolves, move up to your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. You may move through the triggering creature's space as difficult terrain and must end closer to it.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Rebounding Assault
rules: - Move through the triggering creature's space as difficult terrain only if you have enough movement and can legally pass through its space under this feature. You cannot end in its space.

- Every movement segment must end closer to the triggering creature than the immediately preceding position; the final space must also be closer than your starting space. If no legal closer movement exists, the movement ends.
- The unarmed strike occurs after movement if the target remains within reach. It follows the Granted Attack rule.

- On a hit, Proficiency Bonus Force damage is part of the attack packet. Then choose either a 10-foot push directly away or Prone. No collision damage is created unless another rule expressly supplies it.
sections.summary: - The trigger occurs after the hostile movement, missed melee attack, or damaging melee attack fully resolves. A single hostile activation can trigger this feature only once.

facts: You would be pushed, pulled, thrown, or moved against your will; take falling damage; or take Bludgeoning, Force, or Thunder damage.

items: Store Movement: Reduce forced movement by up to 15 feet. If reduced to 0, you are not knocked Prone by the same effect and gain 1 Momentum.
Store Impact: Reduce the triggering damage by 2d8 + Constitution modifier. If reduced to 0, gain 1 Momentum.

sections.name: Store the Collision
rules: Momentum gained through Store the Collision can exceed the normal once-per-round generation limit.
sections.summary: Choose one:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Store the Collision
rules: - Store Movement is declared after the movement distance and Prone rider are known but before movement occurs. Reduce the total forced movement by up to 15 feet. If the remaining distance is 0, cancel a Prone rider expressly caused by that same movement and gain 1 Momentum.

- Store Impact is declared after Resistance, Vulnerability, and percentage modifiers but before Hit Points are reduced. Apply 2d8 + Constitution modifier as a flat reduction in the shared damage order. If the final triggering packet is reduced to 0, gain 1 Momentum.

- Store Impact can be combined with Stamina Guard when both are legal. The same packet may grant one direct Momentum from Store Impact and the round's normal Momentum from Stamina Guard if both separate requirements are met.
- Falling damage can trigger Store Impact. A fall cannot use Store Movement unless another rule is moving you against your will rather than gravity merely causing the fall.
- Direct Momentum from this feature can exceed the normal generation limit but not your maximum Momentum.
sections.summary: - One triggering event can cause one Reaction and one selected mode, even when it includes both forced movement and qualifying damage.

sections.name: Dragon's Breath
outcomes: A creature takes 4d6 damage, increasing to 6d6 at CL11 and 8d6 at CL17. On a successful save, it takes half damage.
rules: Unattended fragile objects automatically fail the save.
sections.summary: Choose Lightning or Thunder damage.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Dragon's Breath
rules: - The cone originates from your mouth or another recorded breath organ and requires an unobstructed line of effect. It is a bodily projection exception with the printed 15-foot area and does not create a lingering cloud or Field.
- Each creature in the cone makes one save and takes damage once. A creature occupying more than one space in the cone is still affected only once.

- “Unattended fragile object” means a discrete, unworn, uncarried object that the GM has classified as readily breakable, such as ordinary glass, pottery, paper, thin wood, or comparable material. It automatically fails but retains Immunities and Damage Thresholds. Other objects are affected only when their own rules permit the breath to damage them.
- Cover and line of effect are checked from the breath's point of origin. The breath does not pass through total cover.
sections.summary: - Choose Lightning or Thunder when activating the feature. Every damage roll from that activation uses the chosen type.
