sections.name: Dragon's Roar
outcomes: A creature takes 5d8 Thunder damage and is Stunned until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, it takes half damage and cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn.
rules: Unattended objects, temporary barriers, and Formation Anchors in the cone take double damage.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Dragon's Roar
rules: - Stunned and Reaction denial begin after damage is resolved and last exactly as printed. A creature that succeeds is not Stunned.
- An eligible unattended object, temporary barrier, or Formation Anchor takes one damage instance and applies the printed doubling once, even if it belongs to more than one listed category.
- Worn, carried, wielded, piloted, or actively controlled objects are not unattended. Artifact objects and world-scale structures retain their own authority and are not automatically destroyed.

- The roar is a Sound- and body-origin effect. Silence or a rule that specifically blocks supernatural sound can contest or prevent it only to the extent printed by that rule; ordinary ambient noise does not.
sections.summary: - The cone originates from your body and requires line of effect. Each creature in it makes one Constitution save.

sections.name: Dragon Scales
rules: Once per turn when you hit with an unarmed strike, deal additional Lightning damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
sections.summary: While benefiting from Unarmored Defense, gain +1 AC and Resistance to Lightning damage.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Dragon Scales
rules: - Lightning Resistance is a bodily inheritance and remains active while conscious or Unconscious unless an effect specifically suppresses this feature or your Body Refining cultivation.

- The once-per-turn Lightning damage is part of the triggering unarmed strike's damage packet. It applies after the hit is confirmed, cannot critically multiply separately, and cannot trigger another on-hit rider by itself.
- Scales may be visible or concealable as established by the character's recorded anatomy. Visibility has no additional mechanical consequence unless another rule expressly refers to it.
sections.summary: - The +1 AC is an AC bonus that applies only while Unarmored Defense is the formula currently determining your AC. It does not apply while armor or a replacement AC formula is used.

items: Gain a Fly Speed of 60 feet and Hover.
Gain Immunity to Lightning damage.
Gain Resistance to Thunder damage.
You may become Large.
Your unarmed reach increases by 5 feet.
Dragon's Breath becomes a 30-foot cone and deals 8d6.
Use Storm Step once per turn for 1 Stamina instead of 3.
Once per turn when you hit with an unarmed strike, deal an additional 3d6 Lightning or Thunder damage.

sections.name: Ryūjin Ascendant Form
rules: A hostile creature that starts its turn within 10 feet makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, push it 5 feet and prevent it from taking Reactions until the start of its next turn.
sections.summary: For the duration:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Ryūjin Ascendant Form
rules: - “You may become Large” is optional. If chosen, you become Large only if your current space can legally contain that size. If already Large or larger, the feature does not reduce your size. Ending the form returns you to your prior legal size under the transformation procedure.

- The 5-foot unarmed reach increase is persistent for the duration and applies to unarmed attacks and Body features using unarmed reach. It does not enlarge the range of Dragon's Breath, Dragon's Roar, or Storm Step.
- Dragon's Breath retains its Action and 2-Stamina cost. Its cone becomes 30 feet and its damage is 8d6; this is a replacement profile, not additional damage.
- Storm Step retains its Bonus Action and all destination restrictions. It costs 1 Stamina during the form and remains usable no more than once during each of your turns.
- The 3d6 rider is once per turn total and replaces no other Dragon Scales damage; both apply to a qualifying hit because the source prints both benefits.

- At the start of each hostile creature's turn, check whether it is within 10 feet. It saves once for that turn. On failure, push it 5 feet directly away along a legal route and deny Reactions. If no legal space exists, it remains in place but still loses Reactions.
- Suppressing the form makes its benefits dormant and does not extend its duration or refund its scene use.
sections.summary: - This is a temporary bodily transformation. Record the chosen size, occupied space, equipment fit, flight, reach, Resistances, and active breath profile when it begins.

sections.name: Storm Step
ordered: Teleport to an unoccupied space you can see.

Each hostile creature of your choice within 5 feet of the destination makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes 2d6 Lightning or Thunder damage and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and retains its Reactions.
Storm Step cannot cross a spatial lock, sealed planar boundary, Formation explicitly blocking teleportation, or total planar separation.
rules: Each hostile creature of your choice within 5 feet of the destination makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes 2d6 Lightning or Thunder damage and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and retains its Reactions.
Storm Step cannot cross a spatial lock, sealed planar boundary, Formation explicitly blocking teleportation, or total planar separation.
sections.summary: Teleport to an unoccupied space you can see.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Storm Step
rules: - Storm Step is teleportation. It does not trace a movement path, does not provoke Opportunity Attacks, and does not count as crossing intervening spaces.

- If a spatial lock, sealed planar boundary, qualifying Formation, total planar separation, or another explicit prohibition blocks the destination, use Failed Spatial Movement. The arrival burst does not occur when the teleport fails.

- After arriving, choose any number of hostile creatures within 5 feet of the destination. Each chosen creature saves once. A creature cannot be affected more than once by the same Storm Step even if it occupies multiple spaces.

- Reaction denial begins after the save resolves. The feature does not reveal hidden creatures; you can choose only hostile creatures you can identify as valid targets through your current senses or another legal targeting rule.
sections.summary: - Select the destination and damage type when activating the feature. The destination must be an unoccupied legal space you can see on the same plane and within 30 feet.

items: Climb Speed equal to Speed.
Jump distances quadrupled.
Move across liquids and vertical surfaces during your turn.
Once per turn after moving 15 feet, your next unarmed strike has Advantage.

sections.name: Fifth Coil: Ascending Serpent
rules: A target thrown into another creature causes both to take Bludgeoning damage equal to Proficiency Bonus; the second creature avoids it on a successful Dexterity save.
sections.summary: On a hit with that attack, spend 1 Stamina. The target makes a Strength save. On a failure, throw it 20 feet; on a success, push 5 feet.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Ascending Serpent
rules: - Once per turn, after you have physically moved at least 15 feet during the current turn, record Advantage on your next unarmed strike before the end of that turn. Teleportation does not count unless expressly treated as movement.

- After that advantaged strike hits, you may spend 1 Stamina. The target makes one Strength save. On failure, throw it up to 20 feet in a direction you choose along a legal trajectory. On success, push it 5 feet directly away from you.

- A throw or push stops at the nearest legal space before a solid obstruction. If the failed-save target first enters another creature's space and cannot continue, both creatures take Bludgeoning damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus; the second creature makes one Dexterity save and takes no collision damage on success. Resolve one second-creature collision only.
- The thrown target takes its collision damage automatically. Collision damage does not create Prone, an Injury, another throw, or repeated contacts unless another Source Rule says so.
sections.summary: - Climb Speed equals current walking Speed. Quadruple jump distances after ordinary jump calculations. During your turn you can move across liquids and vertical surfaces while movement remains; if unsupported when movement ends, resolve falling immediately.

sections.name: First and Second Coils
rules: - Swift Serpent: Speed +10 feet; once per turn after a hit, move 5 feet without provoking.
sections.summary: - Root Serpent: Advantage against Grappled, Shoved, and Prone; standing costs 5 feet.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — First and Second Coils
rules: - Swift Serpent: Add 10 feet to walking Speed. Once per turn after one attack hits, move up to 5 feet without provoking along a legal route. The movement occurs after the hit resolves and does not require an unarmed strike.
- Each benefit operates only while its Coil remains open. Closing Swift Serpent does not retract movement already completed.
sections.summary: - Root Serpent: Advantage applies to checks and saves made to avoid, resist, or escape Grappled, Shoved, or Prone. Standing from Prone costs 5 feet of movement regardless of current Speed, unless Speed is 0.

items: Speed doubles.
Fly Speed equal to walking Speed and Hover.
Resistance to all damage except Psychic and Void.
Unarmed strikes deal an additional 2d8 Force.
Grapple creatures up to two sizes larger.
A Grappled creature cannot teleport unless it succeeds on a Cultivation Check against your DC; failure uses Failed Spatial Movement.

sections.name: Seventh Coil: Heaven-Swallowing Serpent
rules: - Failed Save: 6d8 Bludgeoning or Force, no Reactions, Speed 0, and Disadvantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saves until your next turn.
- Successful Save: Half damage and Speed halved until your next turn.
At the end of each turn with the Seventh Coil open, take 2d8 Force damage that cannot be reduced, prevented, redirected, absorbed, or used to generate resources.
sections.summary: Once per turn when you hit a Grappled creature, spend 2 Stamina for Heaven-Swallowing Constriction. It makes a Constitution save.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Heaven-Swallowing Serpent
rules: - Gain Fly Speed equal to current walking Speed and Hover. If the Coil closes or is suppressed while unsupported, resolve falling immediately unless another support remains.
- Resistance to all damage except Psychic and Void follows ordinary ordering. The 2d8 Force added to every unarmed-strike hit is part of that hit's packet and does not have a once-per-turn limit.
- Functional size increases by two categories only for Grappling. It combines with Crushing Serpent by using the highest applicable value rather than increasing by three categories.

- A creature Grappled by you that attempts any teleportation or spatial movement must first make one Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC. On failure use Failed Spatial Movement; on success the spatial movement resolves and ordinarily ends the physical Grapple unless its rule says otherwise.

- Once per turn after hitting a creature currently Grappled by you, spend 2 Stamina to use Heaven-Swallowing Constriction. It makes one Constitution save. On failure it takes 6d8 Bludgeoning or Force, cannot take Reactions, has Speed 0, and has Disadvantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saves until the start of your next turn. On success it takes half damage and its Speed is halved until the start of your next turn.
- Constriction damage is a separate packet created by the same activation and does not automatically create an Injury or destroy organs.

- At the end of each turn while the Seventh Coil remains open, before Coil upkeep, take 2d8 Force damage applied directly to Hit Points. It cannot be reduced, prevented, redirected, absorbed by Temporary Hit Points, delayed, shared, or converted into healing, Stamina, Charges, Beats, Momentum, or another resource.
- If that damage makes you Unconscious, all Coils close before upkeep and no Stamina is paid. Otherwise pay the printed 2-Stamina seven-Coil upkeep after the damage.
sections.summary: - Double walking Speed after fixed additions. A movement mode explicitly equal to walking Speed uses the doubled value; fixed Speeds and teleport ranges do not.

items: Blindsight 20 feet.
Advantage against Charmed and Frightened.
Cannot be Surprised while conscious.
Unarmed reach +5 feet during your turn.

sections.name: Sixth Coil: Crowned Serpent
sections.summary: Once per round when a hostile creature within Blindsight moves or teleports, spend 1 Stamina to move 10 feet without provoking, ending closer to it.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Crowned Serpent
rules: - Advantage applies to saves made to avoid or end Charmed and Frightened. You cannot be Surprised while conscious, following the finalized Surprise procedure.
- The +5-foot unarmed reach applies only during your turn and does not enlarge threatened space outside your turn.

- Once per round, after a hostile creature that was within your Blindsight at the start or end of its movement or teleportation finishes that movement, you may spend 1 Stamina to move up to 10 feet without provoking.

- Your movement is physical, follows a legal route, and must end closer to that creature than you began. If no legal destination is closer, you cannot activate the movement. The feature does not follow the creature through a teleport, grant its destination, or bypass total cover.
sections.summary: - Blindsight functions within 20 feet through the senses of your cultivated body. It does not see through total cover, identify a creature beyond the sense's range, or automatically reveal a creature protected by stronger supernatural concealment.

sections.name: Third and Fourth Coils
rules: - Striking Serpent: Once per turn on a hit, additional 1d8 Bludgeoning or Force, or 2d8 if the target is Grappled by you.
sections.summary: - Crushing Serpent: Count as one size larger while Grappling; at start of each turn deal Constitution modifier damage to a Grappled creature; drag at full Speed if no more than one size larger.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Third and Fourth Coils
rules: - While dragging no more than one Grappled creature that is no more than one size category larger than your actual or applicable functional size, your Speed is not halved by the ordinary Grapple drag rule. Terrain and other movement penalties still apply.

- Striking Serpent: Once per turn after any hit, add 1d8 Bludgeoning or Force to that hit's packet, or 2d8 if the target is currently Grappled by you when damage is applied. Choose damage type on use. It cannot critically multiply separately.
- The once-per-turn damage remains one total use across all attacks and turns normally reset it.
sections.summary: - Crushing Serpent: Functional size increases by one category only for initiating, maintaining, escaping, and dragging a Grapple. At the start of each of your turns, choose one creature currently Grappled by you; it takes Bludgeoning damage equal to Constitution modifier, minimum 0. This is not an attack and does not trigger hit riders.

facts: You hit a creature when it is Surprised, has not yet acted during the first round, you were Invisible to it, or you were Heavily Obscured from it.

items: It cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
Move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Apply Pressure-Point Strike without spending Stamina.
Gain Advantage on your next Stealth check before the end of your next turn.

sections.name: Assassination
sections.summary: Deal additional damage equal to 2d8 + your CL.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Assassination
rules: - “Has not yet acted during the first round” means the target has not taken a turn, action, Bonus Action, or Reaction after Initiative was rolled for that scene. A creature that acted before its first turn no longer qualifies under that clause.
- Invisible or Heavily Obscured status is evaluated from the target's perception, not globally. A creature that perceives you normally does not qualify under those clauses.
- The additional 2d8 + CL is one damage packet of the triggering attack's damage type unless that attack has multiple types, in which case choose one type dealt by it.

- The movement occurs after the hit, is granted movement, and does not provoke. The free Pressure-Point Strike spends no Stamina but still requires its save, uses its normal effect, and cannot exceed once per turn.
- Advantage on the next Stealth check is expended on that check and expires at the end of your next turn.
sections.summary: - Check the trigger at the moment the attack hits. Satisfying more than one listed circumstance does not multiply the benefit.

facts: You hit with an unarmed strike.

sections.name: Pressure-Point Strike
outcomes: It cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
rules: - No Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Speed reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn.
- Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of its next turn.
- Disadvantage on its next Concentration saving throw before the start of its next turn.
- It cannot speak above a whisper until the start of its next turn.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Pressure-Point Strike
rules: - The effect can apply to nonhumanoid anatomy through an equivalent vulnerable function unless an explicit immunity blocks that exact impairment.

- A target unable to speak above a whisper can communicate quietly, but cannot produce a command, shout, projected voice, audible activation, or verbal component that explicitly requires clear speech beyond its space. A rule that functions with whispers remains usable.
- Each named effect from you does not stack with itself. Reapplication refreshes the duration or next-roll expenditure.
- On a successful save, only Reaction denial applies. The free use from Assassination still observes Pressure-Point Strike's once-per-turn limit.
sections.summary: - Choose the failed-save effect after the target fails unless the table requires declarations before saves; record the choice and duration. These are temporary physical disruptions, not Injuries or permanent meridian damage.

sections.name: Shadow Afterimage
ordered: Create one Shadow Afterimage. You may maintain only one at a time.
sections.summary: Create one Shadow Afterimage. You may maintain only one at a time.

sections.name: Afterimage Statistics
rules: - Hit Points: 1
- Speed: 30 feet
- Immunities: Poison and Psychic
- Size: Your size
- Source CL: Your CL

The Afterimage cannot attack, deal damage, activate items, or use cultivation features. It acts immediately after your turn and follows your mental commands. It can Move, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Hide, Help, gesture, produce faint sounds, or manipulate an unattended object weighing no more than 5 pounds.
You may see and hear through it while within 300 feet.
sections.summary: - AC: 13 + Proficiency Bonus

sections.name: Shadow Exchange
ordered: Swap spaces with your Afterimage if both spaces are valid and no spatial lock separates them.
The Afterimage is destroyed at 0 Hit Points, when the duration ends, or when you create another.
rules: The Afterimage is destroyed at 0 Hit Points, when the duration ends, or when you create another.
sections.summary: Swap spaces with your Afterimage if both spaces are valid and no spatial lock separates them.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Shadow Afterimage
rules: - You choose one listed action for it when its turn begins without spending an action. It can move before or after that action. If you issue no command, it takes Dodge and remains where it is. The source prints no command range; no added distance limit applies while you are on the same plane and direct control is not blocked.
- Help follows the normal Help action and requires the Afterimage to be in a legal position to assist. It cannot grant help based on knowledge, strength, tools, or physical force it does not possess.
- Hide uses its own Stealth check with a modifier equal to your Stealth modifier, because no independent abilities are printed. It cannot become more physically real by Hiding.

- Seeing and hearing through it within 300 feet is simultaneous with your own senses unless a Source Rule says otherwise. It does not grant special senses, perfect memory, or line of effect from your body.

- Manipulating an unattended object is limited to 5 pounds, ordinary object interactions, and the Afterimage's space and reach. It cannot attack with, activate, consume, attune, steal a worn object, or use a cultivation item.

- Shadow Exchange is spatial movement. Both spaces must be legal for the arriving body or Afterimage, on the same plane, within 60 feet, and connected by a route not blocked by a spatial lock. Pay cost and action on a failed exchange and use Failed Spatial Movement.
- At 0 Hit Points the Afterimage is destroyed. Damage does not transfer to you. Creating another immediately ends the prior one, and no remains or materials persist.
sections.summary: - The Afterimage is a projected Body Asset and visual-auditory decoy, not a creature, Complete Soul, Companion, independent person, or duplicate of your body. It occupies its space but has no physical mass except for the printed object manipulation.

items: Ignore nonmagical difficult terrain.
Gain Advantage on checks to Hide.
Gain a Climb Speed equal to your walking Speed while at least one hand is free.
A creature cannot make an Opportunity Attack against you while you are Invisible to it or Heavily Obscured from it.
groups.lead: While in Dim Light, Darkness, mist, smoke, or an area that is Lightly or Heavily Obscured:

sections.name: Silent Step
rules: Dim Light alone does not prevent Opportunity Attacks from a creature that can see you normally.
sections.summary: Gain proficiency in Stealth. If already proficient, gain a +2 bonus to Stealth checks.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Silent Step
rules: - Determine Dim Light, Darkness, mist, smoke, and obscuration from the current scene. Dim Light grants the listed terrain and Hide benefits but does not by itself block sight or Opportunity Attacks from a creature that sees normally in it.

- The Climb Speed requires at least one functioning free hand for the entire climb. If that hand becomes occupied or disabled, finish the current movement in the nearest legal supported space or begin falling as normal.

- Opportunity Attack protection is evaluated separately for each observing creature at the instant you leave its reach. You are protected only if Invisible to that creature or Heavily Obscured from it.

- Ignoring nonmagical difficult terrain does not permit movement through solid objects, occupied hostile spaces, supernatural Fields, or cultivation-created terrain unless those are independently legal.
sections.summary: - If you already have Stealth proficiency, the +2 is a fixed miscellaneous bonus. It is gained once from this feature and does not multiply with repeated proficiency grants.

items: You are Invisible.
Gain Advantage on Stealth checks.
Gain a Climb Speed equal to your walking Speed.
Move through hostile creature spaces as difficult terrain.
Create a Shadow Afterimage when the feature activates without paying its cost.
Shadow Afterimage does not expire while Vanishing Flesh remains active.

sections.name: Vanishing Flesh
rules: When you make an attack or activate a harmful feature, you become visible until the end of the current turn, then become Invisible again if the duration remains.
The first time you hit during each of your turns, deal an additional 3d6 damage of the attack's type.
A creature capable of perceiving Invisible creatures can target you normally.
sections.summary: For the duration:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Vanishing Flesh
rules: - Moving through hostile spaces treats them as difficult terrain. You cannot end movement in another creature's space and this permission does not bypass a physical barrier.

- The free Shadow Afterimage appears in a legal unoccupied space within 15 feet when the feature activates. It follows the normal Afterimage rules, can still be destroyed, and ends when Vanishing Flesh ends unless another valid duration would end it sooner.

- Making an attack or activating a harmful feature makes you visible immediately before its first attack roll, save, or harmful resolution and keeps you visible until the end of the current turn. All creatures can perceive that visible state normally. If the duration remains, Invisibility resumes at the end of the turn without an action.
- A harmless movement, defensive feature, Hide action, object interaction, or purely diagnostic effect does not reveal you unless its own rule says otherwise.
- The 3d6 additional damage applies to the first hit during each of your turns, not each attack type or target. Use the triggering attack's chosen damage type.
- A creature with a legal means to perceive Invisible creatures ignores only the Invisibility-based targeting restriction; other cover, concealment, Stealth, and defenses remain.
sections.summary: - This is a temporary Body transformation creating supernatural concealment. Invisibility does not make you hidden automatically; Stealth and detection resolve normally.

sections.name: Body Crosses Heaven
rules: Once during each of your turns, after moving at least 30 feet before hitting with an unarmed strike, spend 2 Stamina. The attack deals an additional 4d8 Force damage, and the target makes a Strength saving throw.
- Failed Save: Push it up to 30 feet in a direction you choose and knock it Prone.
- Successful Save: Push it 10 feet.
If it collides with a solid surface, it and the surface each take additional Bludgeoning damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
sections.summary: Gain a permanent Fly Speed equal to your walking Speed and Hover while conscious.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Body Crosses Heaven
rules: - For the once-per-turn attack, count 30 feet of actual movement before the hit during that turn. Teleportation does not add traveled distance. The 2-Stamina cost is declared after the hit and before rolling the 4d8 Force damage.
- The 4d8 is part of the triggering attack's damage packet. Then the target makes the Strength save.

- On failure, choose a legal direction and move the target up to 30 feet along a direct trajectory; on success, push it 10 feet directly away from you. Movement stops at the first surviving solid barrier.

- A collision occurs once when the forced movement is stopped early by a solid surface. The target and that discrete surface each take one Bludgeoning damage packet equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Another creature is not a “solid surface” for this clause unless its own rule expressly functions as one.
- The collision damage does not trigger this feature again, create an Injury, or grant additional forced movement.
sections.summary: - The permanent Fly Speed and Hover function while conscious and derive from your current walking Speed. Losing consciousness removes Hover and causes falling unless another effect supports you.

facts: You hit with an unarmed strike after moving at least 10 feet during the current turn.
lossy: allowlist: results not directly after their save/attack
sections.name: Heaven-Kicking Leg
outcomes: Move the target up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, horizontally, vertically, or both, and it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. If unsupported afterward, it falls.
rules: A creature more than two sizes larger than you has Advantage on this saving throw.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Heaven-Kicking Leg
rules: - Declare after the unarmed strike hits and spend Stamina before the Strength save.

- On failure, choose an unoccupied legal destination within 15 feet of the target's starting space and visible to you. The target travels along the shortest unobstructed physical trajectory, which may be horizontal, vertical, or diagonal. This is forced movement, not teleportation.
- If the full destination is blocked, move the target as far as legally possible along the selected trajectory. If unsupported, falling begins after the forced movement resolves.
- On success, push 5 feet horizontally and directly away from you. If no legal space exists, the target remains in place.
- “More than two sizes larger” means at least three size categories larger than you and grants Advantage only on this save.
sections.summary: - Count at least 10 feet of actual movement during the current turn before the hit. Forced movement can qualify only if you willingly accepted or directed it; teleportation does not count as traveled distance.

facts: A hostile creature you can see within 60 feet willingly moves at least 10 feet or teleports using its own feature.
sections.name: Pursuit Without Horizon
rules: If you end within unarmed reach, make one unarmed strike against it. The attack follows the Granted Attack rule.
sections.summary: Move up to your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. You may use Thousand-Mile Legs and Tread the Empty Sky without paying Tread's normal cost. You must end closer to the triggering creature.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Pursuit Without Horizon
rules: - A teleport qualifies only when activated by the hostile creature's own feature. Movement imposed by another creature, forced movement, or involuntary teleportation does not.

- After the trigger resolves, move up to your current Speed. Thousand-Mile Legs applies normally. If airborne, you may activate Tread the Empty Sky as part of this Reaction without its Stamina cost; this does not require another action.

- Your final space must be legally closer to the triggering creature by straight-line distance than your starting space. If no such legal space can be reached, move as close as possible; if no movement would end closer, the movement fails but the Reaction and Stamina are spent.
- The unarmed strike occurs after movement and only if the creature remains within reach. It follows the Granted Attack rule and cannot trigger another granted attack.
sections.summary: - The trigger resolves after the hostile creature completes the qualifying 10 feet of willing movement or its teleport resolves. Movement split into several segments can trigger once when the cumulative willing movement reaches 10 feet.

sections.name: Thousand-Mile Legs
rules: When you use Stomping Step, until the end of the turn you may move across liquids and vertical surfaces without falling during the movement, and ordinary nonmagical difficult terrain does not cost additional movement. If you end unsupported, you fall normally.

Once during each of your turns, after moving at least 20 feet before hitting with an unarmed strike, deal additional damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus and move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
sections.summary: Your walking Speed increases by 10 feet. Your long jump and high jump distances are tripled, and you do not require a running start.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Thousand-Mile Legs
rules: - Triple the final long-jump and high-jump distances after ordinary Strength calculations and before a feature that supplies a separate fixed jump distance. No running start is required.

- During Stomping Step, movement across liquid or a vertical surface is ordinary movement using your available Speed. You do not sink or fall during that movement. If unsupported when the turn ends, resolve falling normally.

- Ordinary nonmagical difficult terrain costs no extra movement only during that Stomping Step turn. A supernatural Field, Formation, Domain, spatial lock, or explicit movement prohibition retains its authority.

- For the once-per-turn strike rider, count actual distance traveled by voluntary movement during the current turn. Teleportation does not add traveled distance. After a qualifying hit, add Proficiency Bonus damage to the attack packet and take the 5-foot legal movement after the hit resolves.
sections.summary: - The 10-foot increase modifies your walking Speed and therefore any feature that explicitly derives a Speed from walking Speed. It does not directly increase a fixed climb, swim, burrow, or teleport range.

items: Gain a Fly Speed equal to your walking Speed.
Hover.
Your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from creatures at least 10 feet below you.
groups.lead: Until the end of the current turn:

sections.name: Tread the Empty Sky
rules: At the end of the turn, you remain suspended until the start of your next turn. If you do not use Tread the Empty Sky again before that turn ends and remain unsupported, you fall.
Effects explicitly preventing flight, sealing the surrounding air, suppressing Body Refining features, or imposing a spatial lock prevent this movement.
sections.summary: Once during each of your turns while airborne, spend 1 Stamina without using an action.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Tread the Empty Sky
rules: - Until the end of that turn, gain the printed Fly Speed and Hover. The flight uses movement normally and does not create extra movement beyond your remaining movement allowance.
- Creatures at least 10 feet below every part of your space cannot make Opportunity Attacks caused by this movement. Other creatures can.

- At the end of the activation turn, remain suspended in your current legal space until the start of your next turn. During that next turn, you may reactivate the feature once. If you do not reactivate before that turn ends and remain unsupported, you fall at the end of that turn.
- Suppression or an explicit flight prohibition immediately removes flight and suspension. A spatial lock blocks only the movement authority it expressly covers; it does not automatically damage you.
sections.summary: - Activate once during your turn while any part of your space is unsupported or airborne. Spending Stamina requires no action.

items: Use Constitution instead of Strength or Dexterity for attack and damage rolls.
You may use your Cultivation Attack Modifier.
It is integrated into Body Refining.
Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply.
Draw or sheath it as part of an attack.

sections.name: First Cut
rules: The weapon need not begin physically sheathed; Draw represents the first committed release.
sections.summary: The first time you hit with your Draw Weapon during each turn, provided you made no earlier attack that turn, deal additional Slashing or Force damage equal to Proficiency Bonus and move 5 feet without provoking.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Draw Weapon and First Cut
rules: - Drawing or sheathing it as part of an attack changes only its carried state; it does not create a free object interaction usable for another item. The weapon need not begin sheathed for any feature unless that feature expressly says so.

- First Cut qualifies only if the triggering hit is produced by the first attack roll you make during that turn. If that first attack misses, an attack was still made and no later hit that turn qualifies. A save-based technique or nonattack damage made before the attack does not by itself disqualify First Cut unless it includes an attack roll.

- Declare First Cut after the hit. Add Proficiency Bonus as Slashing or Force to the triggering packet, then move up to 5 feet without provoking along a legal route. The movement is optional, occurs after the hit resolves, and cannot pass through occupied spaces without another permission.

sections.summary: - Choose and record one weapon in the Draw Blade group. While wielding that weapon, Constitution replaces Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls, and you may use your Cultivation Attack Modifier. It is integrated into Body Refining and grants no Sphere, extra weapon, or additional attack.

ordered: Move 10 feet before the attack roll resolves, without provoking and without crossing solid barriers or occupied spaces.

Resolve the attack from your new position. If outside reach, it misses. If it misses while you remain within reach, make one Draw Weapon attack after it resolves. The attack follows the Granted Attack rule.
rules: Resolve the attack from your new position. If outside reach, it misses. If it misses while you remain within reach, make one Draw Weapon attack after it resolves. The attack follows the Granted Attack rule.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Empty-Scabbard Step
rules: - The route cannot cross a solid barrier or any occupied space and must end in a space you can occupy. If no movement is legal, you can remain in place; the feature is still spent.

- After movement, recheck the triggering attack's target, reach, line of effect, and any required facing or adjacency. If you are no longer a legal target, that attack misses without a roll. Otherwise make and resolve the triggering attack roll from the new geometry.

- If the triggering attack misses for any reason and you remain within current Draw Weapon reach of the attacker after it resolves, make one Draw Weapon attack against that attacker. The granted attack occurs after every effect of the miss that must resolve first, follows the Granted Attack rule, and cannot grant another attack.
- If the triggering attack is one attack within a Multiattack or Attack action, only that attack is affected. Later attacks can choose legal targets normally.

rules: Choose up to Proficiency Bonus creatures crossed or within 5 feet of the line. Make one Draw Weapon attack against each. On a hit, deal normal damage plus 6d8 Slashing or Force.
After all attacks, each hit creature makes a Constitution save.
- Failed Save: Speed 0 and no Reactions until the end of its next turn.
- Successful Save: Speed halved until the start of its next turn.

When the line intersects a blocking barrier, make one Draw Weapon attack against it before moving through. On a hit, deal normal damage plus 6d8. If destroyed, continue. If it survives, end in the nearest legal space before it. The barrier counts against maximum targets.
Each creature can be attacked once. Attacks follow the Granted Attack rule.
sections.summary: Move in a straight line without provoking, across liquids, vertical surfaces, and open air, and through hostile spaces. You cannot pass through total cover, sealed Formations, spatial locks, or a surviving barrier.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Heaven Divided Before Sound
rules: - You can cross liquids, vertical surfaces, open air, and hostile occupied spaces as printed, but cannot end in an occupied space. Total cover, a sealed Formation, spatial lock, or surviving solid barrier blocks further travel.

- Before moving, choose up to Proficiency Bonus eligible creatures crossed by or within 5 feet of the line. Resolve chosen creatures and blocking barriers in nearest-to-farthest order. Each creature can be attacked once.

- When the line reaches a blocking barrier, make one Draw Weapon attack against it before entering its space. On a hit deal normal damage plus 6d8 Slashing or Force. It counts against the Proficiency Bonus target maximum. If destroyed, continue; if it survives or the attack misses, end in the nearest legal space before it and ignore selected targets beyond it.

- When you reach each selected creature's position along the line, make one Draw Weapon attack. On a hit deal normal damage plus 6d8 Slashing or Force. These are granted attacks and cannot grant additional attacks.

- After all reachable attacks resolve, each creature hit by this activation makes one Constitution save. On failure its Speed becomes 0 and it cannot take Reactions until the end of its next turn. On success its Speed is halved until the start of its next turn.

- A creature hit several times through an unrelated rule makes one save for this activation. The line does not automatically sever limbs, cut space, destroy an undamaged permanent barrier, or ignore explicit higher-Source-CL movement authority.
sections.summary: - Select an unoccupied legal destination within 120 feet and declare the straight line from your current space to that destination. Spend the Action and 7 Stamina. The route is physical movement, not teleportation, and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.

rules: - The first Draw Weapon attack has Advantage.
- Speed becomes 0 until that attack resolves.
- On a hit, additional 3d8 Slashing or Force damage and no Reactions until the start of the target's next turn.
- Afterward, Speed is restored and you move up to half your Speed without provoking.
You may enter this posture once per round. Forced movement does not end it; voluntary movement does.
sections.summary: At the start of your turn, before moving or taking an action, enter Still-Water Posture until the end of the turn.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Still-Water Posture
rules: - While in the posture, current Speed is 0 until your first Draw Weapon attack of that turn resolves or the posture ends. Forced movement does not end it. Any willing movement, teleportation, or spatial relocation before that attack ends the posture immediately and grants none of its attack or follow-up movement benefits.
- The first Draw Weapon attack you make during the posture has Advantage. After it resolves, your Speed returns to its normal current value whether the attack hits or misses.

- On a hit, add 3d8 Slashing or Force to the triggering packet and prevent the target from taking Reactions until the start of its next turn. Then move up to half your restored Speed without provoking along a legal route.
- On a miss, no additional damage, Reaction denial, or follow-up movement occurs, but Speed is restored.
- If you never make the attack, Speed remains 0 until the end of the turn and the posture then ends. Actions that do not move you are legal while waiting to make the attack.
sections.summary: - At the start of your turn, before movement, an Action, Bonus Action, or another voluntary activation, choose whether to enter Still-Water Posture. Entering requires no action and is limited to once per round.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Immovable God
rules: - Lower-Source-CL immunity applies only to effects that directly push, pull, knock you Prone, or teleport you unwillingly. It does not prevent destruction of the surface, movement of a vehicle or world, Grappling, Restrained, or an effect that transforms your body unless it also performs one of the listed movements.

- Against equal or higher Source CL, use one opposed Cultivation Check per movement event. Success prevents that entire movement event; failure allows it to resolve normally. This check does not consume your Reaction.

- The granted strike triggers once during each of your turns after you have willingly moved at least 10 feet total. Select one creature whose space first became within your reach during that movement. A creature that remained within reach for the entire movement did not “enter” your reach. The strike resolves after the movement ends unless the route ends before the creature leaves your reach.

rules: - “Touching a supporting surface” includes standing, kneeling, sitting, bracing with a limb, or being physically anchored to a substantial surface. A creature carried entirely by another creature is not supported unless a feature says it can root through that carrier.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Sun-Chasing Line
rules: - Choose Piercing or Force for the activation. Each creature in the line makes one Dexterity save and is affected once. Damage uses one damage die of the integrated Bow, Constitution modifier once, and 4d8 of the chosen type.
- The line does not apply critical hits, attack-hit riders, ammunition riders, weapon mastery riders, or effects requiring a Bow attack to hit.

- Resolve targets and obstructions from nearest to farthest. Creatures do not stop the line. When the line reaches an object, barrier, structure, vehicle, or Formation Anchor, apply its damage once and double the final damage if the target is an eligible unattended or listed target.

- If that obstruction is reduced to 0 Hit Points or otherwise destroyed by this activation, the line continues. If it survives and physically blocks the line, creatures and objects beyond it are not affected.
- Worn, carried, wielded, piloted, or actively controlled objects are not unattended. A target belonging to several doubled categories receives the multiplier once.
- Half and Three-Quarters Cover apply normally unless the line's path physically bypasses that cover. Total cover from a surviving obstruction stops the line.
sections.summary: - Replace one attack of the Attack action and choose a point up to 120 feet away, creating a 5-foot-wide line from the Bow to that point. The line requires line of effect and is not a weapon attack.

facts: You are hit by an attack or fail a Dexterity or Constitution save against a damaging effect.
sections.name: Brood Substitution
ordered: Reduce damage by 4d8 + Constitution modifier, move 10 feet without provoking, and leave a swarm-shell in your original space until the start of your next turn.
sections.summary: Reduce damage by 4d8 + Constitution modifier, move 10 feet without provoking, and leave a swarm-shell in your original space until the start of your next turn.

sections.name: Swarm-Shell
rules: - Hit Points: 2 x CL
- Immunity: Poison and Psychic
- Vulnerability: Fire and Radiant
- Space: 5 feet; creatures move through as difficult terrain
sections.summary: - AC: Your Cultivation Save DC

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Brood Substitution and Swarm-Shell
rules: - Roll 4d8 + Constitution modifier once and reduce the triggering damage packet at the shared flat-reduction step. The feature does not turn a failed save into a success or remove non-damage consequences.

- After damage resolves, move up to 10 feet without provoking along a legal route. The movement is physical swarm displacement, not teleportation. Leave the Swarm-Shell in your original space only if that space is legal for the Asset.

- The Swarm-Shell is a projected Body Asset with the printed AC, Hit Points, Immunities, Vulnerabilities, and 5-foot space. It is stationary, takes no actions, grants no cover unless normal geometry does so, and lasts until the start of your next turn or until destroyed.
- Creatures can move through its space as difficult terrain but cannot end there unless they could normally share its space. Destroying it causes no damage, Brood loss, Injury, or effect on you.
- If movement fails, the damage reduction still applies and the Shell appears in your current space only when legal; otherwise no Shell is created.
sections.summary: - Declare after an attack hits you or after you fail the listed save, before triggering damage is applied. Spend the Reaction and 2 Brood.

items: It takes 3d8 Poison or Necrotic damage.
It cannot regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points until the start of its next turn.
The Infestation ends.

sections.name: Gnawing Infestation
rules: If not triggered, it repeats the Constitution save at the end of its turn, ending Infestation on a success.
sections.summary: When an Infested creature first spends Cultivation Points, takes Dash, willingly moves 15 feet, regains Hit Points, or gains Temporary Hit Points during its turn:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Gnawing Infestation
rules: - The event commits before Gnawing resolves. Cultivation Points remain spent, Dash remains taken, movement already completed remains, and healing/Temporary Hit Points are first gained, then the feature deals damage and imposes its prohibition.
- Deal 3d8 Poison or Necrotic using the Infestation's recorded type. The creature cannot regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points until the start of its next turn, and that Infestation ends.
- One turn can trigger one Infestation from you once. If no trigger occurs, the creature repeats the recorded Constitution save at the end of its turn and ends the Infestation on success.
- Forced movement, teleportation, involuntary falling, and Cultivation Point loss that is not spending do not satisfy the trigger. A 0-point activation is not spending Cultivation Points.
sections.summary: - During an Infested creature's turn, monitor the first qualifying event: spending Cultivation Points; taking Dash; accumulating 15 feet of willing movement; regaining Hit Points; or gaining Temporary Hit Points.

sections.name: Internal Brood
rules: At the start of your turn, spend 1 Brood to regain 1d8 + Constitution modifier Hit Points, increasing to 2d8 at CL11 and 3d8 at CL17. This requires no action, functions once per turn, and cannot heal you at 0 Hit Points.
sections.summary: Gain Resistance to Poison damage and Advantage against disease.

facts: You hit with an unarmed strike.
sections.name: Infesting Strike
ordered: Deal an additional 1d8 Poison or Necrotic damage. On a failed save, the target becomes Infested until the end of your next turn.
sections.summary: Deal an additional 1d8 Poison or Necrotic damage. On a failed save, the target becomes Infested until the end of your next turn.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Internal Brood and Infesting Strike
rules: - At the start of your turn, spend 1 Brood to restore the printed Hit Points. This uses no action, functions once per turn, and cannot operate at 0 Hit Points before CL18.
- The die scaling replaces the earlier die. Add Constitution modifier once, to a minimum of 0 Hit Points regained.
- Infesting Strike: After an unarmed-strike hit, spend 1 Brood, choose Poison or Necrotic, and add 1d8 to the hit once per turn. The target then makes one Constitution save.

- On failure create one Infested record until the end of your next turn. Record source, Source CL, damage type, trigger status, save DC, and expiration. A new Infestation from you refreshes rather than stacks unless CL14 capacity permits several different creatures.
sections.summary: - Poison Resistance and Advantage against disease use ordinary procedures. “Disease” includes effects explicitly tagged or described as diseases, not every Poison or corruption.

items: Regain Hit Points equal to Proficiency Bonus.
Gain 1 Brood.
Move 10 feet without provoking.
Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to twice Proficiency Bonus.
groups.lead: Once per round when an Infested creature takes Gnawing Infestation damage, choose one:

sections.name: Parasite Sovereignty
rules: Brood gained this way can exceed the ordinary gain limit, but this feature remains once per round.
sections.summary: Poison and Necrotic damage from this Subpath ignores Resistance. Maintain Infested creatures equal to Proficiency Bonus.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Parasite Sovereignty
rules: - Maintain Infested creatures up to Proficiency Bonus. When exceeding the limit, choose one existing Infestation to end or decline the new one.
- Once per round after one Infested creature takes Gnawing Infestation damage, choose one printed benefit.

- Healing restores Proficiency Bonus Hit Points and is self-generated Body Refining healing. Brood gain is direct and can bypass the ordinary gain limit but not maximum. Movement is up to 10 feet without provoking along a legal route. Temporary Hit Points equal twice Proficiency Bonus and follow the normal nonstacking rule.

- Several Infestations triggering in the same round grant one benefit total. The benefit occurs after Gnawing damage and its healing prohibition are applied; choosing healing therefore cannot restore Hit Points if that same target's trigger somehow made you subject to an applicable prohibition.
sections.summary: - Poison and Necrotic damage from this Subpath ignores ordinary Resistance, not Immunity or a superior defense expressly immune to penetration.

items: Resistance to all damage except Fire, Radiant, Psychic, and Void.
Move through creature spaces as difficult terrain.
Pass through openings as narrow as 1 inch.
Cannot be Grappled or Restrained by ordinary physical effects.
Gain 1 Brood at the start of each turn.
Maximum Brood +3.
Internal Brood can heal you at 0 Hit Points.

sections.name: Ten-Thousand Worm Demon Body
rules: If Internal Brood heals you at 0 Hit Points, regain the rolled amount, stand without movement, lose all remaining Brood, and end this transformation. This can happen once per activation.
sections.summary: For the duration:

sections.name: Brood Tide
rules: - Successful Save: Half damage, not Infested, and Speed reduced by 5 feet until the start of its next turn.
A creature already Infested when it fails immediately triggers Gnawing Infestation after Brood Tide, then gains a new Infestation.
sections.summary: - Failed Save: 8d8 Poison or Necrotic, Infested, and Speed reduced by 15 feet until the end of its next turn.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Ten-Thousand Worm Demon Body
rules: - Resistance excludes Fire, Radiant, Psychic, and Void. You can move through creature spaces as difficult terrain and through openings at least 1 inch wide, but must end in a legal space large enough for your current body unless another rule permits compression at the end.
- Ordinary physical Grapples and restraints cannot affect you. Supernatural, spatial, spiritual, conceptual, higher-Source-CL, or expressly swarm-binding effects use their normal procedures.
- Increase maximum Brood by 3 and gain 1 at the start of each turn as a direct gain.

- Internal Brood can function at 0 Hit Points once during each activation. When used, spend 1 Brood, regain the rolled amount, stand without movement if possible, lose every remaining Brood, and end the transformation. This replaces remaining at 0 but is not usable against instant death, total destruction, Erasure, or recovery prevention.

- Brood Tide: The 30-foot cone originates from you and requires line of effect. Choose Poison or Necrotic for the use. On failure deal 8d8, Infest, and reduce Speed by 15 feet until the end of the target's next turn. On success deal half, do not Infest, and reduce Speed by 5 feet until the start of its next turn.

- If a failed target was already Infested by you, resolve its existing Gnawing Infestation immediately after Brood Tide damage, end that old record, then create the new Infestation. This immediate trigger counts as Gnawing damage for Parasite Sovereignty and does not require one of the ordinary trigger events.
- A target can be affected once per use. The cone does not leave a persistent swarm, contaminate terrain, or create independent parasite creatures.
sections.summary: - This is a whole-body swarm transformation. Equipment is carried and merged or suspended under the transformation procedure; it does not fall into individual worms or create duplicates.

sections.name: Calamity Appraisal
rules: Learn its AC, whether Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution is highest and lowest, and whether it is above or below half maximum Hit Points.
Once per turn on a hit against it, deal additional damage equal to Proficiency Bonus.
sections.summary: At the start of your turn, choose one creature within 60 feet as Appraised until the start of your next turn.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Calamity Appraisal Record
rules: - Record identity, Source CL, known AC, highest and lowest among Strength/Dexterity/Constitution, half-Hit-Point band, and expiration.
- If two or more physical abilities tie for highest or lowest, learn every tied ability. You learn only whether current Hit Points are above or below half maximum, not exact Hit Points or maximum.

- Appraisal reads current observable combat structure. A higher-authority disguise, false body, Secret concealment, or anti-divination effect can produce a contest or block the information under its own rules.

- The additional damage equal to Proficiency Bonus applies once per turn on one hit against the currently Appraised target and uses the triggering attack's damage type unless you choose Force. It is part of that hit and cannot critically multiply separately.
sections.summary: - At the start of your turn after choosing Open Eyes, select one creature you can perceive within 60 feet. It becomes Appraised until the start of your next turn.

facts: A creature you can see makes an attack roll against you.
sections.name: Eye beneath the Skin
rules: If it misses, the attacker becomes Appraised until the end of your next turn, you move 5 feet without provoking, and it cannot gain Advantage against you merely by becoming unseen before your next turn.
sections.summary: Add Proficiency Bonus to AC against that attack.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Eye beneath the Skin
rules: - If the modified attack misses, resolve the printed benefits after the miss: Appraise the attacker until the end of your next turn, move up to 5 feet without provoking, and deny unseen-only Advantage until before your next turn ends.
- The movement is physical and follows legal-space rules. It cannot change whether the already resolved attack hit.
- If the attack still hits, none of the miss benefits occur. The Reaction and Stamina remain spent.

- The temporary Appraisal can coexist with the start-of-turn Appraisal at CL18 only when the feature's maintained-target limit permits it; before CL18, it replaces the prior Appraised target for overlapping duration unless the source explicitly permits more.
sections.summary: - Declare after a visible creature makes an attack roll against you but before the roll's success is announced. Spend the Reaction and 1 Stamina, then add Proficiency Bonus to AC against that attack only.

facts: Your Appraised Target moves, teleports, attacks, or activates a technique within 60 feet.

items: Blindsight 40 feet.
See in every direction and cannot be flanked.
Automatically notice visible creatures entering your reach.
Advantage against illusions and gaze effects.
Know when a visible creature begins casting, invoking, or circulating a technique, though not necessarily its identity.
groups.lead: While at least 4 Eyes are open:

items: Move 15 feet without provoking.
Make one unarmed strike if within reach.
Impose Disadvantage on one attack roll it makes.
Add Proficiency Bonus to one save you make against the triggering feature.

lossy: allowlist: header fact inside the body
sections.name: Hundred Eyes Open
rules: The attack follows the Granted Attack rule.
sections.summary: Choose one:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Hundred Eyes Open
rules: - Seeing in every direction prevents flanking benefits that rely only on facing or an unwatched side. It does not see through total cover or negate concealment beyond your senses.
- Automatically noticing a visible creature entering reach reveals that entry; it does not grant an Opportunity Attack or interrupt unless another rule supplies one.

- You know that a visible creature has begun casting, invoking, or circulating a technique when its activation becomes observable. You do not automatically learn the technique's name, target, cost, hidden mode, or result.
- The Reaction trigger occurs when the Appraised target commits movement, teleportation, an attack, or a technique activation within 60 feet. Choose one response and spend 1 Stamina.

- Movement occurs immediately after the trigger commits and before later effects when legally possible. A granted unarmed strike occurs before the triggering movement finishes or attack resolves if the target is currently within reach; it follows Granted Attack rules and does not automatically cancel the trigger.

- Imposing Disadvantage affects one attack roll from the triggering activation, chosen before that roll. Adding Proficiency Bonus affects one save you make against the triggering feature, chosen before that save is resolved.
- A trigger without an attack roll or save can still be answered by movement or the granted strike.
sections.summary: - The passive benefits function while at least 4 Eyes remain open. Closing below 4 makes them dormant immediately.

items: Unclouded Line: Ignore Disadvantage, Half Cover, and Three-Quarters Cover on one attack roll.
Piercing Appraisal: On a hit, additional 2d8 damage.
Exposed Meridian: When a Body Refining feature forces its identified lowest physical save, subtract 1d4 from that save.
Denied Escape: On a hit, no Reactions until the start of its next turn.
Read Resistance: The triggering attack ignores one Resistance revealed by the Appraisal; not Immunity.

sections.name: Read the Killing Line
sections.summary: Once per turn when targeting an Appraised creature, spend 1 Stamina and choose one:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Read the Killing Line
rules: - Unclouded Line: Declare before one attack roll. Remove Disadvantage from that roll and ignore Half and Three-Quarters Cover. Total cover, blocked line of effect, and an illegal target remain.
- Piercing Appraisal: Declare after a hit. Add 2d8 damage to that hit using one of the hit's damage types or Force.

- Exposed Meridian: Declare when one of your Body Refining features forces the physical save identified as the target's lowest. Subtract 1d4 from that save result after the roll. If several abilities tied for lowest, any tied save qualifies.
- Denied Escape: Declare after a hit. The target cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn; this does not cancel a Reaction already resolved.

- Read Resistance: Declare on an attack before damage is applied. Ignore one ordinary Resistance you actually learned through Appraisal or another explicit information source. This never ignores Immunity or an unconfirmed guessed Resistance.
- One use cannot combine modes. A miss after choosing an attack-dependent mode spends the Stamina and use unless the mode expressly declared on hit.
sections.summary: - Use once per turn while targeting an Appraised creature. Spend 1 Stamina and choose exactly one mode at the mode's required timing.

items: Truesight 120 feet and Blindsight 60 feet.
Cannot be Surprised.
Attack rolls against you cannot gain Advantage.
Maintain Appraised Targets equal to Proficiency Bonus.
Learn exact Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution save bonuses.
Once per turn on a hit against an Appraised Target, additional 4d8 Psychic or Force.
Read the Killing Line costs 0 Stamina once per turn.

sections.name: Thousand-Eyed Revelation
sections.summary: All Eyes open.

sections.name: Calamity Gaze
rules: - Successful Save: Half damage and Appraised until the start of your next turn.
A creature is affected once per use.
sections.summary: - Failed Save: 8d8 Psychic, Appraised for the duration, cannot become Invisible to you, and no Reactions until the start of its next turn.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Thousand-Eyed Revelation
rules: - Truesight 120 feet and Blindsight 60 feet replace lower ranges. “Attack rolls cannot gain Advantage” removes every Advantage source from attacks against you; Disadvantage still applies normally and can make the roll disadvantaged.

- Maintain Appraised targets up to Proficiency Bonus. Each record uses the normal Appraisal data plus exact Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution save bonuses. When exceeding the limit, choose a record to end.
- The once-per-turn 4d8 Psychic or Force rider applies to one hit against any Appraised target and replaces no other Appraisal rider.
- Read the Killing Line costs 0 Stamina for one use each turn. Additional legal uses, if another rule grants them, pay normal cost.

- Calamity Gaze: The cone originates from you and requires line of effect. Each creature is affected once per use. On failure it takes 8d8 Psychic, becomes Appraised for the transformation's remaining duration, cannot become Invisible to you, and loses Reactions until the start of its next turn. On success it takes half and is Appraised only until the start of your next turn.

- “Cannot become Invisible to you” means Invisibility does not make that creature invisible to your senses; it does not dispel Invisibility for other observers. A superior Source CL concealment can contest this authority under its own rule.
sections.summary: - Activation opens every Eye to your current maximum and overrides the ordinary start-of-turn choice for the duration. Suppression can lower the effective maximum and closes excess Eyes first.

items: Perfect Edge: Additional 4d8 Slashing or Force and reduce AC by 1 until your next turn.
Perfect Spine: Temporary Hit Points equal to 2 x Proficiency Bonus + Constitution modifier; cannot be pushed, pulled, or knocked Prone until your next turn.
Perfect Reed: Move 20 feet without provoking and through hostile spaces as difficult terrain.
groups.lead: Once per turn on a melee hit, choose one:

sections.name: Body Beyond the Hammer
rules: - You cannot be Disarmed by an ordinary effect.
- Unarmed strikes and integrated melee weapons count as adamantine.
- Immune to ordinary effects permanently breaking, rusting, warping, corroding, or dulling your body or integrated weapons.
- When an effect would destroy or permanently deform a limb, take 4d10 Force damage instead and the limb remains functional. This damage cannot be reduced by this Subpath.
Each option can be selected only once per turn.
sections.summary: All three Forms are active simultaneously.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Body Beyond the Hammer
rules: - Ordinary Disarm immunity and immunity to ordinary permanent breaking, rusting, warping, corrosion, or dulling protect your body and current Tempered Weapon. They do not restore an item already destroyed, protect another creature's weapon, or override artifact, divine, Secret, Foundation, Method, Immortal, or explicit equal- or higher-Source-CL authority.
- Unarmed strikes and the Tempered Weapon count as adamantine for rules that recognize that material. This does not change their damage type or grant an item property not printed here.

- When a Source Rule would destroy or permanently deform one physical limb, natural-weapon structure, or equivalent reconstructable appendage, replace only that anatomical result with 4d10 Force damage and keep the structure functional. This replacement does not apply to conceptual erasure, complete bodily destruction, Foundation destruction, or an effect that does not target anatomy.

- The replacement damage cannot be reduced by Thousand-Fold Steel Body, including Spine Form, Spine Quench, or Perfect Spine. Other independent legal defenses can interact unless the original Source Rule says otherwise. Other nonanatomical consequences of the triggering effect still resolve.
- Once per turn after one melee hit, choose one Perfect result. This use is separate from Folded Edge, Hidden Spine and can coexist on the same hit.
- Perfect Edge: Add 4d8 Slashing or Force and reduce AC by 1 until the start of your next turn. It refreshes, not stacks with, this Subpath's other AC reduction.

- Perfect Spine: Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus + Constitution modifier and become immune to physical push, pull, and Prone until the start of your next turn. It does not block teleportation or voluntary movement.
- Perfect Reed: Move up to 20 feet without provoking. You can pass through hostile spaces as difficult terrain but cannot end in an occupied space or pass through a solid obstruction.
- Each Perfect option can be selected at most once during the same turn even if another rule would permit another Perfect choice.
sections.summary: - All three Forms are active simultaneously and no start-of-turn Form choice is required.

sections.name: Body Forged in Three Forms
ordered: Your body and a melee weapon currently benefiting from this Subpath's weapon-integration feature count as smithing tools only for maintaining, sharpening, cleaning, or repairing your own weapons and armor during rest or downtime. This does not replace Blacksmith proficiency for crafting.
rules: Your body and a melee weapon currently benefiting from this Subpath's weapon-integration feature count as smithing tools only for maintaining, sharpening, cleaning, or repairing your own weapons and armor during rest or downtime. This does not replace Blacksmith proficiency for crafting.
sections.summary: Gain the Tempering Forms.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Tempered Weapon Integration and Smithing Use
rules: - While wielding the Tempered Weapon, Constitution replaces Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls, you may use your Cultivation Attack Modifier, and it is integrated into Body Refining. Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply through their printed integrated-weapon interface. This grants no proficiency, Sphere, talent, duplicate weapon, or extra attack.
- The Tempered Weapon can be changed through the same 10-minute procedure. A destroyed, lost, or unwielded weapon provides no integration benefit until recovered or replaced.

- Your body and current Tempered Weapon count as smithing tools only for maintaining, sharpening, cleaning, or repairing your own weapons and armor during a rest, Full Cultivation Session, or downtime. This supplies the tool object but not Blacksmith proficiency, formulas, materials, facility authority, or permission to craft a new item.
- This paragraph repairs an explicit missing dependency in the source and does not alter any printed damage die, cost, range, limit, or tier.
sections.summary: - The source references this Subpath's weapon-integration feature without printing its record. To make the referenced function executable, choose one melee weapon you are proficient with when you finish a Full Cultivation Session or spend 10 minutes tempering it against your body. It becomes your Tempered Weapon until you choose another.

items: Reduce target AC by 1 until the start of your next turn.
Prevent Reactions until the start of its next turn.
Deal an additional 2d8 Slashing or Force damage.
Deal double damage to an unattended object, temporary barrier, vehicle, structure, or Formation Anchor.
groups.lead: Once per turn when you hit while Edge Form is active, choose one:

sections.name: Folded Edge, Hidden Spine
rules: The AC reduction does not stack with itself.
sections.summary: Your Body Refining melee attacks ignore ordinary Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Folded Edge, Hidden Spine
rules: - Once per turn after hitting while Edge Form is active, choose exactly one printed result. This is separate from Edge Form's Proficiency Bonus damage and can be applied to the same hit.
- AC reduction begins after the hit resolves and lasts until the start of your next turn. Reapplication refreshes duration and does not stack with itself.
- Reaction denial lasts until the start of the target's next turn and does not cancel a Reaction already spent.
- The 2d8 Slashing or Force is part of the triggering hit's packet and cannot critically multiply separately.

- Against an eligible unattended object, temporary barrier, vehicle, structure, or Formation Anchor, calculate the triggering hit's final damage under ordinary modifiers and then double that hit's damage once. The doubling does not apply to later damage packets or world-scale terrain that is not a legal target.
- A target cannot receive several choices from one use even if several effects would be legal.
sections.summary: - Body Refining melee attacks ignore ordinary Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing. “Ordinary” excludes Immunity, artifact defenses, divine authority, Secret protections, Immortal defenses, and an explicit equal- or higher-Source-CL rule that cannot be bypassed.

items: Edge Quench: Your next melee attack before the end of your next turn deals an additional 2d8 Slashing or Force damage.
Spine Quench: Reduce triggering damage by 2d8 + Constitution modifier.
Reed Quench: After damage resolves, move 15 feet without provoking.

sections.name: Quench the Impact
rules: The selected form remains until the start of your next turn.
sections.summary: Change your active form immediately and apply its Quench benefit:

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Quench the Impact
rules: - At CL3–13, the selected Form replaces the current active Form. At CL14+, use the feature's two-Form replacement rule. Selecting a Form already active is legal and still grants its Quench benefit.

- Edge Quench: After the triggering damage resolves, record one charge. Your next melee attack before the end of your next turn adds 2d8 Slashing or Force to its damage on a hit. A new Edge Quench refreshes rather than stacks with an unused charge.

- Spine Quench: Reduce the triggering packet by 2d8 + Constitution modifier at the shared damage-reduction step. This is separate from Spine Form's first-packet reduction and can apply to the same packet if both are available.

- Reed Quench: After the triggering damage resolves, move up to 15 feet without provoking along a legal route. The movement occurs even if final damage became 0, but not if the damage event was canceled before it existed.
- Changing Forms is prospective. It does not retroactively alter the triggering attack roll, percentage modifiers, damage type, or another event already resolved.
sections.summary: - Declare when qualifying hostile damage would be applied to you, after percentage modifiers are known but before Hit Points are reduced. Spend the Reaction and 1 Stamina, choose one Form, and make it active immediately until the start of your next turn.

items: Edge additional damage becomes twice Proficiency Bonus.
Spine damage reduction becomes twice Proficiency Bonus.
Reed movement becomes 10 feet.

sections.name: Ten Thousand Reforgings
sections.summary: Maintain two different Tempering Forms simultaneously. When using Quench the Impact, replace one or both active forms but apply only one Quench benefit.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Ten Thousand Reforgings
rules: - When you use Quench the Impact, choose one Quench benefit. You may replace one active Form with another, replace both active Forms with the other two-Form combination, or retain the current pair. Forms must remain different.
- Applying one Quench benefit does not apply the benefit of the second newly selected Form. Its normal Form benefit becomes active prospectively.

- Edge Form's once-per-turn damage becomes twice Proficiency Bonus. Spine Form's first-packet reduction becomes twice Proficiency Bonus. Reed Form's once-per-turn movement becomes 10 feet. These replace, rather than add to, their earlier numerical values.
- If effective CL suppression removes this feature, retain one legal active Form chosen by you and make the second dormant until access returns or the next start-of-turn choice.
sections.summary: - Choose two different active Forms at the start of each turn. Each Form keeps its own limit and benefit.

facts: A hostile creature crosses your Guarded Threshold.
sections.name: Guardian at the Gate
ordered: Make one unarmed strike or melee weapon attack against it before it completes the crossing.
its movement ends in the nearest legal space before the threshold, its Speed becomes 0 until the end of the turn, and it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
A creature can trigger this only once during the same movement. The attack follows the Granted Attack rule.
outcomes: Its movement ends in the nearest legal space before the threshold, its Speed becomes 0 until the end of the turn, and it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
rules: A creature can trigger this only once during the same movement. The attack follows the Granted Attack rule.
sections.summary: Make one unarmed strike or melee weapon attack against it before it completes the crossing.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Guardian at the Gate
rules: - Make exactly one unarmed strike or melee weapon attack against the crossing creature. The attack follows the Granted Attack rule.

- On a miss, the crossing continues. On a hit, finish the attack and its damage, then place the creature in the nearest legal space on the side from which it attempted to cross. End that movement, set every Speed to 0 until the end of the current turn, and deny Reactions.

- If several spaces are equally near, you choose one that does not place the creature across the threshold. If no legal space exists, use Failed Spatial Movement with the status quo on the originating side.

- One creature can trigger Guardian at the Gate only once during one continuous movement, even if its space intersects the threshold repeatedly. A later separate movement can trigger again if you have a Reaction.
sections.summary: - Trigger immediately before an ordinary or forced movement segment would complete a crossing. Teleportation, phasing, appearing, or a threshold being placed across a stationary creature does not trigger this Reaction.

sections.name: Heaven's Closed Gate
rules: A hostile creature attempting to cross makes a Strength or Charisma saving throw, its choice.
- Failed Save: Movement ends at the boundary, Speed becomes 0 for the turn, it takes 4d8 Force damage, and cannot attempt to cross again that turn.
- Successful Save: It crosses, but the boundary is difficult terrain for that movement.
A hostile teleport or phase attempt instead uses the Cultivation Check and Failed Spatial Movement rules.
Ranged attacks and effects crossing the boundary grant Three-Quarters Cover to targets inside.

Four visible anchor posts appear at cardinal points. Each has AC equal to your Cultivation Save DC, Hit Points 3 x CL, Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, and Force, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic. Destroying two reduces protection to Half Cover; destroying all four ends the Gate.
You may maintain only one Heaven's Closed Gate.
sections.summary: A vast threshold manifests around the boundary. You and chosen allies cross freely.

sections.name: Normalized Procedure — Heaven's Closed Gate
rules: - Choose any number of willing allies you can perceive when activating the Gate. You and those allies cross freely. A creature not chosen is treated according to its current hostility and the feature's normal crossing procedure.

- The boundary is the cylinder's vertical outer surface and top. A hostile creature crosses when ordinary movement would take any part of its space from outside to inside or inside to outside through that surface.

- On a failed Strength or Charisma save, place the creature in the nearest legal space on the side where the attempt began, deal 4d8 Force damage, set Speed to 0 for the turn, and prevent another crossing attempt that turn. On success, it crosses; movement through the boundary costs double as difficult terrain for that crossing.
- Hostile teleportation, phasing, and other spatial movement across the boundary use one Cultivation Check and Failed Spatial Movement instead of the Strength or Charisma save.

- Three-Quarters Cover applies only to a target inside when an attack or cover-sensitive effect originates outside and crosses the boundary. Destroying two posts changes this to Half Cover. Destroying all four ends the complete Gate, including crossing restrictions and spatial checks.
