sections.name: HEAVEN AND EARTH BECOME THE DIAGRAM
rules: Timing Detail: Action, or 1 minute if used as a prepared ritual
You unfold the World-Array Scripture. For a short time, the surrounding world is treated as if it had always been built from your Nodes, Gates, and Flow Lines.
Choose five World Laws from the list below. The area becomes a World Array with those laws.
Law of the Eye: You always know the location of creatures inside the area unless hidden by a Secret technique or stronger effect. You do not learn their thoughts, statistics, or secrets.

Law of the Gate: Keyed allies may teleport up to 60 feet inside the area as a Bonus Action. Hostile creatures attempting to teleport inside, out of, or through the area must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or the teleport fails.

Law of the Locked Road: Hostile creatures treat the entire area as Difficult Terrain. Once per round when a hostile creature moves more than 10 feet, you may force it to make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, its movement ends.

Law of the Hidden Road: Keyed allies have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and may Hide while Lightly Obscured inside the area. Hostile creatures have Disadvantage on checks made to find your Nodes, Eyes, hidden Gates, or concealed keyed allies.

Law of the Killing Line: Once during each of your turns, choose a line up to 120 feet long inside the area. Hostile creatures on that line make Dexterity saving throws. A creature takes 8d8 Force damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success.

Law of the Returning Breath: Once per round when a keyed ally inside the area is reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, it instead drops to 1 Hit Point and is moved up to 30 feet to a legal space inside the area. A creature can benefit from this law only once per use of the inheritance.

Law of the Suppressed Current: The first time each round a hostile creature spends CP inside the area, it must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the CP is spent and the effect fails. On a success, the effect works, but the creature cannot benefit from this law again until the start of its next turn.

Law of the Shattered Formation: Choose one non-Secret Formation, Barrier, Domain, or prepared magical battlefield effect inside the area. Make a Formation Check against its creator’s save DC. On a success, suppress it while this inheritance lasts. On a failure, suppress one of its minor benefits until the end of your next turn.

Law of the Nine Palaces: Divide the area into up to nine visible or invisible palaces. Once per turn, when a hostile creature crosses from one palace into another, it must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, choose whether it becomes lost, slowed, or exposed until the start of your next turn. A lost creature cannot willingly move closer to a chosen objective. A slowed creature’s Speed is halved. An exposed creature cannot benefit from Invisible or Half Cover.

Law of the World Anchor: Create nine Anchors. Each Anchor has AC 19, Hit Points equal to 15 × your Proficiency Bonus, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. The World Array does not require Concentration while at least five Anchors remain. If fewer than five remain, you must Concentrate to maintain it. If fewer than three remain, it collapses.
While this inheritance lasts, you may Pulse one Pattern Layer or World Law once during each of your turns without using an action.

Limits: This inheritance does not permanently create territory, erase a kingdom, make you omnipotent, automatically kill creatures, rewrite the past, or suppress a stronger Secret Inheritance without a contested scene. It does, however, allow a Formation master to fight like a sect defending its ancestral mountain.

This is not mind control and does not command plants. A hostile guardian, oath-bound spirit, or starving beast may still refuse.

sections.summary: When you spend at least 1 day surveying a wilderness region, mountain valley, sect field, forest, marsh, or underground route, make a Gathering Check.

sections.name: Name-the-Harvest Mandate - Unique, Realm Evolution
rules: For the next hour, you have Advantage on checks to find, approach, harvest, preserve, and transport that material from the site.
If the site does not contain that material, the use is wasted.
This is not divination strong enough to invent treasure. It is a Nascent Soul gatherer’s mandate aligning attention, luck, field memory, and practiced instinct toward the chosen harvest.
sections.summary: Once per Long Rest, when you successfully Read the Sign for a Resource Site, you may name one material type that the site could plausibly contain.

facts: CL 17+, Heavenly Material Recognition, Sovereign Clean Cut, GM approval, and a lost gatherer scripture or world-root pact

sections.name: One Leaf, One World Harvest Scripture
rules: You may attempt to harvest a Secret material without destroying the source, even when ordinary doctrine says the source must be uprooted, slain, mined out, or consumed entirely.
This requires a major scene, not a routine check.
Make a Gathering Check against a DC set by the GM, usually 30 or higher.
On success, gain the Secret material and preserve the source.
On success by 5 or more, the Secret material is Perfect.
On Natural 1, the source rejects the harvest. Resolve a story consequence such as a guardian awakening, secret-realm collapse, curse mark, oath debt, sect alarm, beast pursuit, or heavenly omen.
This inheritance should be rare. It changes how sects think about priceless materials.
sections.summary: “Do not take the garden. Take the moment in which the garden offers one leaf.”

sections.name: Pill-Hall Supply Chain - Route
rules: During downtime, a Pill Hall, Medicine Hall, or alchemical workshop supplied by you reduces waste, spoilage, and missing-ingredient delays.

If the Alchemy sphere’s Sect Pill Hall is present and you manage the supply chain, its Common and Uncommon production can continue with fewer interruptions, provided the GM agrees the region can support the ingredients.
This talent does not create ingredients and does not refine pills.
sections.summary: You can coordinate harvesters, carts, contracts, storage, guards, ledgers, pack beasts, river transport, and sect tribute for a pill hall or medicine market.

sections.name: Quick Field Harvest - Cut
rules: When harvesting this quickly, make the Gathering Check with Disadvantage unless you spend 1 CP or the source is already prepared, exposed, dead, or stabilized.

sections.summary: You can attempt Clean Harvest as an Action for Common materials or as 1 minute of work for Uncommon materials.

If an affected attack misses and one of the attacker’s allies is within 30 feet of the original target, the ammunition veers toward the nearest such ally. It loses Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage. If it had no such Resistance, it gains Vulnerability to the next instance of Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage it takes before the start of your next turn.

Augment 2 CP. You can apply Harden or Brittle to a creature. A creature affected by Harden gains Resistance to one of Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, chosen when you place the Mandate. A creature affected by Brittle loses one such Resistance, or takes extra damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus the next time it takes damage of the chosen type before the start of your next turn.

ordered: You create an area where weight obeys your Mandate.
Choose Light Field or Heavy Field.

Light Field. Creatures and unsecured objects in the area are half-weight. Creatures have Advantage on jumping checks and Disadvantage on checks to resist being pushed or pulled. Falling creatures descend at half speed and take half falling damage.

Heavy Field. The area is Difficult Terrain. Creatures have Disadvantage on jumping checks, cannot take the Dash action unless they succeed on a Strength saving throw at the start of their turn, and unsecured objects weigh twice as much.
As a Bonus Action on later turns, you may switch the field between Light and Heavy.

rules: Choose one direction: up, down, north, south, east, west, or toward a visible anchor point. Unsecured objects and creatures in the area fall in that direction until they strike a surface, exit the area, or reach the boundary.

A creature that can grab a fixed object may make a Dexterity saving throw to secure itself and avoid falling. Creatures with a fly speed may use their movement to resist as normal. When the effect ends, normal gravity resumes.

sections.name: The Edict That Names the World Again
rules: You speak an Edict that briefly renames one property of the battlefield.

All Armor Forgets Mercy. Willing allies’ armor and shields reduce incoming damage by your Proficiency Bonus + key ability modifier. Hostile armor and shields must save or lose magical AC bonuses until the end of your next turn.

All Weight Obeys My Palm. Choose up, down, inward, outward, or toward one visible point. Unsecured objects and creatures that fail a Strength saving throw fall or slide in that direction up to 60 feet, taking damage as appropriate if they collide.

All Voices Are Mine to Permit. Willing allies can speak, transmit commands, and use verbal techniques through noise, silence, or distance inside the area. Hostile creatures must save or be unable to speak clearly, use verbal components, or issue command words until the end of your next turn.

All Vessels Wake and Bow. Unattended objects up to Large size in the area animate until the end of your next turn and obey one simple command. Attended objects may save through their bearer. Magic items and artifacts may resist with opposed Cultivation Checks.

All Weakness Becomes Obvious. Until the end of your next turn, you and allies in the area know which of Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is lowest for each hostile creature you can perceive. The first saving throw each hostile creature makes against that ability before the duration ends has Disadvantage.

All False Nature Is Denied. Choose one ongoing enhancement, degradation, polymorph, item buff, weight change, speed alteration, false vigor, animated object, or similar property-changing effect on each hostile target in the area. Make one Imbuement Check against the highest relevant DC. On a success, suppress all chosen effects until the end of your next turn.

Failure or Resistance. A creature, artifact, sect treasure, Secret Inheritance, or superior Realm effect may resist with an opposed Cultivation Check. On a failed Edict against a superior effect, you take psychic or force damage equal to twice your Cultivation Level and cannot use this inheritance again until you complete a major cultivation session.

This inheritance does not permanently rewrite reality, create permanent sentience, forge artifacts, replace Talismans/Formations/Alchemy, or grant ownership of another cultivator’s soul-bound treasure. It is one impossible command, not a new world.

rules: The Edge Finds the Gap. sections.name: Serious Ingrained Toxin Stages
rules: Success: The poison stage decreases by 1. If it would decrease below Stage 1, the poison ends.
Failure: The poison stage increases by 1, to a maximum of Stage 4.
A creature cannot suffer more than one Serious Ingrained Toxin at a time.
Stage 1 - Bitter Channels. The target has Disadvantage on the first Cultivation Check it makes each day, and cannot reduce CP costs below their printed values.

Stage 2 - Numb Meridian Flow. The target’s maximum CP is reduced by your Proficiency Bonus, and it has Disadvantage on concentration saving throws. This maximum CP reduction ends when the poison ends.

Stage 3 - Foundation Corrosion. The target’s Hit Point maximum is reduced by your Cultivation Level, and the target regains only half as much CP from short-rest or scene-based recovery. This maximum Hit Point reduction ends when the poison ends.

Stage 4 - Life-Gate Closing. The target cannot regain CP above half its maximum CP, cannot gain Temporary HP, and has Disadvantage on death saving throws. If the target fails three daily saves while at Stage 4, it dies unless the GM decides the poison instead triggers a major cultivation injury, coma, sealed meridians, or story crisis.

facts: Core Formation Realm, Source Lock; Secret Inheritance

For 1 minute, the target is held by a simple source seal. A creature can force the target open, break the seal's hold, or move through the sealed section only by succeeding on a Strength (Athletics) check against your Source Save DC. The seal ends early if the target is destroyed.

This talent does not affect creatures, worn or carried items, magical locks, active formations, talisman seals, soul seals, oath seals, or structures larger than a 5-foot section unless the GM approves the target as simple enough for this talent.

sections.name: Anchor Gate
rules: Open a stable two-way gate between two Spatial Anchors you created on the same plane.
CL 20: 5 miles.

rules: Once per combat, when you draw a Concealed or Hidden weapon against a creature that did not know you had it, you may use Hidden Method without counting against your once-per-turn Weapon Method limit.
sections.summary: You have Advantage on checks to hide Concealed or Hidden weapons on your body.

facts: Expend Martial Focus and 5 CP or Stamina, depending on Path expression

items: you may apply one minor Weapon Method per turn without using your once-per-turn Weapon Method limit;
you may draw or stow one additional weapon each turn;
enemies in the aura have Disadvantage on checks made to disarm you;
when an enemy in the aura misses you with a melee attack, you may move 5 feet or change weapon grip;
once per round, when you reduce a creature's speed, prevent a reaction, or break a guard with a Weapon Method, you may regain Martial Focus.

sections.name: Court of Ten Thousand Weapons
rules: This court is martial discipline, not external qi projection unless the character's Path expression makes it qi-shaped.

sections.name: Empty Hand, Full Armory
rules: Once per short rest, when disarmed or apparently unarmed, you may draw, seize, or improvise a legal weapon as part of rolling initiative or as a Reaction when a hostile creature enters your reach.
sections.summary: You may treat an improvised object as a legal weapon if its shape reasonably matches a catalogue profile. It uses the nearest weapon's damage die and tags, but loses any exotic special effect unless the GM says the object can support it.

sections.name: Formation Weapon Drill
sections.summary: When you wield a Reach, Polearm, Staff, Fork, Halberd, or Long weapon, allies within 5 feet of you gain Advantage on ability checks or saving throws made to avoid being forcibly moved through your threatened area.

sections.name: Hook, Catch, and Turn
sections.summary: When you use Hooking Method, you may choose one additional result on a failed save if the weapon has both Hooking and Disarming, or both Flexible and Returning Line.

sections.name: Iron Against Iron
outcomes: The item is rattled, cracked, caught, or driven out of line. Until the start of your next turn, attacks made with that item suffer a -2 penalty.
rules: This does not destroy magic items or cultivation treasures unless the GM allows it.
sections.summary: When you use Breaking Method against a weapon, shield, or object held by a creature, the holder makes a Strength saving throw.

sections.name: Long Weapon Measure
rules: This does not stack with specialized Spear sphere interception unless a feature explicitly says so.
sections.summary: When you use a Reach weapon, creatures provoke opportunity attacks from you when they enter your reach, not only when they leave it. You may make only one such opportunity attack per round.

sections.name: Master of Strange Implements
rules: If you already had proficiency, choose one additional method tag for each selected weapon, approved by the GM.
sections.summary: Choose three Exotic weapons. You gain proficiency with them, and their Special property no longer imposes Disadvantage or mishap risk on ordinary attacks.

sections.name: One Weapon, Ten Thousand Forms
rules: While wielding it, you may treat it as having one additional weapon tag from Cut, Thrust, Guard, Hook, Bind, Sweep, Smash, Pin, Cast, or Hidden.
You may change this chosen tag when you finish a long rest or complete a 2-hour cultivation session.

rules: You establish a Domain where incomplete force is compelled toward completion.

items: Possessing Intruder: It is forced out of the Host into the nearest legal unoccupied space within 10 feet. It is visible to Spiritual Sense and cannot repossess that Host until the end of the scene. If it has no legal independent manifestation, it is sealed in a temporary spiritual outline adjacent to the Host until the end of your next turn and is Incapacitated during that time.

Extraplanar Spirit, Fiend, or Demon: It is banished from the current battlefield until the end of its next turn, then returns to the nearest legal space to where it departed. If its Source CL is at least 5 lower than yours and it is not anchored to the plane, it is instead expelled to its home plane for the scene.

Native Ghost, Undead Soul, or Restless Dead: It is Frightened of you and cannot willingly move closer to its Host, corpse, grave, or sustaining Anchor for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each turn.

Cursed or Contaminated Host: Suppress one ordinary possession, curse, or spiritual contamination affecting it until the end of your next turn. The Host may immediately repeat one save the effect normally permits, with Advantage.

rules: Choose any number of allies, Hosts, Intruders, Restless Dead, fiends, demons, undead spirits, possessions, curse Anchors, and hostile spirit Assets in the area. Each hostile chosen creature makes a Charisma saving throw.
sections.summary: You invoke the full authority of departure, rightful hosting, burial, and spiritual boundary.

items: Possessing Intruder: It is forced out of every Host in the area, cannot repossess those Hosts for the scene, and is either manifested in a legal space or sealed in a visible spiritual outline. require one hostile creature in the field to save against entry into the Far Constellation;
move one Near creature 20 feet by conceptual translation;
exchange the positions of two willing Near creatures;
use Make the Blow Far without spending Resonance;
use Collapse the Interval on yourself without spending Resonance.

sections.name: Rewrite the Constellation
sections.summary: Once on each of your turns, choose one:

items: make one weapon attack with a weapon you are proficient with;
use Mind Spike with maximum damage on its damage dice on a failed save;
activate one single-target Spirit Awakening technique of CL14 or lower, paying its normal Resonance cost.

sections.name: No Distance to the Chosen Edge
rules: If the target is in the Far Constellation and its Source CL is at least 5 lower than yours, ordinary movement, range, cover short of total sealed cover, and non-Secret escape cannot prevent the effect. Equal or higher conceptual, Boundary, Space, Void, Seal, Formation, divine, or artifact authority contests normally.
sections.summary: Once during the activation, choose one creature in the field that is Near to you or belongs to the Far Constellation. For one attack or single-target Spirit Awakening technique, the distance between you and that creature becomes 0 for range and reach while preserving legal line of effect.

sections.name: Make Sanctuary Unreachable
rules: - Hostile single-target effects lose it as a legal target.
- Area effects already placed still affect its actual space.
- It cannot make attacks or use hostile techniques while protected.
- It may move up to 20 feet toward another Near member without provoking.
A Secret execution, true-name effect, internal possession, effect already inside the creature, or higher-Source-CL authority can contest this sanctuary.
sections.summary: Once during the activation, use your Reaction when a Near creature would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, possessed, banished, or struck by a hostile effect. Until the start of that creature’s next turn, declare it Far from every hostile creature in the field.

sections.name: End of the World
rules: Using World Without Between leaves a visible or spiritually perceptible sign of your Permanent Price for the remainder of the scene.
sections.summary: When the Domain ends, every Near and Far designation created by it ends. Ordinary geometry resumes immediately. Creatures are not moved merely because their relations end.

sections.name: Gentle Knife
sections.summary: Choose one result:

sections.name: Ease Pain
ordered: Suppress one ordinary pain, fear symptom, despair symptom, or minor spiritual disturbance until the end of the scene. The underlying source remains and resumes afterward unless treated.
sections.summary: Suppress one ordinary pain, fear symptom, despair symptom, or minor spiritual disturbance until the end of the scene. The underlying source remains and resumes afterward unless treated.

sections.name: Take the Edge
ordered: The target gains Temporary Hit Points equal to Proficiency Bonus + Wisdom modifier and Advantage on its next saving throw against Frightened or Spiritual Pressure before the end of your next turn.
sections.summary: The target gains Temporary Hit Points equal to Proficiency Bonus + Wisdom modifier and Advantage on its next saving throw against Frightened or Spiritual Pressure before the end of your next turn.

sections.name: Lift the Tremor
rules: After resolving the chosen result, take Psychic damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. This damage cannot be reduced.
If Gentle Knife suppresses or ends an effect created by a meaningful hostile creature, you may gain 1 Mercy Scar instead of taking this damage.
sections.summary: End one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect, or allow the target to repeat one saving throw against an ordinary Charmed or Frightened effect.

sections.name: Diagnostic Incision
sections.summary: When you touch the target, you also learn whether its pain or disturbance is ordinary, Restricted, Forbidden, Secret, divine, artifact-level, cultivation-based, bodily, emotional, memory-based, identity-based, or possession-based. Protected causes can require a Cultivation Check.

facts: The receiving target is Resonance Marked by you, bears your Mercy Scar through a prior link, or is touching a Flayed Burden Anchor

sections.name: Give the Pain a Name
outcomes: Transfer the Mercy Scar to the target until the end of its next turn. Choose one expression appropriate to the burden:
The transfer fails. The target suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect, and the Scar remains where it was.
rules: Choose one Mercy Scar carried by you, a willing ally within 30 feet, or a Flayed Burden Anchor. Name its broad burden aloud: fear, pain, despair, contamination, possession-pressure, nightmare, curse-pressure, or another accurate category.
A willing receiving target accepts the transfer. An unwilling receiving target makes a Wisdom saving throw.
- impose one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect;
- impose Frightened until the end of its next turn if the Scar came from fear;
- reduce Speed by 10 feet and prevent Reactions if the Scar came from pain;
- impose Disadvantage on the next Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma save if the Scar came from spiritual contamination;
- suppress one source of healing or Temporary Hit Points until the end of its next turn if the Scar came from a curse or bodily wound.
At the end of the target’s next turn, the Scar returns to its prior bearer or Anchor unless another procedure receives it.
sections.summary: You can transfer a burden after defining what it is.

sections.name: Permanent and Protected Burdens
ordered: This feature cannot transfer a permanent injury, destroyed organ, complete curse, complete possession, memory deletion, identity severance, Foundation damage, Method damage, or Secret-Law harm unless a separate Source Rule expressly permits it. It may transfer one symptom or pressure expression from such harm for the printed duration.

sections.name: Named Relief
sections.summary: When a willing creature accepts a Mercy Scar from another willing creature, both gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. This can occur only once per scene for each creature.

facts: An ally within 30 feet takes damage, fails an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, or would gain a Mercy Scar, Nightmare Scar, spiritual contamination, possession effect, memory wound, or identity wound
sections.name: Painless Martyr
sections.summary: Choose one result.

sections.name: Divide the Blow
ordered: You take half the triggering damage, rounded down, and the ally takes the remainder. Damage type and bypass properties are preserved. Damage transferred to you this way cannot be reduced below your Proficiency Bonus unless the triggering damage was already lower.
sections.summary: You take half the triggering damage, rounded down, and the ally takes the remainder. Damage type and bypass properties are preserved. Damage transferred to you this way cannot be reduced below your Proficiency Bonus unless the triggering damage was already lower.

sections.name: Carry the Failure
ordered: The ally rerolls the triggering saving throw and must use the new result. You gain 1 Mercy Scar. If the reroll succeeds, the hostile source becomes Resonance Marked by you.
sections.summary: The ally rerolls the triggering saving throw and must use the new result. You gain 1 Mercy Scar. If the reroll succeeds, the hostile source becomes Resonance Marked by you.

sections.name: Catch the Wound
rules: If the source is equal or higher authority, make a Cultivation Check. On failure, you may still delay one symptom until the start of the ally’s next turn, but not the complete consequence.
sections.summary: Delay one ordinary possession, contamination, memory wound, identity wound, or permanent-injury consequence until the end of your next turn. You immediately gain 1 Mercy Scar. During the delay, the ally or another creature can heal, escape, exorcise, surrender, sever an Anchor, or perform another meaningful intervention.

sections.name: Martyr’s Limit
ordered: You cannot use Painless Martyr if doing so would force you above your Mercy Scar maximum unless you rupture a Scar first. If the feature would reduce you to 0 Hit Points, it still resolves; you fall unconscious afterward.
sections.summary: You cannot use Painless Martyr if doing so would force you above your Mercy Scar maximum unless you rupture a Scar first. If the feature would reduce you to 0 Hit Points, it still resolves; you fall unconscious afterward.

facts: One willing creature, or one restrained/unconscious creature whose current custodian lawfully permits emergency treatment
sections.name: Peel the Wound
rules: Success: Choose one result.
- Suppress: Suppress the effect for the scene.
- Extract: If the effect is ordinary and has lower Source CL, end it and gain 1 Mercy Scar.
- Expose: Reveal the effect’s Anchor, current host, transmission route, restoration condition, or one legal way to remove it.
Failure: The target gains Advantage on its next saving throw or Cultivation Check against the effect. You take Psychic damage equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus.
sections.summary: Choose one poison, disease, Charmed effect, Frightened effect, ordinary curse, ordinary possession, Nightmare Scar, Devoured Dream, spiritual contamination, or Spiritual Pressure package affecting the target. Make a Cultivation Check against the effect’s save DC. If it has no save DC, use 8 + source Proficiency Bonus + source key ability modifier.

items: AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
Hit Points: 4 × Proficiency Bonus
Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL
Immunities: Poison, Psychic, and ordinary bodily conditions
Duration: Until treated, destroyed, deliberately opened, or the burden is transferred

sections.name: Flayed Burden
rules: A Flayed Burden Anchor can hold one Mercy Scar. You can maintain a number of such Anchors equal to your Wisdom modifier, minimum one.

If an Anchor is destroyed without purification, resolve Escaped Burden Priority from the Procedure Addendum. Apply the first legal result; no additional penalty is invented. An equal-or-higher-authority effect also retains its own printed recovery and persistence rules.
sections.summary: When you Extract an effect, you may place the Mercy Scar into a prepared strip of cloth, paper skin, wax figure, surgical thread, spirit parchment, or other suitable vessel instead of carrying it personally. The vessel becomes a Flayed Burden Anchor:

items: Allies of your choice have Advantage on death saving throws and saves against Charmed, Frightened, possession, despair, pain, ordinary spiritual contamination, and ordinary memory or identity pressure.
Once on each of your turns, choose one ally in the aura. It regains 3d8 + Wisdom modifier Hit Points or repeats one save against an effect listed above.
A willing creature in the aura can transfer one ordinary pain, fear, Spiritual Pressure effect, Nightmare Scar, Mercy Scar, or minor contamination to an empty Flayed Burden Anchor as an Action.
Hostile creatures cannot force a willing ally to reveal information through pain, fear, or ordinary spiritual coercion while that ally remains in the aura.

sections.name: White Room Mercy
sections.summary: Create a silent 30-foot aura of white spiritual pressure centered on you. The aura is a Spirit Awakening field with your Source CL. Sound can exist within it, but cries of pain, panic, and involuntary confession do not travel beyond its boundary unless you permit them.

sections.name: Once During the White Room — Impossible Triage
sections.summary: When a creature in the aura would die, suffer a permanent wound, lose a memory, have its identity altered, become possessed, have its soul displaced, or suffer permanent cultivation-system harm, you may use your Reaction and choose one result:

sections.name: Defer
ordered: Delay the complete consequence until the end of the scene. The target remains alive and functional enough to act, though it may be at 1 Hit Point and visibly unstable. If the consequence is not properly repaired, escaped, exorcised, or otherwise changed before the scene ends, it returns in full.
sections.summary: Delay the complete consequence until the end of the scene. The target remains alive and functional enough to act, though it may be at 1 Hit Point and visibly unstable. If the consequence is not properly repaired, escaped, exorcised, or otherwise changed before the scene ends, it returns in full.

sections.name: Take the Burden
sections.summary: If the consequence is ordinary or lower Source CL, transfer it to yourself as a White Mercy Scar. The target avoids it. A White Mercy Scar counts as two Mercy Scars, cannot rupture for a save bonus, and cannot be removed by an ordinary Full Cultivation Session. It requires the White-Mercy Restoration procedure in the Procedure Addendum or treatment by an explicit equal-or-higher-authority restoration Source Rule.

items: AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
Hit Points: 10 × Proficiency Bonus
Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL
Immunities: Poison, Psychic, Necrotic, Radiant, and ordinary bodily conditions

sections.name: House the Burden
rules: The Anchor persists after the aura ends until the burden is reconstructed, transferred, purified, or released. If destroyed without completing a transfer, purification, or reconstruction, resolve Escaped Burden Priority from the Procedure Addendum using the housed consequence as the burden.
sections.summary: Place the consequence into a specially prepared White Room Anchor occupying one space in the aura. The Anchor has:

sections.name: Authority Limits
ordered: Secret-Law erasure, divine judgment, artifact execution, tribulation injury, complete soul destruction, voluntary refusal to return, and equal- or higher-Source-CL permanent harm can resist Impossible Triage. On a successful Cultivation Check, you may still stabilize the victim and prevent escalation until a proper restoration procedure is attempted.
White Room Mercy is powerful because it creates time and custody. It does not make catastrophic harm cease to exist without someone or something carrying it.

sections.name: Soul Splitting Expression — Burden-Bearing Double
sections.summary: While Soul Splitting is active, use Burden-Bearing Double as your Subpath Expression. Move your Soul Fragment up to 20 feet, then transfer one Mercy Scar you carry to the fragment or return one Scar it carries to you. The Scar still counts against your maximum. While carried by the fragment, it cannot be ruptured for a saving-throw bonus, but Give the Pain a Name and White Room Mercy may treat the fragment as its bearer and origin. If the fragment is destroyed or Soul Splitting ends, the Scar immediately returns to you; if that exceeds your maximum, resolve overflow normally.

sections.name: Kami Descent
rules: Concentration: No
Choose one Descent Aspect appropriate to your shrine or covenant. You gain the universal benefits and the chosen Aspect.
sections.summary: A willing greater kami or perfected shrine office descends into your cultivated spirit. This is negotiated hosting, not uncontrolled possession.

sections.name: Universal Benefits
rules: - Choose one Descent Movement when the covenant is recorded: Heavenly Flight (Fly 60 feet and hover), Sacred Ascent (Climb 60 feet, including ceilings), River Passage (Swim 60 feet and breathe air and water), or Processional Step (walking Speed becomes 60 feet and you ignore nonmagical difficult terrain and liquid surfaces). Kami Descent grants the recorded movement.
- Advantage on saving throws against possession, curses, Frightened, Charmed, and spiritual contamination.
- Ordinary and lower-Source-CL spirits recognize the manifest kami authority and cannot disguise their broad Nature from your Spiritual Sense.
- Your Brief Purification and Minor Kami Favors can originate from you, your Soul Fragment, your Shrine Anchor, or your Manifest Messenger, but each activation still uses only one origin.

sections.name: Descent of Purity
rules: Once during the Descent, use Kami Purification as an Action without additional Resonance or Offering cost. Choose up to your Proficiency Bonus willing creatures within 60 feet. Each chosen creature selects one benefit: end one ordinary Charmed or Frightened condition; repeat one saving throw against possession, curse, dream intrusion, memory alteration, Spiritual Affliction, or Heart Demon influence with Advantage; return its displaced soul to its body if both are within 60 feet and no equal-or-higher-authority seal prevents return; or suppress one equal-or-higher-Source-CL Spiritual Affliction until the end of the scene if you succeed on a Cultivation Check against its save DC. Kami Purification grants no hostile damage, soul destruction, planar expulsion, or Anchor damage.
sections.summary: Once per turn when you spend Resonance on a Miko or Spirit Awakening feature, one willing creature affected by that feature regains Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier or repeats one save against possession, curse, poison, disease, Frightened, or spiritual contamination.

sections.name: Descent of Protection
rules: Once during the Descent, create Sacred Ground without an Offering or Resonance cost. It lasts only until the Descent ends and uses no destructible Anchor; it is centered on you and moves with you.
sections.summary: You and allies within 20 feet gain Resistance to Psychic and Necrotic damage. Once per round when an ally in that aura takes damage, use your Reaction and spend 1 Resonance to reduce the damage by 2d10 + Wisdom modifier.

sections.name: Descent of Revelation
rules: Once during the Descent, ask the descending kami three questions concerning the current site, spiritual conflict, local history, or an entity the kami can perceive. The kami answers truthfully according to its knowledge and Nature.
sections.summary: Your Spiritual Sense becomes 120 feet and can perceive through ordinary walls up to 5 feet thick for the limited purpose of detecting spirits, souls, possession, curses, dream intrusion, spiritual Assets, and sacred or profane Anchors. Total cover still prevents ordinary targeting.

sections.name: Descent of Renewal
rules: Once during the Descent, touch one creature and restore 8d8 + Wisdom modifier Hit Points, end one ordinary poison or disease, and suppress one curse, possession, Heart Demon, or spiritual contamination for the scene. Equal or higher authority requires a Cultivation Check.
sections.summary: At the start of each of your turns, one willing creature you can perceive within 30 feet regains Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier if it has at least 1 Hit Point.

sections.name: Reciprocity and Taboo
rules: If you knowingly violate the recorded Taboo during the Descent, apply the recorded Taboo Consequence immediately: one of the four consequences below must have been selected when the Shrine Covenant was created.
- Gain 1 level of Exhaustion.
- Your Soul Anchor becomes Strained until you complete the recorded Restitution.
- Lose access to one recorded Minor Kami Favor until you complete the recorded Restitution.
- Your Shrine Anchor and Manifest Messenger become unavailable until you complete the recorded Restitution.
The covenant also records one Restitution from the Procedure Addendum. The consequence cannot be changed after the breach and the GM or AI does not invent a harsher replacement during resolution.
A kami cannot use Descent to seize control of the character without a separate hostile possession procedure and saving throw. You remain the acting character.
sections.summary: When Kami Descent ends, the kami withdraws. If you upheld its Nature and Taboo, no automatic Exhaustion is gained.

sections.name: Domain Integration
sections.summary: If Domain Manifestation is active when you use Kami Descent, your Domain becomes recognized sacred territory for the duration. Sacred Ground effects you create inside it use the Domain’s boundary if smaller, and willing spirits inside can communicate through spiritual impression even without a shared language.

sections.name: Kami’s Messenger
ordered: Your messengers can cross the border between ordinary distance and recognized spiritual relationship.
sections.summary: Your messengers can cross the border between ordinary distance and recognized spiritual relationship.

sections.name: Omen Message
ordered: Send a message of up to 25 words to one creature you have met, one recognized shrine, one willing ancestor, one bonded spirit, or one community that knows your shrine name. The target must be on the same plane.

The message arrives within 1 hour through one chosen omen form: dream, foxfire, reflected text, moving paper charm, bird call, shrine sign, sudden scent, or writing produced by an unattended brush. The form is cosmetic and grants no concealment, control, damage, item activation, or additional information. The recipient knows the message is spiritually sent and can send a response of up to 25 words if willing.
Omen Message cannot cross a sealed planar boundary, reach a creature whose soul is completely hidden by equal or higher Source CL without a Cultivation Check, or force a target to read or answer.

sections.summary: When the form ends, choose one cost:

sections.name: Wingless Ascent
ordered: Unfold incomplete spiritual wings. At the start of each of your turns, choose one mode.
sections.summary: Unfold incomplete spiritual wings. At the start of each of your turns, choose one mode.

sections.name: Ascending Beat
ordered: Gain a fly Speed equal to your walking Speed until the end of the turn. If you end the turn without another way to remain aloft, descend safely up to 60 feet.
sections.summary: Gain a fly Speed equal to your walking Speed until the end of the turn. If you end the turn without another way to remain aloft, descend safely up to 60 feet.

sections.name: Folding Glide
sections.summary: Until the start of your next turn, you can move across liquids, fragile surfaces, open air gaps of up to 20 feet, and vertical surfaces without falling during the movement. You must end on a surface or descend safely.

sections.name: Shielding Pinions
ordered: Choose yourself or one ally within 10 feet. Until the start of your next turn, reduce the first instance of Psychic, Radiant, or Necrotic damage to that creature by Wisdom modifier + Proficiency Bonus.
You may use one mode each turn without additional Resonance. After using Ascending Beat on three turns during the same scene, each later Ascending Beat costs 1 Resonance.

sections.summary: Choose yourself or one ally within 10 feet. Until the start of your next turn, reduce the first instance of Psychic, Radiant, or Necrotic damage to that creature by Wisdom modifier + Proficiency Bonus.

sections.name: Torn Wings
sections.summary: If an equal- or higher-Source-CL effect suppresses the wings while you are airborne, you descend safely 30 feet before falling normally. A feature that explicitly destroys spiritual anatomy can instead inflict a Hidden Injury or Molt Debt according to its printed procedure.

sections.name: Lord of the Dead
rules: Concentration: No
Create a Warden-Wraith, a Large Spirit Cultivation Asset in an unoccupied space within 30 feet.
sections.summary: You establish temporary jurisdiction over the dead in the scene and manifest a warden-wraith built from your cultivated office.

sections.name: Warden-Wraith Profile
rules: - Hit Points: 12 × Proficiency Bonus
- Speed: Fly 50 feet; hover
- Saving Throws: Uses your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throw bonuses
- Resistances: Psychic, Necrotic, Radiant
- Immunities: Poison, Disease, Poisoned, Prone, Grappled, Restrained, and ordinary bodily effects
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL
- Action economy: No independent turn. At the end of each of your turns, it moves up to its Speed. As a Bonus Action, direct one Wraith Expression.
sections.summary: - AC: Your Cultivation Save DC

sections.name: Wraith Expressions
rules: - Chain the Departing: One spirit, incorporeal undead, projected soul, or creature attempting teleportation, reincarnation, soul escape, or possession within 30 feet makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the attempted movement or transition fails and the creature is Restrained by spiritual chains until the end of its next turn. On success, its Speed is halved or it suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect.

- Open the Proper Gate: Release one willing spirit, end one ordinary lower-Source-CL coercive binding, or permit one soul under Death Custody to depart through the correct afterlife, reincarnation, ancestor court, or Soul Anchor route. Equal or higher custody requires a Cultivation Check.

- Procession of Witnesses: Up to Proficiency Bonus corpses, grave residues, or willing local dead within 60 feet produce brief testimony, reveal their direction of death, or indicate the presence of a murderer, possessor, necromantic Anchor, or concealed spirit they genuinely perceived.

- Burial Silence: Create a 20-foot-radius zone centered on the wraith until the start of your next turn. Hostile spirits and undead in the zone cannot regain Hit Points, restore Cultivation Points, become invisible, or create new possessed hosts.
sections.summary: - Warden’s Scythe: Make a Cultivation Attack against one creature within 10 feet. On a hit, deal 4d10 + Wisdom modifier Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage. A spirit or undead hit cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn.

items: Ordinary lower-Source-CL undead and unbound specters within 60 feet cannot attack you unless they succeed on a Charisma saving throw at the start of their turn.
You know when a creature dies within 60 feet and whether its soul departs, remains, is seized, reincarnates, or becomes concealed.
You may maintain a number of Soul Fragments equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus for the activation’s duration.
Coerced fragments cannot be hidden from you by ordinary means.

sections.name: Complete Soul Boundary
rules: The target makes a Charisma saving throw.

- Failed Save: Its complete soul or governing death-fragment is sealed inside the Warden-Wraith until the feature ends. While sealed, it cannot reform, possess, reincarnate, return to a phylactery-like Anchor, or activate a death-triggered escape. Before the feature ends, you must release it, transfer it to a legal prison or afterlife route, or create a specific long-term Anchor under a separate Source Rule.
- Successful Save: Its attempted escape is delayed until the end of its next turn and it suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect.
Final Custody is not permanent soul destruction. Equal- or higher-Source-CL targets use their printed escape procedures and may force a Cultivation Check contest.
sections.summary: Once during the activation, when a hostile spirit at least 5 Source CL lower than you, undead ruler, or soul predator is reduced to 0 Hit Points within 60 feet, you may attempt Final Custody.

sections.name: Wraith Destruction
sections.summary: If the Warden-Wraith is destroyed, you take 6d10 Psychic damage that ignores Resistance, every Soul Fragment beyond your normal maximum is released, and any complete soul held by Final Custody escapes to the nearest legal route. You cannot use Lord of the Dead again until you complete a Full Cultivation Session.

sections.name: Forbidden Consequences
ordered: Using Lord of the Dead to release, protect, or lawfully imprison spirits creates no Grave Debt. Each of the following creates 2 Grave Debt when completed: consume an unwilling Complete Soul; create permanent slavery of a Complete Soul; obstruct a recorded rightful afterlife route for personal gain; or weaponize a protected ancestor against its recorded will. One act can create Grave Debt only once under this list, even if several descriptions apply. Higher spiritual authorities may perceive or contest the act according to their Source Rules.
sections.summary: Using Lord of the Dead to release, protect, or lawfully imprison spirits creates no Grave Debt. Create the specter in an unoccupied space within 30 feet
lossy: allowlist: header fact inside the body
sections.name: Raise Specter
rules: Choose Warden Specter or Predatory Specter when created.
sections.summary: You construct a temporary manifestation from corpse memory or a Soul Fragment. It is a Spirit Cultivation Asset, not the creature restored and not a full companion.

sections.name: Specter Profile
rules: - AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 6 × Proficiency Bonus
- Speed: Fly 40 feet; hover
- Saving Throws: Uses your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throw bonuses
- Resistances: Psychic and Necrotic
- Immunities: Poison, Disease, Poisoned, Prone, Grappled, Restrained, and ordinary bodily effects
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL
- Action economy: No independent turn. At the end of each of your turns, it moves up to its Speed. As a Bonus Action, direct one Specter Expression.
sections.summary: - Size: Medium

sections.name: Warden Specter Expressions
rules: - Seize Intruder: One spirit, incorporeal undead, possessed creature, or Resonance Marked creature within 10 feet makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, its Speed becomes 0 and it cannot possess another creature until the start of your next turn.
- Testify: The specter reproduces one memory, route, image, or statement contained in the spent fragment. Protected information remains limited to what the fragment held.
sections.summary: - Guard the Threshold: One ally within 10 feet of the specter gains Half Cover and Advantage on its next saving throw against possession or soul displacement before the start of your next turn.

sections.name: Predatory Specter Expressions
rules: - Harrier of the Living: One creature within 10 feet cannot take Reactions and has Disadvantage on the next death saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn. This cannot target an ally unless the ally willingly accepts the risk.

- Drink Fear: One Frightened or Resonance Marked creature within 10 feet makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it takes 2d8 Psychic damage and you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
sections.summary: - Spectral Strike: Make a Cultivation Attack against a creature within 5 feet. On a hit, deal 2d10 + Wisdom modifier Necrotic or Psychic damage.

sections.name: Destruction
rules: The source’s complete soul is not harmed merely because the specter is destroyed. A manifestation cannot use the source creature’s attacks, spell list, Legendary actions, equipment, full statistics, or identity-defining features.
sections.summary: If the specter is reduced to 0 Hit Points, it disperses. If created from a Coerced fragment, you take Psychic damage equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus as the custody breaks.

sections.name: Soul Splitting Expression — Twin Custody
sections.summary: While Soul Splitting is active, the Soul Fragment may serve as the origin of a Specter Expression. The specter still receives only one expression per Bonus Action and gains no independent action.

sections.name: Soul Drain and Death Custody
outcomes: The target takes 6d8 + Wisdom modifier Necrotic or Psychic damage, your choice. Until the end of its next turn, it cannot regain Hit Points or restore Cultivation Points. If it is a spirit or undead, it also cannot become incorporeal, possess another creature, or return to a prepared vessel during that time.
It takes half damage and cannot become spiritually concealed until the start of your next turn.
rules: Choose one creature. It makes a Constitution saving throw. A spirit, incorporeal undead, possessed creature, or creature bearing your Resonance Mark may use Charisma instead if that bonus is higher.
sections.summary: You can draw spiritual vitality from a living soul or collapse the animating residue of an undead creature.

items: Create one Soul Fragment without using your Reaction.
Stabilize the creature and place its departing residue under Death Custody until the end of the scene.
Release it to die or depart normally.
Permit legal healing.
Transfer custody to a willing healer, funerary authority, or prepared vessel.
Attempt a lawful interrogation through Speak with the Dead if death occurs.
Convert the residue into a Coerced Soul Fragment, gaining 1 Grave Debt unless necessary to prevent a greater spiritual catastrophe.
groups.lead: A creature under Death Custody does not die, depart, reincarnate, become undead, or have its soul seized by an ordinary lower-Source-CL effect while custody remains. It is stable at 0 Hit Points. You must choose one outcome before the scene ends:

sections.name: Capture at the Brink
rules: Equal- or higher-authority death claims, divine custody, Secret Laws, Samsara, or artifacts can contest Death Custody with Source CL and their printed procedures.
sections.summary: If Soul Drain reduces a qualifying hostile creature to 0 Hit Points, choose one:

sections.name: Warden’s Reversal
ordered: As a Reaction when an ally within 30 feet would have its soul displaced, consumed, trapped, or converted into an undead manifestation, spend one Soul Fragment. The ally gains Advantage on the relevant save. If no save exists, it makes a Charisma saving throw against the effect’s save DC. On success, delay the effect until the end of the ally’s next turn, allowing escape, healing, Exorcism, or another intervention.

facts: A meaningful creature dies within 30 feet, an undead or spirit is destroyed within 30 feet, or a willing spirit within 30 feet deliberately gives you a fragment
lossy: allowlist: header fact inside the body
sections.name: Soul Harvest
rules: Create one Soul Fragment from the triggering source, subject to your maximum.
The fragment is Consensual if freely given, Unclaimed if the complete soul has already departed and no lawful custody contests it, or Coerced if the source resists or you obstruct departure.
sections.summary: You can catch a fragment at the moment a meaningful soul sheds residue.

sections.name: Unwilling Source
rules: - Failed Save: You capture one fragment, not the complete soul. If the source is meaningful and nonhostile or helpless, gain 1 Grave Debt.
- Successful Save: You gain no fragment, but learn whether the soul is departing, claimed, reincarnating, concealed, or bound by another effect.
A creature at least 5 Source CL lower than you that dies after being damaged by you cannot prevent collection of ordinary residue, but this still does not grant custody of its complete soul.
sections.summary: If a spirit or soul remains present and unwilling, it makes a Charisma saving throw.

items: Recover Resonance equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded up. You can do this only once per scene.
Gain Advantage on one Soul Gaze, Speak with the Dead, or Cultivation Check involving death, undead, or the fragment’s source.
Cause one specter Asset you control to regain Hit Points equal to 5 × Proficiency Bonus.
Prevent one spirit or soul within 30 feet from becoming spiritually concealed until the start of your next turn; an equal- or higher-Source-CL creature may resist with a Charisma saving throw.

sections.name: Fragment Uses
rules: Spending a fragment releases or consumes the residue according to the declared use. Consuming a Coerced fragment for personal recovery without necessity gains 1 Grave Debt.
sections.summary: As a Bonus Action, spend one Soul Fragment for one benefit:

sections.name: Speak with the Dead
rules: Ritual: 1 minute

Choose a corpse with an intact head, chest, or other body part that retains a memory-bearing organ or a funerary object linked to the deceased, funerary object, grave marker, severed body part containing meaningful residue, or location where a creature died within the last year.

Ask up to 1 + half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down, questions. The response comes through voice, gesture, corpse movement, remembered sensation, nearby shadows, written condensation, or another appropriate medium.
sections.summary: You can awaken corpse memory or lingering residue without importing a spell’s fixed assumptions.

sections.name: What the Dead Know
ordered: The residue can answer only from information the creature knew, perceived, believed, or experienced before death. It may be confused, biased, incomplete, or emotionally distorted. It does not know what occurred after death unless the lingering spirit remained present.
sections.summary: The residue can answer only from information the creature knew, perceived, believed, or experienced before death. It may be confused, biased, incomplete, or emotionally distorted. It does not know what occurred after death unless the lingering spirit remained present.

items: The creature was hostile to you.
Its funeral rites prohibit questioning.
Its soul or memory is sealed.
Another authority claims custody.
It died under Secret, divine, artifact, or higher-Source-CL concealment.

sections.name: Resistance and Protection
rules: Make a Cultivation Check against the protecting effect or the creature’s Charisma save bonus converted into a DC of 8 + Proficiency Bonus + Charisma modifier. On failure, you learn whether the resistance is unwillingness, ignorance, damage, concealment, or higher custody.
sections.summary: The corpse or residue can resist if:

sections.name: Repeat Questioning
sections.summary: Once you use Speak with the Dead on a given residue, you cannot question the same residue again until you learn materially new information, repair it, obtain consent, or a new scene begins. Repetition cannot force a different answer through dice fishing.

sections.name: Funerary Reading
ordered: Gain proficiency in Medicine or Religion. If already proficient in both, gain proficiency in Investigation or Insight instead.
sections.summary: Gain proficiency in Medicine or Religion. If already proficient in both, gain proficiency in Investigation or Insight instead.

sections.name: Dance of Borrowed Limbs
outcomes: Consume one String. At the start of each of the target’s turns, choose one command:
rules: The target makes a Wisdom saving throw.
- lose 10 feet of Speed;
- drop one held object that is not soul-bound or inseparably attached;
- move up to 10 feet along a legal path;
- fall Prone;
- make one weapon attack at Disadvantage against a legal target you choose within reach;
- spend its Reaction making a harmless involuntary gesture, step, or guard motion;
- speak or remain silent for one brief phrase, provided this does not compel protected information or a lie the creature cannot formulate.
The target repeats the save at the end of each turn, ending the feature on a success. Each successful save removes one remaining Choreography String.
Successful Initial Save: The feature does not take hold. The target suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect, and you do not consume a String.

A substantially lower-Source-CL ordinary creature can be forced to repeat harmless choreography without further saves after three failed saves during the same activation, but hostile attacks, self-endangerment, and major actions always preserve the saving throw procedure.

sections.name: Marionette Defense
ordered: Choose one String-bearing creature that is within the triggering attack’s reach, line, area, or legal target geometry. It makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Consume one String. You move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. If the chosen creature remains a legal target for the triggering attack after that movement, the attack targets it instead and retains the original attack roll.
You gain +2 AC against the triggering attack and may move 5 feet after it resolves.

Marionette Defense cannot redirect an effect to an illegal target, force an attacker to spend another resource, change a self-only effect, or redirect a precise effect whose Source Rule states it cannot change targets.
outcomes: Consume one String. You move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. If the chosen creature remains a legal target for the triggering attack after that movement, the attack targets it instead and retains the original attack roll.

ordered: A willing ally bearing one of your Strings may choose to fail the save. If it does, it gains Resistance to the triggering attack’s damage and the String is consumed after damage resolves. This permits deliberate bodyguard choreography without creating infinite redirection loops.
sections.summary: A willing ally bearing one of your Strings may choose to fail the save. If it does, it gains Resistance to the triggering attack’s damage and the String is consumed after damage resolves. This permits deliberate bodyguard choreography without creating infinite redirection loops.

outcomes: Consume one String and choose two effects until the start of your next turn:
Do not consume the String. Choose one effect from the list.
rules: - Speed reduced by 10 feet;
- cannot take Reactions;
- Disadvantage on the next weapon attack;
- cannot benefit from Advantage created by an ally’s Help;
- must spend 5 additional feet of movement to stand from Prone or change elevation;
- cannot take the same movement mode twice during the turn, such as teleporting twice or flying after walking.
sections.summary: The target makes a Wisdom saving throw.

sections.name: Catch the Beat
sections.summary: If the target fails while bearing three Strings, you may instead consume all three to make its Speed 0 until the start of your next turn. It can still teleport or be moved by another source unless that source also fails a Source CL contest against you.

items: When a hostile creature starts its turn in the field, you may place one Choreography String on it if it is Resonance Marked by you, failed a Spirit Awakening save since the end of its last turn, or moved unwillingly during the round.
A creature can receive no more than one String from the field per round.
Once per round when a creature in the field moves, attacks, stands, falls, teleports, or changes elevation, you may move another String-bearing creature 5 feet along a legal path.
You and willing allies in the field ignore the first 10 feet of difficult terrain each turn and can stand from Prone using 5 feet of movement.
Hostile String-bearing creatures cannot take Opportunity Attacks against you.

sections.name: Theater of Strings
rules: Create a 30-foot-radius Theater of Strings field centered on you. It moves with you and has your Source CL.
sections.summary: You transform the battlefield into a stage whose rhythm is spiritually legible to you.

sections.name: Final Choreography
outcomes: Consume all three Strings. Choose one sequence:
It removes one String and suffers two different Spiritual Pressure effects until the start of its next turn.
rules: - Empty Turn: It loses its Action on its next turn performing harmless involuntary movement.
- Crossed Blades: It uses its Reaction immediately to make one weapon attack at Disadvantage against a legal target you choose.
- Broken Formation: Move it up to half its Speed along a legal route, and it cannot take Reactions until the end of its next turn.
- Kneeling Beat: It falls Prone, its Speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn, and it suffers one Spiritual Pressure effect.

Equal- and higher-Source-CL targets can contest forced movement or target redirection through a Cultivation Check after the save. Theater of Strings controls motion; it does not erase agency, create an additional sustained puppet-control system, or create a permanent puppet.
sections.summary: Once during the activation, choose one creature in the field bearing three Strings. It makes a Wisdom saving throw.

items: Echo the Step: Move one creature bearing your Choreography String within 30 feet of the fragment by 5 feet along a legal path. A creature can be moved by this fragment option only once per round.

sections.name: Soul Splitting Option — Second Dancer
rules: The fragment does not place Strings, consume Strings, or use Final Choreography.
sections.summary: Your Soul Fragment gains the following Subpath Fragment option:

sections.name: Threaded Step
rules: - This is forced movement and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- It cannot move the creature into an obviously lethal hazard unless another Source Rule permits it.
- A creature with equal or higher Source CL can make a Strength or Wisdom saving throw to ignore the movement while still receiving the String.
sections.summary: When you hit a creature with Mind Spike or it fails a saving throw against one of your Spirit Awakening features, you may place one Choreography String and move it 5 feet in a direction of your choice if it is Large or smaller and physically able to move.

sections.name: Dancer’s Counterstep
sections.summary: Once per round when a creature bearing one of your Strings moves willingly within 30 feet of you, you may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. This does not use your Reaction, but you cannot use it while Incapacitated or Restrained.

sections.name: Break Their Will
sections.summary: When your authority gains momentum, resistance becomes spiritually expensive.

facts: A meaningful hostile creature within 60 feet is reduced to 0 Hit Points, surrenders, becomes Incapacitated through one of your Spirit Awakening effects, or fails a saving throw against Commanding Voice.
sections.name: Submission Shock
ordered: Choose another hostile creature within 30 feet of the triggering creature that can perceive you, the creature, or the spiritual collapse. It makes a Wisdom saving throw.

It is Dazed by Submission until the end of its next turn. While Dazed this way, it cannot take Reactions, can take either an Action or a Bonus Action on its turn but not both, and its Speed is halved.
It suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect.
A creature can be targeted by Submission Shock only once per round.
outcomes: It is Dazed by Submission until the end of its next turn. While Dazed this way, it cannot take Reactions, can take either an Action or a Bonus Action on its turn but not both, and its Speed is halved.
It suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect.
rules: A creature can be targeted by Submission Shock only once per round.
sections.summary: Choose another hostile creature within 30 feet of the triggering creature that can perceive you, the creature, or the spiritual collapse. It makes a Wisdom saving throw.

sections.name: Command the Marked
sections.summary: When you use Commanding Voice against a creature Resonance Marked by you, you may spend 1 Mandate instead of 1 Resonance. The creature still receives its saving throw.

sections.name: Commanding Voice
outcomes: The target follows the command on its next turn to the best of its ability. Choose or phrase a command equivalent to one of these:
The target also becomes Resonance Marked by you and you gain 1 Mandate if it is meaningful and hostile.
Choose one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect.
rules: - Approach: Move toward a legal space you indicate by the safest reasonably direct route.
- Drop: Drop one held object that is not fused to the body or protected by a stronger Source Rule.
- Flee: Spend its movement moving away from you by a reasonably safe route.
- Halt: Its Speed becomes 0 and it takes no voluntary movement.
- Kneel: Fall Prone and do not stand until the end of the turn.
- Silence: Do not speak or use an audible technique until the end of the turn.
- Yield: Take the Dodge action and do not make hostile attacks until the end of the turn.

The creature may still take actions not contradicted by the command. The command cannot force direct self-harm, compel use of a limited Secret or artifact resource, reveal information the target does not know, violate an absolute Source Rule, or require an impossible action.
sections.summary: Speak one brief command to one creature that can hear you or spiritually perceive your authority. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw.

sections.name: Voice of Office
ordered: You may use Wisdom instead of Charisma for Persuasion or Intimidation checks made to issue formal commands, adjudicate a dispute, demand surrender, or speak from a recognized office. This does not force compliance and applies only when the authority claim is intelligible in the scene.

facts: Until the start of your next turn

items: No Advance: The target cannot willingly move closer to a point or creature you designate.
No Escape: The target cannot willingly move farther from a point or creature you designate.
No Reaction: The target cannot take Reactions.
No Violence: The target cannot make attacks or activate a technique whose immediate purpose is to deal damage.
No Speech: The target cannot speak, issue audible commands, or activate an expressly Audible technique.
No Passage: The target cannot teleport or cross a threshold you designate within range.

sections.name: Edict of Heaven
outcomes: The target must obey the edict for the duration. If it attempts a prohibited act, the act is wasted before costs are paid unless a stronger Source Rule says costs are committed on declaration.
The target resists the edict but suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect.
rules: Declare one clear edict and choose any number of creatures within range that can hear you or spiritually perceive you. Each target makes a Charisma saving throw.

An edict cannot prohibit all actions, erase a Path, prevent passive defenses, force self-harm, suppress an unknown category, or forbid an entire Sphere or cultivation system without higher authority. Equal- or higher-Source-CL targets may use a Cultivation Check in place of the Charisma save if they are contesting the edict with a coherent Domain, throne, true name, oath, or comparable authority.
sections.summary: You impose one local law upon the conduct of lesser wills.

sections.name: Mandate of Clarity
sections.summary: When a creature fails against Edict of Heaven, you know whether it understood the edict and whether a stronger Source Rule prevented full obedience. You do not learn the hidden Source Rule’s exact text.

sections.name: Hegemon’s Domain
rules: When you activate Domain Manifestation, you may spend 4 additional Resonance to transform it into Hegemon’s Domain for the scene. This is part of the same activation and does not require Concentration.
While active:
sections.summary: Your Domain becomes a court in which your authority is locally real.

sections.name: Court of Submission
rules: - Failed Save: Its Speed is halved, it cannot take Reactions, and the first time during the turn it attempts to act directly against you, resolve the Court Tax before the action's effects. If the action or technique has a printed expendable cost, increase one such cost by 1 unit of the same resource; the acting creature chooses among multiple eligible printed resources. If it cannot or will not pay, or if the action has no printed expendable cost, it instead takes Psychic damage equal to 2d10 + Wisdom modifier before resolving the action. The damage does not cancel the action unless it incapacitates the creature or another rule does so.
- Successful Save: Choose either Speed reduced by 10 feet or no Reactions until the start of its next turn.
A creature makes this save only once per turn, regardless of how many Assets express your authority.
sections.summary: At the start of each hostile creature’s turn in the Domain, if it can perceive you or one of your spiritual Assets, it makes a Charisma saving throw.

sections.name: Lesser-Realm Command
sections.summary: When a hostile creature with Source CL at least 5 lower than yours fails a saving throw against Commanding Voice or Edict of Heaven inside the Domain, it does not repeat or negate that command through an ordinary legendary resistance, ordinary condition immunity, or mundane morale rule unless that protection expressly defeats spiritual command. It still cannot be ordered to perform impossible or directly self-destructive acts.

sections.name: Equal Thrones
ordered: An equal- or higher-Source-CL creature may contest Court of Submission with a Cultivation Check instead of the Charisma save if it expresses a coherent sovereign identity, Domain, true name, oath, divine mandate, or equivalent authority. On a successful contest, it ignores Court of Submission until the start of its next turn, but does not suppress your Domain for other creatures.

sections.name: Absolute Edict

sections.name: Price of Tyranny
sections.summary: If you knowingly use Hegemon’s Domain to command a willing ally into direct self-destruction, violate a freely accepted Soul Anchor oath, or enslave an unwilling Complete Soul, your Soul Anchor becomes Strained after the scene. Record the harmed creature, violated relationship, command, and result as a Tyranny Breach. The Strain ends only through the Tyranny Restitution procedure in the Procedure Addendum. This consequence does not classify every Sovereign Will cultivator as Forbidden; it classifies the abusive act.

sections.name: Creating the Retainer
rules: An unwilling full soul cannot be made into this Retainer without a separate Forbidden or Secret Source Rule. A fading combat impression can provide mannerisms and one simple combat expression, but is not the dead creature’s continuing consciousness.

sections.summary: Conduct a 1-hour rite and spend 6 Resonance. You require one of the following:

items: Spectral Strike: Make a melee or ranged Cultivation Attack from the Retainer against one target within 30 feet. On a hit, deal 2d8 + Wisdom modifier Psychic, Necrotic, or Radiant damage, chosen when the Retainer is created.
Interpose: One ally within 5 feet of the Retainer gains Temporary Hit Points equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus.
Herald: Extend the audible or spiritually perceptible origin of Commanding Voice or Edict of Heaven from the Retainer.
Counsel: Gain Advantage on one Insight, Persuasion, Religion, History, or Intimidation check whose subject falls within the Retainer’s established office or memory.

sections.summary: Refuse the Moment automatically delays an ordinary, Open, Restricted, or equal-Source-CL consequence when all other requirements are met.

sections.name: Soul Splitting — Hold This Breath
rules: This does not use your Reaction, but it creates 1 Time Debt and still counts against the limit of one Deferred Consequence from Well of Hours. If you are already at maximum Time Debt, the Hour Comes Due normally at the start of your next turn.
sections.summary: When an ally within 30 feet of your soul fragment takes damage, the fragment can use its Subpath Fragment action and spend 2 Resonance from you to defer up to 2d8 + Wisdom modifier of that damage until the end of that ally’s turn.

sections.name: Ripple of Before
ordered: Your soul recognizes the pressure of a moment immediately before the body understands it.
sections.summary: Your soul recognizes the pressure of a moment immediately before the body understands it.

facts: You roll Initiative, become Surprised, fail a Wisdom (Perception) or Wisdom (Insight) check, or fail a Cultivation Check to notice an immediate spiritual danger

items: Add your Proficiency Bonus to the Initiative roll, ability check, or Cultivation Check. You decide after rolling but before the final outcome is declared.

If Surprised, you can move up to half your Speed, speak a short warning, draw or stow one item, use Spiritual Sense, or take the Dodge action during your first turn. You remain Surprised and cannot use another Action or Bonus Action during that turn unless another Source Rule removes Surprise.

If the check concerned an ambush, trap, possession, dream intrusion, concealed spirit, imminent attack, or immediate temporal disturbance, learn the direction of the danger even if the added bonus does not produce a success.

sections.name: The Well Has No Bottom
rules: The area becomes a Well of Hours, a spiritual-temporal field and Source Rule.
This record is its Round Image.

At the start of each of your turns, replace the Round Image of each chosen creature currently in the field with its current state. When a creature enters the field after it appears, you may choose it for the field. If chosen and still in the field, it gains a Round Image at the start of your next turn.
sections.summary: You reveal the local truth that every present moment rests above an immeasurable depth of moments that might have been.

items: move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks;
stand from Prone without spending movement;
draw or stow one item and use Spiritual Sense;
gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 2 × your Proficiency Bonus;
suppress one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect on itself until the end of the turn.

sections.name: Return to the Bell
rules: - Place it in its recorded space or the nearest legal space within 15 feet.
- If the recorded Hit Point value is higher, set its Hit Points to that value.
- Remove ordinary conditions gained after the image was recorded.

- Restore no Resonance, Stamina, Qi, Hit Dice, item charges, consumed materials, actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, movement, Concentration, Sphere resources, Insight uses, Domain activations, or other spent resources.

This damage ignores Resistance and Immunity and cannot be redirected, deferred, transferred, or reduced by a Well of Hours feature.

sections.name: Drink the Unlived Hour
rules: You can choose Borrowed Second’s weapon-attack or Mind Spike option only once during the entire activation of The Well Has No Bottom.
sections.summary: Once on each of your turns, you may gain 1 Time Debt to use Borrowed Second without spending Resonance.
